Swordsman.x: Swordsman is the go-to “tank” of the six first jobs. With high HP, access to great defensive gear, and skill options to boost sustain and reduce damage taken, they are adept at getting into bigger fights than they can handle and finding a way to come out on the other side.

The Swordsman’s weakness comes from their damage. Though they can generate decent amounts of sustained DPS from the Bleed status, they have few other ways to output damage, meaning they often find themselves needing to leverage that increased survivability to win encounters in the first place.
Swordsmen have two key Status Effects: Bleed and Vulnerable.

The Bleed status effect does constant damage based on the user’s Strength, scaling up with Base Level. With few other damage options, and all of those options being very SP intensive, this becomes the primary source of damage for Swordsmen before they job change to Knight or Crusader.

The Vulnerable status is similar to the Provoke status of Vanilla RO, with one major change: it does not increase the ATK of the target. This allows the user to strip up to 40% of the target’s defenses (both hard and soft) at will, increasing their own damage and that of any party members...though its primary purpose is to combo into other skills belonging to the Knight and Crusader classes.
Swordsmen cap at job level 50, giving them 50 skill points to spend on the following skills:
Sword Mastery: Increases the damage of One-Handed Swords.
Slash: Deals two quick hits, with a chance to inflict the Bleed status on enemies.
Lash Out: Strike all enemies around the user. For each enemy in range, including those the attack misses, gain a small amount of HP.
Improved Constitution: Increases the effects of healing items that restore HP, and restore a small amount of HP every 10 seconds the user isn’t moving.
Provoke: Attempts to grab the attention of a distant mob and inflict the Vulnerable status on them.
Endure: For a few seconds, reduce all damage taken from all sources by 30%. The user will not flinch while taking damage when this skill is active.

Knight.x: Knight is the primary advancement option for the Swordsman class. Like Swordsmen before them, Knights rely on naturally high HP, high defensive stats from their available equipment, and increased potion efficiency to sustain themselves in encounters.

In terms of combat style, they are one of the simplest jobs to play. Whether built to use swords or spears, their skills take advantage of Bleeding and Vulnerable statuses on enemies to amplify their damage, with only a couple skills that work to bolster their defenses.

The Knight skill tree is divided into two quite disparate paths: one geared toward the use of Swords and Two-Handed Swords, the other toward Spears and Two-Handed Spears. Though offensively speaking both one- and two- handed variants of their weapons are permitted, Knights will find themselves gravitating more toward the higher damage option of two-handed weapons, as their few defensive options require a two-handed weapon to be utilized. That said, new Knights will have to be careful — swapping to a new weapon type means losing the advantages of their first job masteries, thus making early levels a bit more challenging if they make the switch too soon.
Knights gain access to the following skills:
Two-Handed Sword Mastery: Passive. Mastery for Two-handed swords. Damage and Accuracy with Two-Handed Swords. Two-Handed Swords typically gain bonus Crit Rate as a mastery bonus.

Rend: Sword Skill. Simple follow-up skill to Slash. Deals additional damage to enemies that are Bleeding or Vulnerable. Inflicts Bleeding if the enemy is already Vulnerable, or Vulnerable if the enemy is already Bleeding.
Devastating Blow: Sword Finisher skill. Strikes all enemies in a small area, dealing additional hits to Bleeding targets and refreshing the duration of their Bleeding effects.
Quicken: Sword skill. Maximizes the user’s Attack Speed and increases their Hit and Crit Rate for five seconds, but blocks the usage of skills while active.
Spear Mastery: Passive. Mastery for spears. Increases damage and accuracy with spears, both one- and two-handed. Spears typically gain bonus Vulnerable Potency as a mastery bonus.
Pierce: Spear attack with bonus Defense Pierce. Enemies suffering from Bleeding or Vulnerable statuses take extra hits.

Spear Stab: Targets a distant enemy (4 cells range), then hits all enemies between them and the caster (including the target). Has a chance to inflict the Vulnerable status, and deals additional damage to targets that are already Vulnerable.
Brandish Spear: Performs a large AoE in front of the user, dealing heavy damage. Vulnerable targets have their Vulnerable duration refreshed and take additional damage.
Armor Mastery: Passive. Improves the physical defenses of the user when not wearing a shield.
Deflect: The user takes a defensive stance, blocking all physical attacks for a short duration. Requires a Two-Handed Sword or Two-Handed Spear.

Lord Knight.x: Lord Knight is the primary advancement option for Knights. It continues the original path of the knight—tight, rotation based skill patterns—and expands it, adding new skills that can serve as replacements for old skills to enhance the Knight level rotations, or that can slot in happily beside them adding a second full rotation to the menu, filling much of the downtime Knights experienced in their combat with new skills.

On top of the usual split between Sword and Spear skills, Lord Knights gain another branching path to choose in two new Stances. The first, Vanguard Stance, is tuned towards Lord Knights who wish to dive deep into enemy lines and tear them apart personally, enhancing the user’s offensive capabilities. Alternatively, they have the option of picking Warden Stance, a defensive stance that increases their resistance to all damage and grants control effects to most of their skills.

Sword skills reinvest heavily into the Bleeding status, though they are less interested in dealing damage through the Bleeding status itself. Instead, they gain a number of skills that have enhanced damage and effects based on the user’s bonuses to Bleeding damage, and based on whether the target is Bleeding or not. Their ultimate skill, Execute, does a massive burst of damage based on the strength of the Bleeding Status that the target is suffering from.

Spear skills put Bleeding on the back burner and focus on Vulnerable, capitalizing on its ability to strip enemies of almost all defenses right out of the box by gaining further bonuses based on the user’s bonuses to Vulnerable Potency. They culminate in the ultimate skill Gatling Pierce, which does tremendous damage across a large area to enemies suffering from Vulnerable.

Vanguard Stance: The user shifts into an offensive stance, optimizing their ability to deal damage. Increases the user’s Hit Rate and adds Agility scaling to all Lord Knight skills. Requires a Two-Handed Weapon.
Warden Stance: The user shifts into a defensive stance, maximizing their survivability. Increases the user’s resistance to all damage and adds Vitality scaling to all Lord Knight skills.

Sonic Wave: Flexible Skill. The user swings their weapon violently, creating a shock wave that strikes a distant enemy. Inflicts Bleeding if the user has a Two-Handed Sword equipped, or Vulnerable if the user has a Two-Handed Spear equipped. Grants the user increased Movement Speed during Vanguard Stance, or inflicts Slow during Warden Stance.

Shattering Strike: Flexible Skill. The user dashes toward a distant enemy, delivering a precision blow with remarkable speed. If the user is wielding a Two-Handed Sword, the damage is treated as Bleeding damage. If the user is wielding a Two-Handed Spear, the damage is increased by Vulnerable Potency. During Vanguard Stance, the skill also inflicts Bleeding. During Warden Stance, it also inflicts Vulnerable.

Flourish: Sword Skill. The user swings their weapon in a wide arc, tearing apart all enemies in the area. Any enemies struck receive the Bleeding Status. This skill gains Luck Scaling, plus scaling based on the active Stance. During Vanguard Stance, the damage is treated as Bleeding Damage. During Warden Stance, the Bleeding Status inflicted by this skill has doubled duration.

Storm Slash: Sword Skill. The user delivers a flurry of wild slashes, dealing devastating damage to a single foe. This skill deals additional damage to Bleeding enemies, and scales with Luck and the user’s Stance. Its cooldown is halved during Vanguard Stance, and grants the user the Endure status during Warden Stance.

Execute: Sword Skill. Deals a final, fatal blow to the targeted enemy, consuming their Bleeding to deal a massive burst of damage. If the target is Bleeding, it ends and they take additional damage based on the strength of the Bleeding Status they had. If used during Vanguard Stance, Knight-level Sword skills have their cooldowns refreshed. If used during Warden Stance, it additionally stuns the target.

Phantom Thrust: Spear Skill. Strikes a distant enemy with the user’s spear, throwing them off balance and attempting to leave them Vulnerable. The skill’s damage scales with the user’s Dexterity, as well as the scaling granted by their Stance. Its damage is enhanced by the user’s Vulnerable Potency if used during Vanguard Stance, and pulls the enemy to the user if used during Warden Stance.

Clashing Spiral: Spear Skill. The user drives their spear into the target while spinning it, dealing exceptional damage to their person and their armor. Deals additional damage based on the user’s Vulnerable Potency, and scales with the user’s Dexterity and their Stance scaling.
During Vanguard Stance, its cooldown is halved, and during Warden Stance, it deals additional damage based on the user’s current HP.

Gatling Pierce: Spear Skill. The user delivers a rapid flurry of stabs with their spear, dealing exceptional damage to the target and all enemies in the area around them. Targets suffering from the Vulnerable Status take additional damage. During Vanguard Stance, this skill refreshes the cooldowns of all Knight-level Spear skills. During Warden Stance, all enemies affected are also stunned.

Rune Knight.x: Rune Knight is the alternative advancement option for Knights. While the Lord Knight continues the orthodox style of the Knight, expanding its stable rotations with more skills that function in much the same way, the Rune Knight takes an entirely different direction.

Rather than a skill tree, the Rune Knight’s skills are more accurately described as a “Skill Pool.” With virtually no prerequisites for their skills, they are free to select any skills they wish right from the start. This turns their third job skills into a versatile toolbox that can be selectively applied to enhance the user’s own particular style of play.

The skills available for Rune Knight are evenly distributed between direct attack skills and self buffs. Some of these slot perfectly well into the original rotational gameplay of the Knight, but others demand an entirely new playstyle to appreciate. In particular, all Rune Knight attack skills benefit heavily from Int investment, making stat point distribution a bit more challenging than it was previously for them.

In addition to this toolbox of skills, the Rune Knight has the unique ability to craft Runes. These are single-use items that function in the same manner as Cards, able to be slotted into equipment and used by any class. Furthermore, each Rune comes with a unique bonus that can only be used by Rune Knights.
Each variety of Rune comes in five levels, each progressive level giving a stronger bonus but requiring more difficult materials to create. There are ten varieties of Rune available at present.

Rune Research: Research into the nature and use of Rune Magic. Increases the user’s Int and enhances the effectiveness of all Rune Knight skills. Has no effect on the creation of Rune Stones, or their effectiveness after creation.

Rune Inscription: Study into the creation of Rune Stones, single-use items that can be slotted into equipment in the same manner as cards. Runes have a level from 1 to 5. The maximum level of Rune that can be created is based on the level of Rune Inscription learned.
Created Runes can be used by any class, but gain additional effects based on the Rune Inscription level of the character equipping them.

Winter Razor: Releases a blast of icy wind around the user, slicing apart nearby enemies. Attempts to inflict the Bleeding status on all enemies struck. Damage dealt by this skill is increased by the user’s Int and is treated as Bleeding damage.
Ignition Break: Creates a burst of mystical fire from the user’s weapon, incinerating enemies in the area. This skill deals additional damage based on the user’s Int and is treated as Burning damage.

Burning Breath: Unleashes a burst of flame to envelop the targeted location. Deals Physical Fire Property damage and attempts to inflict the Burning status on all enemies in the area. This skill deals additional damage based on the user’s Int.

Storm Blast: Strikes the targeted enemy, then explodes outward, striking all enemies in an area around them.. If the original target is Bleeding, Burning, or Vulnerable, spreads those statuses to all enemies struck by the blast. Deals additional damage based on the user’s Int.

Crush Strike: Delivers a crushing blow to the target, smashing through their defenses. Inflicts the Vulnerable status. If the target was already Vulnerable, additionally inflicts the Stun Status. This skill deals additional damage based on the user’s Int and Vulnerable Potency.
Bloodthirst: For a short duration, all autoattacks from the user are treated as Bleeding damage and have a chance to autocast the Rend skill.
Refresh: For ten seconds, reduces the Cooldown of the next skill cast by the user.

Burning Rage: For a short duration, all Physical Skills cast by the user are treated as Burning Damage. (This skill does not affect Ignition Break, as it is already Burning Damage). The duration of this skill is increased by the user’s Rune Research level.
Tenacity: Rapidly regenerates the user’s HP over a short duration.

Millennium Shield: Creates a mystical shield around the user that blocks a certain amount of damage. The amount of HP the barrier has is influenced by the skill level and the user’s Rune Research level.

Crusader.x: Crusader is the alternative advancement option for the Swordsman class, marrying the inherent defense and damage mitigation strategies of the Swordsman with the holy magic of the Acolyte.

While there are two general build options, they are not as strictly divided as the Knight’s are. Spear builds branch out of Swordsman's Slash, compounding the Bleed status with an additional Blind status from Brilliant Strike. Holy Cross takes advantage of both, inflicting devastating damage if the enemy is Bleeding and Blinded at the same time. Spear Flurry creates an exceptional damage window for burst, instantly refreshing the Cooldowns of all of the Crusader’s Spear skills.

The Shield Build sacrifices this exceptional burst potential for a balanced approach to damage and survivability. Faith, the stand-in for Shield Mastery, increases the user’s physical and magical defenses. Shield Slam is the core damage skill, supplemented by Shield Boomerang to strike at enemies before they enter melee range. Both skills receive a large damage bonus from the target being Vulnerable, while Boomerang also helps to reapply the status.

The class’s two "ultimate" skills mirror each other in function. Restoration is a ground based spell that heals the user and their allies over time. Grand Cross takes the opposite approach, sacrificing the Crusader's HP to deal massive damage in an area around them, while also applying the Blind and Vulnerable statuses in case any follow-up is necessary. Neither skill requires any investment in Int or Magic Attack for optimal performance, allowing the Crusader to focus on building toward stats that will be more impactful in general use.
Crusaders gain access to the following skills:
Spear Mastery: Passive. Mastery for One-Handed and Two-Handed spears. Increases damage and accuracy with spears. Spears typically gain additional Vulnerable Potency as a mastery bonus.
Brilliant Strike: A plain damage skill that has a high chance to inflict the Blind status. Not element locked.
Holy Cross: Deals two consecutive hits of Holy property physical damage. Bleeding and Blinded enemies take significantly increased damage.
Spear Flurry: Increases the user’s attack speed for a short duration. Also refreshes the cooldowns of Slash, Brilliant Strike, and Holy Cross when activated.
Faith: Passive. Increases the user’s Max HP, while also boosting their Defense and Magic Defense if a shield is equipped.
Shield Boomerang: Ranged attack with a chance to inflict the Vulnerable status. Deals additional damage to enemies that are already Vulnerable. Damage is unaffected by shield weight.
Shield Slam: Delivers a crushing blow to a nearby enemy. Vulnerable enemies take increased damage. Damage is unaffected by shield weight.
Guard: Enters a defensive stance, blocking all physical damage for a short duration. Requires a shield.
Restoration: Enchants the ground beneath the user’s feet with holy energy, restoring life to allies over time. The healing amount is based on skill level, and scales up with the target’s Max HP.

Grand Cross: Deals Holy property PHYSICAL damage to all enemies in an area around the user. Each hit has a chance to inflict the Blind and Vulnerable statuses. Gains no benefit from Int or Magic Attack.

Paladin.x: Paladin is the primary advancement option for the Crusader. It acts as an extension of the Crusader skill tree, expanding their rotations and replacing some of the lower level skills with higher powered ones.

The main character of the Paladin is exemplified in their two new buffs. Castigating Aura provides the user access to Holy property attacks, increases their Hit Rate, and grants offensive and damaging bonuses to all of their other skills. Its counterpart, Providence, does the opposite: it endows the user’s Armor with the Holy Element, increases their Perfect Dodge, and grants all of their skills defensive and control based effects. These two buffs do not stack, but have low cooldowns to allow switching between them as the situation demands.

Beyond that, the Paladin skill tree is divided into two branches, much like Crusader before them. The first is focused on Spear skills, making use of Bleeding and Blind to maximize damage output, while the latter is focused on Shield Skills, utilizing the Vulnerable Status to fight at any range.

Unlike most classes, each branch also comes with two “ultimate” skills. The first (Grand Banishment and Hesperus Lit) operates like most of the tree before them, being powerful Spear and Shield based skills respectively that slightly alter their behavior based on whether the user is in Castigating Aura or Providence. The second (Martyr’s Reckoning and Gloria Domini) instead leverage the user’s HP to do incredible damage to the targeted enemy, providing an excellent burst option outside the standard skill rotation.

Finally, Paladins have access to one more “neutral” skill that slots comfortably into builds of either branch. Sanctify creates a massive area of consecrated ground around the user, granting a boost to Attack, Magic Attack, Defense, and Magic Defense for all allies that stand within it. At the same time, it periodically deals damage to all enemies that linger within the effect for too long.
Skills:

Castigating Aura: Enchants the user’s weapon with the Holy property, increases the user’s Hit, and grants all Paladin skills additional effects based on damaging and disabling enemies. Does not stack with Providence.
Providence: Enchants the user’s armor with the Holy Property, increases their Perfect Dodge, and grants all Paladin skills additional effects focused on protecting and sustaining the user.
Sanctify: Creates an area of consecrated ground that buffs the Atk, Matk, Def, and Mdef of all allies within, while periodically inflicting Holy Property damage on all enemies.
Banishing Strike: Spear skill. Deals weapon-property physical damage to a single target, dealing additional damage to Demon, Undead, and Angel Race enemies.
During Castigating Aura, the bonus damage is applied to all races instead, and the skill inflicts Bleeding.
During Providence, the skill heals the user for a portion of the damage dealt, and the skill inflicts Blind.

Overbrand: Spear Skill. The user whirls their spear around, striking all enemies in the area and attempting to inflict Bleeding and Blind. Enemies already suffering from these statuses take additional damage.
During Castigating Aura, the Status Chance is increased.
During Providence, the user gains the Endure effect for a short time.
Grand Banishment: The user calls a massive spear from the heavens to obliterate the target, striking all enemies in the area around them for massive damage and inflicting Holy Weakness.
During Castigating Aura, the skill’s damage is doubled.
During Providence, this skill stuns all enemies struck for two seconds.

Martyr’s Reckoning: The user sacrifices their own HP to deal massive damage to a single target. The base damage of the skill is the same as the user’s Weapon property. The HP-based portion of the damage ignores Flee, Defense, and all elemental modifiers.
During Castigating Aura, this skill also inflicts Bleeding, Vulnerable, and Blind.
During Providence, the HP Based portion of the damage is doubled.

Rapid Smiting: Shield skill. Hurls the user’s shield to strike a distant target multiple times. Damage is increased by the weight of the user’s shield, and deals additional damage to Vulnerable enemies.
During Castigating Aura, the damage is increased further by the user’s Vulnerable Potency.
During Providence, the target is briefly immobilized.
Ray of Judgement: Shield Skill. The user fires a beam of holy light from their shield, dealing Weapon-property Ranged Physical damage.
During Castigating Aura, this skill inflicts the Severe Burning status.
During Providence, this skill also inflicts the Slow status.

Hesperus Lit: Shield skill. The user delivers a crushing blow with their shield, empowered by the weight of divine judgement. Deals Weapon-property Melee Physical damage, which is increased if the target is Vulnerable. This skill also inflicts the Vulnerable Status, and deals additional damage based on the user’s Vulnerable Potency.
During Castigating Aura, this skill is guaranteed to be Critical.
During Providence, this skill inflicts the Stun Status for two seconds.
Gloria Domini: The user calls down the wrath of God on a single target, dealing exceptional damage that ignores Defense and all elemental modifiers.
During Castigating Aura, this skill inflicts the Vulnerable, Breach, and Holy Weakness Statuses.
During Providence, this skill inflicts additional damage based on the user’s Current HP.

Royal Guard.x: Royal Guard is the alternative advancement option for Crusaders. While Paladins focus on infusing the Crusader’s playstyle with additional holy might, the Royal Guard instead opts to turn to sheer physical prowess to protect their allies and dispatch their foes.

The Royal Guard Skill Tree divides into three branches. Most Royal Guards will likely choose to invest a little into all three, but dedicating themselves to a single one will unlock a very different playstyle than the others.

The first two are precisely what one would expect, Spear and Shield skills respectively. The Spear Skills continue to make use of Bleeding, Vulnerable, and Blind, culminating in a powerful AoE that takes advantages of these statuses to deal immense damage and stun the enemies. In contrast, the Shield skills focus on the user themselves, granting protective Barriers for themselves while they deal damage, ending with the ability to convert the user’s Barrier into offensive power for a single devastating blow.

Straddling the line between these two distinct trees are the Royal Guard’s utility skills. Guardian Angel allows the Royal Guard to sacrifice their own HP to provide a powerful shield to all allies, while Assault Break gives all of their autoattacks a chance at inflicting double damage. A strange effect, you might think, until you read the next two skills: Guardian Stance and Assault Stance both grant the user a massive boost to Attack Speed, but entirely block the use of other skills. Once they come to an end, however, they trigger an explosive effect based on the damage taken or the damage dealt by the user during their time active. This gives Royal Guards a unique autoattack style build, if the user is wise about timing their stances correctly.

Radiant Sweep: Spear Skill. The user delivers a whirling slash with their spear, attempting to blind enemies struck with holy light. All enemies struck have a chance of receiving the Blind Status. The damage of this skill is enhanced by the user’s Dexterity, and deals additional damage to Bleeding targets.

Impale: Spear Skill. The user hurls a holy spear at a distant target, attempting to pin them in place. Deals Ranged Physical damage to a single target, attempting to inflict Bleeding and Slow. If the target is Blind, it also immobilizes the target for a short duration. The damage of this skill scales with the user’s Dexterity and deals additional damage to Blinded enemies.

Cannon Spear: Spear Skill. The user launches their spear like a cannon, driving it through all enemies before them. Does massive damage that is increased against Blind, Bleeding, and Vulnerable enemies. Any enemy struck that has at least two of these statuses is additionally stunned. Scales with the user’s Dexterity.

Shield Press: Shield Skill. The user slams their shield into an enemy, dealing damage and generating a protective Barrier around themselves with HP based on the amount of damage dealt. The damage of this skill scales with the user’s Vitality.

Shield Shooting: Shield Skill. The user hurls their shield at a distant target while taking a defensive stance to prepare for retaliation. Deals Ranged Physical damage to a single target, then creates a Barrier for the user with HP based on the damage dealt. The damage of this skill scales with the user’s Vitality.

Burst Slash: The user delivers a vengeful slash with their weapon, turning their defensive Barrier into offensive power. Deals massive damage to a single target which is increased if the target is Vulnerable. If the user has an active Barrier, it is consumed to deal additional damage. Additionally scales with the user’s Vitality.

Guardian Angel: The user expends their own life force to bestow a protective blessing on their party. Consumes half of the user’s remaining HP to create a temporary Barrier that blocks damage for all party members. The amount of HP the Barrier has is based on the amount of HP consumed to activate this skill. When mastered, this skill also reduces the cooldown of Guardian Stance by 10 seconds.

Guardian Stance: The user takes up a defensive stance, ready to block any damage they might receive. For a short duration, the user cannot cast any skills, but their ASPD Limit is increased and all damage they receive is reduced. When Guardian Stance ends, the user is healed for a portion of the damage they took while it was active.

Assault Break: The user infuses their weapon with divine power, giving all of their autoattacks a chance to inflict double damage for the duration. When mastered, this skill reduces the cooldown of Assault Stance by 10 seconds.

Assault Stance: The user takes up an offensive stance, focused on dealing exceptional damage at the cost of all else. For a short duration, the user cannot cast any skills, but their ASPD Limit and Crit Rate are significantly boosted. When Assault Stance ends, it triggers a burst attack that strikes all enemies around them for an amount of damage based on the damage they dealt while in Assault Stance.

Merchant.x: The Merchant is the “Bruiser” of the first jobs. Merchants aim to survive their fights in the simplest way possible: kill the enemy fast enough that it can’t kill you. Merchant skills give options to boost Hit, Crit, and ASPD all very early in the game, and have multiple skills capable of dealing Critical damage and inflicting the Stun status, briefly disabling enemies to buy the extra few seconds needed to close out a fight before it gets too hairy.

This of course is also the Merchant’s primary weakness. With all of its skills aimed toward offensive utility, it has difficulty engaging in prolonged encounters, especially those with multiple enemies at a time. And though it boasts greater ASPD and auto-attack damage than other classes, its damage skills are extremely SP intensive, making the leveling experience very “stop and go” until they can secure a decent beginning equipment set.
Merchants have two key “status effects”: Stun and Extort.
The Stun status is exactly what it sounds like: it disables the enemy for a short time, typically two or three seconds. Stunned enemies cannot act, and their flee is reduced to zero.

The Extort status isn’t really a status, per se. Instead, it functions using the Spirit Sphere system. By using the Extort skill, Merchants build up stacks (or “coins,” if you like) which can be expended to boost the damage of other skills.
Merchants cap at job level 50, giving them 50 skill points to spend on the following skills:
Axe Mastery: Boosts the damage and Hit rate of One and Two-Handed Axes.
Axe Boomerang: Throws the user’s axe at a distant target, knocking them back a few cells and also having a chance to inflict the Stun status.
Crush: Delivers a single heavy blow to the target with a chance to Stun them. This skill gets bonus damage and Crit Rate against enemies that are already stunned.
Extort: Deals a small amount of damage to an enemy, increasing the user’s “coin” count by one. The coins provide a minimal ATK boost, but are mostly used as a resource to be consumed by other skills.
Mammonite: Deals heavy damage to a single target. If the user has any stacks of Extort, consumes all of them to do massively improved damage and guarantees the skill will Crit.
Crazy Uproar: Consumes Extort stacks to whip the party into an uproar, increasing the ASPD and Crit Rate of all members.

Blacksmith.x: Blacksmith is the primary advancement option for the Merchant. In keeping with the Merchant’s strategy of “damage over all else,” the Blacksmith class has virtually nothing in the way of defensive options, relying on good equipment and exceptional damage output to see it through most encounters.

Offensively, the Blacksmith has two primary strategies. The first is to focus on self-buffs and deliver damage through autoattacks. In exchange for no longer affecting party members, the Blacksmith buffs have been made considerably stronger, and gain additional bonuses that apply only to autoattacks.

The second strategy is the more familiar one to the Merchant: build up Extort stacks through either Merchant’s Extort or Blacksmith’s Rush Down, then expend them all for tremendous burst through either Merchant’s Mammonite or Blacksmith’s Axe Tornado, supplemented with Hammer Fall to provide a bit more AoE damage and an additional source of Stun to sneak through some more challenging encounters.

In addition to these offensive skills, the Blacksmith also has access to a suite of supportive skills. Though they require some time investment to set up in crafting the required components, they allow the Blacksmith to tune the party’s weapons and armor to deal with the varied situations they will face, making them an invaluable member of any party even beyond their exceptional DPS.
Blacksmiths have access to the following skills:
Steel Heart: Passive. Increases the Neutral Resist and Potion Effectiveness of the user. The only truly defensive skill in the tree.
Adrenaline Rush: Increases the user’s Attack Speed and Hit Rate for a duration. Has full uptime.
Weapon Perfection: Removes the size penalty of all weapons, while also increasing the Critical Damage of autoattacks. Has full uptime.
Power Thrust: Increases the damage of all skills used by a small amount, while greatly increasing the damage and Defense Pierce of autoattacks. Has full uptime.
Rush Down: The user rushes to a distant target, dealing significant damage that can be Critical. Generates an Extort stack on hit, but has increased cooldown for each Extort stack on the user.
Hammer Fall: Slams the ground, dealing damage with a chance to stun all enemies in a small area and generates one stack of Extort.

Axe Tornado: Spins with the axe, dealing heavy damage to all enemies around the user. If the user has any Extort stacks, consumes all of them to deal massively increased damage that is guaranteed to be Critical.

Maximize Power: The user focuses all of their strength into a short burst, maximizing their damage output for a short duration. Immediately generates five stacks of Extort and increases the user’s Crit Rate by 100 for five seconds.
Equipment Maintenance: Passive. Increases the duration and effectiveness of Weapon and Armor Reinforcement.

Weapon Reinforcement: Reinforces the weapons of the party, providing a different beneficial effect depending on which level is used. Each level except level 1 requires a specific Maintenance Kit, which must be crafted at the Blacksmith’s Guild.
At Level 1, this skill gives additional Neutral Property damage to physical attacks and increases the Weapon Attack of all party members.

Armor Reinforcement: Reinforces the armor of the party, providing different beneficial effects depending on which level is used. Each level except level 1 requires a specific Maintenance Kit, which must be crafted at the Blacksmith’s Guild.
At Level 1, this skill gives additional Hard and Soft defense to all party members.

Mastersmith.x: Mastersmith is the primary advancement option for the Blacksmith. It very much continues in the same vein as the Blacksmith before it: build lots of damage and hope the enemy dies before you do, relying almost entirely on gear to build up the survivability needed to make your way through each encounter while your skills deal the maximum damage possible, making those encounters as short as possible.

The Mastersmith tree builds out in the same way as the Blacksmith tree. There is a branch focused on autoattacks, a branch focused on building and spending Extort, and a branch focused on item crafting.

The autoattack branch provides a number of short-term buffs to give a large boost to your attacks. These have nothing close to full uptime, so you will need to wait patiently for the opportunity to utilize them to their maximum effect.

The Extort branch gains three skills of ascending Cooldown - a short CD to replace the use of the Extort skill in your primary combo, a medium CD to add a large spike of damage and grant access to the Vulnerable status, and a very long CD to expend accumulated Extort stacks for massive damage.

The crafting branch allows the Mastersmith to create permanent Weapon and Armor mods. These can be used by any class, replacing the Random Options they generated with more focused bonuses. While the bonuses offered by these modifiers affect all classes, they have enhanced effects for Mastersmiths who have the Weapon and Armor Modification skills.
Skills:

Meltdown: The user superheats their weapon, passively increasing their Burning Damage and giving their Whirling Axe procs a chance to inflict the Severe Burning status. When activated, autoattacks and Whirling Axe procs will be treated as Burning damage for a short duration.

Whirling Axe: The user adopts a wild, whirling fighting style, passively giving their attacks a chance to splash in a 5x5 area around them. This splash will also deal additional damage to the original target of the attack. When activated, the trigger chance is massively increased for a short duration.

Berserk: The user enters a battle frenzy, gaining massive Damage Reduction, Attack, and ASPD for the duration. While active, the user cannot use any skills or consumables. When the Frenzy status ends, the user’s HP is reduced to 10% of their maximum, and their SP is reduced to zero. Triggering this skill automatically activates Meltdown and Whirling Axe at their learned levels, extends their duration to 10 seconds, and increases the user’s ASPD cap to 190.
Overwhelm: Slams into the enemy with tremendous force, generating a stack of Extort. If the enemy is Stunned or Staggered, they take additional damage.

Cleave: Delivers a sundering blow to the enemy, shredding any protective abilities. Strips most defensive abilities from the target, then deals heavy physical damage that is increased if the target is Vulnerable. If the target is not Vulnerable, has a chance to inflict the Vulnerable status instead.

Power Swing: Slams the user’s weapon into the head of the enemy, dealing massive damage based on the user’s Extort stacks. Gains bonus effects cumulatively based on the number of Extort stacks consumed. If the user has no Extort stacks, the skill will miss.
Inflicts Vulnerable for 5 Seconds
Refreshes the Cooldown of Overwhelm
Inflicts Stun for 2 Seconds
Refreshes the Cooldown of Cleave
Splashes in a 5x5 Area

Equipment Modification: Increases the efficiency of Weapon and Armor Mods on the user’s equipment. This only affects mods used by the owner of this skill. It does not influence the strength of mods crafted by the user but used by other players.

Weapon Modification: Combines materials to create a Weapon Modification Device. The device can be used to replace the Random Options on any weapon. The level of this skill learned improves the efficiency of those mods for the user, but does not influence the success rate of crafting or the strength of the rolls received.

Armor Modification: Combines materials to create an Armor Modification Device. The device can be used to replace the Random Options on any Armor (not garments or shoes). The level of this skill learned improves the efficiency of those mods for the user, but does not influence the success rate of crafting or the strength of the rolls received.

Mechanic.x: Mechanic is the alternative advancement option for Blacksmiths. While the Mastersmith focuses their efforts on drawing the maximum possible power out of the equipment they and their friends use, the Mechanic turns to creating brand new tools to aid them in combat.

This manifests in two very different build paths. The first is the construction of the Madogear, a massive suit of power armor that grants the wearer greatly enhanced physical abilities. The Madogear gives access to a wide variety of skills from single target heavy damage, to ranged attacks, to even defensive shielding to protect them from harm. The user also has the option of pushing the Madogear into overdrive, greatly increasing its capabilities at the cost of overheating and dealing constant damage to themselves over time.

The second build path revolves around the creation of support drones. These drones fight alongside the user, attacking and using skills at their own discretion, while also providing a passive bonus to their summoner while alive. These are coupled with a pair of Command skills, allowing the Mechanic to push their drones past their ordinary limits for short bursts of time to exhibit greater combat effectiveness.

Unlike the Mastersmith, the Mechanic gains no new abilities that generate Extort Stacks, and virtually all of their abilities cost Extort Stacks to use. But things are not so dire as they appear: while wearing a Madogear, all Madogear skills have their Extort costs reduced to 0. Similarly, while the user is NOT wearing a Madogear, all Drone skills have their Extort costs waived. This allows Mechanics to splash into both trees if they so wish, while rewarding those that dedicate fully to one side.

Madogear Construction: Skill in the construction of Madogear, a mechanical suit of power armor that enhances the user’s abilities. Each level increases the effectiveness of Madogear skills and reduces the amount of damage taken from the Burning status. These bonuses only apply while the Madogear is equipped. While it is equipped, the Extort Cost of all Madogear skills is removed.

Machine Slam: Madogear Skill. The user leverages the immense strength of the Madogear to crush the targeted enemy, dealing massive damage in an area around them. The damage of this skill scales with the user’s Vitality. During Overdrive, this skill has a reduced Cooldown and additionally inflicts Stun.

Arm Cannon: Madogear Skill. The user fires a barrage from the Madogear’s cannon, dealing repeated hits to a single target. Deals additional damage to targets that are Stunned or Staggered, and inflicts the Staggered status. The damage of this skill scales with the user’s Vitality. During Overdrive, this skill has a reduced Cooldown and additionally inflicts Vulnerable and Severe Burning.

Active Shielding: Madogear Skill. The user activates the defensive shielding of the Madogear, creating a protective Barrier that blocks all damage received for a short duration. The Barrier’s HP is based on the Madogear Construction level of the user and the current amount of Extort Stacks they have. If a Madogear is currently equipped, the Extort stacks are counted, but they are not consumed. During Overdrive, this skill always treats the user as having five Extort Stacks.

Overdrive: Madogear Skill. The user forces the Madogear into overdrive, increasing its performance but causing it to overheat to a dangerous degree. Instantly refreshes the cooldowns of all Madogear Skills when activated, then gives them bonus effects for a short duration, but continuously inflicts Burning Damage on the user until its duration expires.

Support Unit Construction: Skill in the construction and deployment of support drones. Each level increases the base stats of constructed drones and enhances the effects of supporting Protocol skills. While a Madogear is NOT equipped, the Extort Cost of all Drone skills is removed. Support Drones inherit their summoner’s Hit Rate and half of their Crit Rate, and are not targeted for attacks by monsters.

Deploy Combat Drone: Drone Skill. Deploys a mobile combat drone to fight alongside the user. Its stats are influenced by the user’s Base Level and stats, and the user’s level of Support Unit Construction. Combat Drones are melee combatants that regularly inflict the Severe Burning status. While a Combat Drone is active, its master gains a bonus to their ASPD Limit.

Deploy Support Drone: Drone Skill. Deploys a mobile support drone to fight alongside the user. Its stats are influenced by the user’s Base Level and stats, and the user’s level of Support Unit Construction. Support Drones are ranged combatants that regularly inflict the Blind status on enemies they attack. While a Support Drone is active, its master gains a bonus to their Defense Pierce.

Attack Protocol: Drone Skill. Issues an offensive command to all currently active drones, causing them to enter a berserk state where they gain new skills. At the same time, all allies in the area of the user have their Attack increased.

Defense Protocol: Drone Skill. Issues a defensive command to all currently active drones, causing them to enter a protective state where they gain new skills. At the same time, all allies in the area of the user receive a small Barrier.

Alchemist.x: Alchemist is the alternative advancement option for the Merchant. Unlike its first class, the Alchemist enjoys multiple possible playstyles, from the very familiar “all gas no breaks” style of the Merchant to more defensive and supportive options.

On the offensive side, the Alchemist uses its newly acquired Chemical skills to do exceptional damage to enemies, even from a distance. Acid Terror and Demonstration serve to both deal regular and consistent damage to enemies, while also inflicting the Vulnerable and Burning statuses respectively. These skills also function to generate Extort stacks, allowing the Alchemist to very quickly build up Extort for use with Mammonite or their new finisher, Conflagration, to deal massive damage over a wide area.

But offense isn’t the only choice available for the Alchemist. Similar to, though not quite as flexible as, the Blacksmith’s Reinforcement skills, Alchemist has access to a suite of Alchemical Enhancements that provide powerful improvements to their party’s equipment. That said, these skills do not need a party to find themselves useful, as they all can apply their full effect to both the user themselves and their Homunculus. (Scroll down for a more detailed look at the Homunculus system)
Alchemists gain access to the following skills:
Chemical Research: “Mastery” skill for Chemical-type skills. Increases the damage of Acid Terror, Demonstration, and Conflagration, while also increasing their chance to apply their status effects.
Acid Terror: Deals significant Ranged Physical damage to a distant target with a chance to inflict the Vulnerable status. This skill generates one Extort stack on use.

Demonstration: Ignites a small fire at the targeted location, dealing constant Fire property damage to enemies in a small area around it. The initial cast generates one stack of Extort, while each hit has a chance to inflict the Burning status.
Conflagration: Consumes all of the user’s Extort stacks to deal massive Ranged Physical damage over a wide area. This skill has a chance to inflict the Bleeding and Burning status effects.
Enhancement Research: Passive. Increases the duration and effectiveness of all Alchemical Enhancements.
Energized Armor: Coats an ally’s armor with an alchemical agent that disperses the force of incoming attacks. Increases the target’s resistance to attacks of all elements for a duration.
Synthetic Shield: Creates an autonomously acting shield to protect the target. Increases the targets Magic Defense, while also giving them a chance to block any physical damage taken.
Alchemical Weapon: Coats the target’s weapon with an alchemical agent that increases its potency. Increases the Attack, Magic Attack, Defense Pierce, and Magic Defense Pierce of the target.

Aid Potion: Hurls a specially crafted Throwing Potion at the target, recovering HP (or SP) based on the potion thrown. Throwing potions must be crafted at the Alchemist’s Guild, but are not consumed on use.
Homunculus Research: Passive. Enables the user to craft Homunculi at the Alchemist’s Guild. Each additional level beyond the first improves the stats of any Homunculus summoned by the user.
Homunculus System:

The Homunculus System has been entirely reworked. The vanilla system for using Homunculi has been entirely removed: Homunculi have predetermined stats, predetermined skills, and do not gain experience.

Another major change is that the player has virtually no control over the Homunculus’s actions. Homunculi have their own AI (which cannot be changed by the player in any way). All Homunculi behave differently, based on what type of Homunculus they are, and will use all of their skills automatically as they see fit. That said, the Alchemist has access to seven Command skills that allow them to give instructions to their Homunculus, triggering their skills while ignoring their internal cooldowns. These Command skills are obtained immediately upon job change, and thus are available to all Alchemists regardless of build.

Alchemists can craft Homunculus Embryos at the Alchemist’s Guild. These embryos are used to summon their relevant Homunculus, but are not consumed on use. When first crafted, these Embryos will summon a Homunculus that is level 60 and has access to only one skill. Further crafting at the Alchemist’s Guild will allow them to upgrade their Homunculus, each level giving it higher stats and more skills to use. The highest level of Homunculus available to an Alchemist is level 99, after which the Alchemist must advance to either the Biochemist or Geneticist job to continue their Homunculus’s growth.
A brief overview of the four available Homunculus types and their behavior:

Lif: Kind and compassionate, Lif will do everything in her power to support you while you fight. However, she doesn’t like fighting herself, and will even refuse to attack back in cases where she manages to pull aggro. Careful use of the Return and Hide commands will be needed to keep her out of harm’s way so she can continue supporting her master and allies.

Vanilmirth: Bloodthirsty and dangerous, Vanilmirth will proactively seek out enemies to fight and hold nothing back when it finds one. However its defensive options are rather weak, requiring a discerning master to keep it from biting off more than it can chew, lest it face frequent and untimely deaths.

Amistr: Brave and highly protective of its master, Amistr will go out of its way to seek out and hold the attention of enemies in the area. While it has great defensive capabilities which it can even share with its master, it doesn’t have the damage output to handle many encounters on its own. Amistr’s natural toughness combined with clever use of the Defend command can make it an exceptional tank for the Alchemist that wants to focus their own efforts on putting out damage.

Filir: Filir is quick and deadly, boasting a high physical attack stat, high attack speed, and low cooldowns on its offensive abilities, which it learns relatively early in life. However, it is very much a coward, with only its natural Flee and the Hiding skill to protect itself. Filir will not proactively engage enemies, and may even ignore Attack commands if it isn’t already fighting, preferring to wait until its master has the monster’s attention before swooping in to secure the kill.
The following is a list of the seven Command skills available to Alchemists. Each skill is unlocked once a Homunculus capable of responding to that command is crafted.
Command: Attack!
Orders the Homunculus to perform its “Attack” action. The Homunculus may not respond to this command if it is not currently engaged with a target, or if there is no applicable target in range.
Command: Defend!
Orders the Homunculus to perform its “Defend” action, typically involving blocking or reducing incoming damage for itself.
Command: Support!
Orders the Homunculus to perform its “Support” action, typically involving buffing the Alchemist, and sometimes itself in the process.
Command: Hide!
Orders the Homunculus to perform its “Hide” action. This is always to use the Thief skill “Hiding,” making it (mostly) invulnerable and dropping all aggro for a short duration.
Command: Ultimate!
Orders the Homunculus to perform its “Ultimate” action. The effect of this varies widely based on the type of Homunculus.
Command: Return!
Orders the Homunculus to return to its master’s side, immediately teleporting it back regardless of the distance between them (as long as they are on the same map).
Command: Move!
Orders the Homunculus to move to the targeted location. It will ignore enemies until it reaches its destination.

Biochemist.x: Biochemist is the primary advancement option for Alchemists. They turn their insatiable curiosity for the workings of chemical matter toward the interaction of chemicals with each other and organic bodies.

Biochemist skills are divided into two trees, which much like the chemical compounds they work with, are very much intended to be mixed together. The first tree is the one that will be most familiar to Alchemists, the Chemical Skills. This new suite of skills leverage the user’s bonuses to Burning Damage and Vulnerable Potency to deal exceptional damage even over an area, and rather than generating or consuming Extort stacks, instead receive a reduction to their cooldowns for every Extort Stack the user maintains. The one exception is the ever feared Acid Demonstration, which consumes the user’s Extort Stacks to deal an absurd amount of damage to a single target.

Opposite the Chemical skills are a new line of skills, known as Stimulants. These stimulants are powerful drugs concocted by the Biochemist to enhance their allies for combat, providing incredibly strong short term buffs, but at the cost of severe negative side effects. Some skills even turn these side effects to great use, inflicting them on enemies to make these drugs into effective weapons in and of themselves. These Stimulant skills also gain beneficial effects for the user maintaining a high Extort count, but unlike the Chemical Skills, these will actually generate Extort stacks for the user too...if the user is willing to invest enough skill points into them to unlock their full effects.

Unlike Geneticists, Biochemists gain no skills that directly interact with homunculi created during their time as an Alchemist. They do, however, gain access to evolved versions of those homunculi, allowing them to grow up to level 150 along with their master. And unlike Geneticist homunculi, which must gradually gain their abilities over time, Biochemist homunculi mastered all of their abilities by level 99, so they are able to wield their full arsenal of skills right from the beginning.
Skills:
Greater Aid Potion: Throws a potion and scatters its contents over a wide area, healing all allies within its range. Uses the same Throwing Potions as the regular Aid Potion skill.

Incinerate: Chemical Skill. Throws a combination of volatile chemicals that ignite to create a short-lived field of fire. Enemies within the field take Physical Fire Property damage rapidly over time, which is treated as Burning Damage and scales with the user’s Intelligence. For each Extort Stack the user has, the Cooldown of this skill is reduced.

Acidic Cloud: Chemical Skill. Unleashes a cloud of acidic gas around the target, dealing Weapon Property Physical Damage to all enemies in an area around them. The damage of this skill is increased by the user’s Vulnerable Potency and scales with the user’s Intelligence. For each Extort Stack the user has, the Cooldown of this skill is reduced.

Alchemic Cannon: Chemical Skill. Using intense alchemical reactions, the user fires a projectile at devastating speed toward the target, which explodes on contact from its sheer velocity. Deals damage to the target and all enemies around them, dealing additional damage to Vulnerable and Burning targets, and scaling with the user’s Intelligence. For each Extort Stack the user has, the Cooldown of this skill is reduced.

Acid Demonstration: Chemical Skill. The user throws a combination of volatile chemicals that explode violently when they reach the target, doing massive Neutral Property damage to a single foe. This skill consumes all of the user’s Extort Stacks, gaining benefits based on the number consumed. The damage is heavily influenced by the number of Extort Stacks consumed, and scales with the user’s Intelligence. If the user has no Extort Stacks available, the skill will miss.
1 Extort: Inflicts Vulnerable for 10 Seconds
2 Extort: Damage is increased by Vulnerable Potency
3 Extort: Inflicts Burning for 10 Seconds
4 Extort: Damage is treated as Burning Damage
5 Extort: Extort Stacks are not consumed

Stimulant Research: Research into the safe and effective use of various drugs and stimulants. Each level reduces the negative side effects of Stimulant Skills cast by the user on allies, and enhances the effectiveness of Stimulant skills used on enemies.

Crystal Clarity: Stimulant Skill. Administers a drug to the target that helps clear their mind, improving the effectiveness and efficiency of their skill casting, but causes them to focus so intensely on offense that they neglect their own safety. Increases the target’s Hit Rate and reduces all of their Fixed Cast Times, but also massively reduces their Defense and Magic Defense. If cast at level 3 or higher, the user generates one stack of Extort and the target’s skills cannot be interrupted for the duration.

Frenzy: Stimulant Skill. Administers a drug to the target that invokes a berserk madness in them, making their attacks remarkably vicious, but also putting an intense strain on their bodies. Massively increases the target’s Defense Pierce and Magic Defense Pierce, but also reduces the target’s Max HP and SP for the duration. If cast at level 3 or higher, the user generates one stack of Extort and the target’s Movement Speed is increased for the duration.

White Ice: Stimulant Skill. Administers a drug to the target that numbs their senses, making them extremely tolerant to pain, but also makes it difficult for them to wield their weapons and magic with the same dexterity as before. Reduces the damage the target takes from Bleeding, Burning, and Poison, at the cost of reducing their Crit Rate and increasing their Variable Cast Times. If cast at level 3 or higher, the user generates one stack of Extort and the target gains the Endure effect for the duration.

Moonveil: Stimulant Skill. Administers a drug to the target that accelerates their senses, giving them the impression that time has slowed down around them. In this state, they are able to avoid incoming attacks with ease, but will have difficulty gauging their own strength properly. Boosts the target’s Perfect Dodge for the duration, but also reduces their Attack and Magic Attack. If cast at level 3 or higher, the user generates one stack of Extort and the target’s skills all have reduced cooldowns for the duration.

Death Drip: Stimulant Skill. Administers a lethal neurotoxin to the target, dealing an instant burst of Poison Property damage that ignores Defense and is treated as Poison Status damage. If cast at level 3 or higher, the user generates one stack of Extort, and the target also receives the Deadly Poison status.

Pyrelight: Stimulant Skill. Administers a searing toxin to the target, burning them from the inside out. Inflicts significant damage to the target that is treated as Burning Damage. If cast at level 3 or higher, the user generates one stack of Extort and also inflicts the Severe Burning status on the target.

Geneticist.x: The Geneticist is the alternate advancement option for Alchemists. They turn away from research into chemicals and potions and instead focus on the study of life itself. Their skills split evenly between two schools: Fauna skills, based on developing skills learned from the Homunculi they can create, and Flora skills, based on using genetically modified plants in combat.

Fauna skills are each inspired by one of the five Homunculus S: Eira, Bayeri, Sera, Dieter, and Eleanor. While any Fauna skill can be used by any Geneticist, the active Homunculus they have will change the behavior of their skills: the off-theme skills will generate stacks of Extort and have slightly weaker effects, while the on-theme skill will consume stacks of Extort to have a much stronger effect.

Flora skills are more directly offensive. They include both summoning skills, creating short-term plant companions to attack enemies and support allies, and instant use skills to damage and hinder enemies.

However, the Geneticist is not forced to commit entirely to one side of the skill tree. With low max levels on all of their skills, they are quite capable — and in fact will eventually be required to — split between both sides of the skill tree. Finding which skills from each side of the skill tree synergize together and with the individual player’s playstyle is the key to building an effective Geneticist. And like most 3-2 jobs, integrating those skill choices with their previous Merchant and Alchemist skills will be the key to true mastery.
Fauna Specialization: Increases the stats of summoned Homunculi, and enhances the effects of all Fauna-type Geneticist skills.

Gift of Life: Sacrifices a portion of the user’s HP to heal all allies in the area, including summoned entities. If Eira is present, consumes the user’s Extort stacks to reduce this skill’s Cooldown. Otherwise, generates one stack of Extort.

Gift of Light: Shines a holy light on the user and their summoned entities, protecting them from harm. Cures numerous negative status effects and provides immunity to them for a short duration. If Bayeri is present, consumes the user’s Extort stacks to also reduce all damage taken for the duration. Otherwise, generates one stack of Extort.

Gift of Venom: Creates a pool of toxic venom on the ground, dealing constant Poison property damage and attempting to slow enemies within it. If Sera is present, consumes the user’s Extort stacks to increase the duration of the pools. Otherwise, generates one stack of Extort.

Gift of Flame: Invokes a burst of flame at the target’s location, dealing Fire damage to enemies in the area with a chance to inflict the Burning status. If Dieter is present, consumes the user’s Extort stacks to do massively improved damage. Otherwise, generates one stack of Extort.

Gift of Strength: Draws out the savage nature of the user and their summoned entities, massively increasing their Crit Rate. If Eleanor is present, consumes the user’s Extort Stacks to increase the Defense Pierce of all affected for the duration., Otherwise, generates one stack of Extort.
Flora Specialization: Increases the stats of summoned Plants, and improves the effectiveness of all Flora skills.

Explosive Growth: Causes a massive growth of plants in the targeted area that rapidly grow, strike all enemies in the area, then immediately wither and die. This skill gains bonus effects based on the user’s Summoned Flora.

Mandragora Howl: Pulls a mandragora from its resting place, inducing it to howl so intensely it damages nearby enemies. Deals physical damage around the user with a chance to Slow. This skill inflicts various Status Effects based on the summoned Flora. If the user has a Summoned Warrior or Fairy, the cast will be centered around them instead of around the caster.

Summon Warrior: Summons a Wooden Warrior to fight by the user’s side for a short duration. Only one Wooden Warrior can be present at a time, and it cannot be summoned alongside a Forest Sprite. Wooden Warriors are melee combatants that deal increased damage to enemies suffering from Bleeding and Vulnerable, and reduce the cooldown of the user’s Acid Terror while alive.

Summon Fairy: Summons a Forest Sprite to fight for the user for a short duration. Only one Sprite can be summoned at a time, and it cannot be summoned alongside a Wooden Warrior. Forest Sprites are ranged combatants that use a mixture of supportive and offensive skills, and reduce the cooldown of the user’s Demonstration while alive.

Summon Infernal Tree: Summons a Cursed Tree to fight for the user for a short duration. Only one Cursed Tree can be summoned at a time, but it can be summoned alongside other Flora. Cursed Trees do not move or attack, but occasionally immobilize enemies and empower allies in the area around them. While alive, Wooden Warriors and Forest Sprites nearby will enter a berserk state, causing them to use skills more frequently and deal more damage.

Thief.x: The Thief occupies a role somewhere between the Swordsman and the Merchant. With more than half of its skill tree dedicated to defensive options, Thieves are remarkably resilient even with their lower HP pools. Envenom and Dagger Mastery give them the ability to put out a stream of consistent damage over time, all while avoiding virtually all incoming damage, be it through Flee, or through their evasion skills in Hiding and Backslide.

Unfortunately, this survivability does not come without caveats. Hiding and Backslide can mitigate tremendous amounts of damage, but both come with heavy cooldowns, leaving the brunt of survivability to be carried by the Flee rate. This leaves Thieves uniquely vulnerable to enemies that use large amounts of magic, or that attack in large numbers. With no burst or AoE options, the Thief is forced to rely on their slow and steady DPS to deal with these tricky situations, giving their survivability a very “feast or famine” vibe.
Thieves have two key status effects: Poison and Blind.

Poison deals constant damage over time to enemies. This damage is based on the user’s Agility, and scales up with their base level. Though they have few other damage options available, Poison allows the Thief to continue dealing damage to enemies even while weaving in and out of attacks, only needing to swoop back in for another hit every five or so seconds to keep the damage rolling.

Blind, while applied offensively, is generally more of a defensive status. Blind greatly reduces a target’s Hit and Flee rate, thus making it easier to apply damage to them and harder for them to apply damage to you.
Thieves cap at job level 50, giving them 50 skill points to put into the following skills:
Dagger Mastery: Increases the damage and Double Attack rate of Daggers.
Envenom: Deals minor poison damage, with a chance to inflict the Poison status.
Sand Attack: Deals a fair amount of Neutral damage at a small range, with a chance to inflict the Blind status.
Nimbleness: Increases the base Flee and Movement Speed.
Hiding: Hides under the ground to avoid all attacks for a brief time. Has a lengthy cooldown that can be reduced with higher skill levels.
Backslide: Shifts the user backward instantly 7 cells. Has a lengthy cooldown that can be reduced with higher skill levels.

Assassin.x: The Assassin is the primary advancement option for the Thief class. While the Thief’s skill tree was very much defensively minded, the Assassin uses that foundation to fill their skill bar with offensive options.

The core of the Assassin kit lies in their Blade Enchants. While each Enchant adds its own passive ability to the Assassin, they also serve to enhance all of the Assassin’s damage skills in various ways. While only one Blade Enchant can be active at a time, the short cooldown on them makes swapping between them as the situation dictates very possible, giving the Assassin incredible versatility in the field.

As for their actual damage skills, these are divided into two general categories: Katar skills, focusing on Critical Hits and high burst damage, and Dagger skills, focused on delivering a consistent stream of damage and increased mobility.

Finally, the Assassin draws on its roots for two defensive skills, Cloaking and Hallucination Walk. The former is a short term invisibility skill, allowing the Assassin to weave in and out of combat as necessary, while the latter gives an impressive layer of defense, maxing the user’s Perfect Dodge for a short time to help them squeak out of exceptionally dangerous situations.
Assassins gain access to the following skills:
Toxic Blades: Blade Enchant. All attacks have a chance to inflict the Poison status. Associated Status: Poison
Flashing Blades: Blade Enchant. Gain a small boost to Crit Rate. This boost is doubled by Katars. Associated Status: Blind
Rejuvenating Blades: Blade Enchant. All attacks gain a small amount of life steal. Associated Status: Slow
Katar Mastery: Passive. Increase damage and accuracy with Katars. Katars typically gain increased Crit Damage as a mastery bonus.
Grimtooth: Katar Skill. Deals ranged splash damage. Cannot be used while Hiding. Applies a different status effect based on the active Blade Enchant.

Sonic Blow: Katar Skill. Deals a high amount of physical damage. Deals bonus damage to Poisoned enemies under Toxic Blades. Ignores 50% Defense under Flashing Blades. Has a high chance to Stun under Rejuvenating Blades.
Dual Wield Mastery: Reduces the Damage and ASPD penalty for wielding multiple daggers.
Rolling Cutter: Dagger skill. Deals splash damage around the user. This skill applies a different status based on the active Blade Enchant.

Cross Impact: Dagger skill. Jumps to a distant target and delivers a quick flurry of blows. Inflicts the Deadly Poison status while under Toxic Blades. Cooldown is halved under Flashing Blades. Puts the user in Cloaking status for 2 seconds under Rejuvenating Blades.

Cloaking: The user fades into the shadows, making themselves undetectable even from Insects, Demons, and Bosses for a short time. While cloaked, they also enjoy increased Movement Speed. This skill does not evade ground-targeted skills, nor skills that targeted the user before Cloaking was cast.
Hallucination Walk: The user wraps themselves in shadows and illusions, making them all but impervious to ordinary attacks. Increases Perfect Dodge by 100 for a short duration.

Assassin Cross.x: Assassin Cross is the primary advancement option for Assassins. In contrast to the Guillotine Cross, which devotes its entire arsenal to the perfection and use of a variety of poisons, the Assassin Cross seeks to perfect their own martial skill. Following the same core principles as the Assassin before them, the Assassin Cross gains a variety of Weapon-based skills that allow them to dictate the flow of any encounter.

Dagger skills revolve around the Weapon Blocking skill. Weapon Blocking protects the user from any one physical attack, entirely nullifying its damage and giving the user the Counter State buff. While in this state, the other Dagger skills used by the Assassin Cross have their effects enhanced and their cooldowns refreshed. The tree concludes with Savage Blade, a ranged attack that proactively triggers the Counter State to allow fearsome pushes on the user’s own timing.

The Katar skills have a much different focus: deal damage fast. These skills revolve around Sonic Acceleration, a buff that increases the Attack Speed, Max Attack Speed, and reduces the Cooldowns of all other katar skills while active. This allows the Assassin Cross to bring down enemies with a swift flurry of skills or a lightning-speed barrage of autoattacks, whichever the situation demands.

The two trees are supplemented by a triplet of generic skills useful in any build. Peerless Blades is added to the lineup of Blade Enchants, granting bonuses based on how high the user is able to keep their HP. Deadly Shadow offers another way to access the Cloaking state, and grants bonus Defense Pierce and Crit Damage to the first skill used afterward. Finally, Soul Destroyer turns the user’s active Blade Enchant into a deadly projectile, consuming it to do enormous damage with a variety of properties based on which Blade Enchant was chosen.
Skills:

Peerless Blades: Infuses the user’s weapons with their own life force, providing strong benefits while the user’s HP remains high. Increases the user’s Physical Attack while their current HP meets certain thresholds, and grants new effects to all Assassin skills.
Deadly Shadow: The user turns invisible for a short time. Upon leaving the invisible state, the first skill used has a bonus to its Defense Pierce and Crit Damage.

Soul Destroyer: The user channels their active Blade Enchant into a deadly projectile and fires it at an enemy. Deals exceptional Ranged Physical damage that has additional properties based on which Blade Enchant is active.
Toxic Blades Bonus: Treated as Poison Damage
Flashing Blades Bonus: Guaranteed to Crit, ignores Physical Defense
Rejuvenating Blades Bonus: Reduces all active skill cooldowns by 5 Seconds
Peerless Blades Bonus: Deals additional damage based on the user’s Current HP

Weapon Blocking: Dagger Skill. Parries an incoming attack, blocking the next physical attack against the user. If an attack is successfully blocked, Rupture and Counter Slash have their cooldowns refreshed and the user gains the Counter State for a short time.

Rupture: Dagger Skill. Delivers a precision strike, landing a savage blow under the opponent’s guard. Deals Melee Physical damage to a single target and inflicts the Vulnerable status. If used during the Counter State, the attack deals additional damage based on the user’s Vulnerable Potency.
During Toxic Blades, also inflicts Poison.
During Flashing Blades, also inflicts Bleeding.
During Rejuvenating Blades, also inflicts Blind.
During Peerless Blades, reduces Weapon Blocking’s Cooldown by 5 seconds.

Counter Slash: Dagger skill. Lash out with perfect timing, delivering a punishing blow to all enemies in the area around the user. Deals Melee Physical damage in an area around the user, inflicting additional damage on Vulnerable enemies. If the user is currently in the Counter State, the skill repeats once for half damage.
During Toxic Blades, the damage is treated as Poison Damage.
During Flashing Blades, gains an additional 50% Defense Pierce.
During Rejuvenating Blades, grants the Hallucination Walk effect for three seconds.
During Peerless Blades, reduces the cooldown of Weapon Blocking by 5 seconds.

Savage Blade: Dagger skill. The user throws a spinning blade at a distant target, dealing moderate damage and throwing them off balance. Deals Ranged Physical damage. If the skill hits an enemy that was in the middle of casting a skill, the user enters the Counter State for a short time.
During Toxic Blades, this skill deals additional damage to Poisoned enemies.
During Flashing Blades, this skill cannot miss and is guaranteed to Crit.
During Rejuvenating Blades, this skill inflicts the Stun status.
During Peerless Blades, refreshes the Cooldowns of Rolling Cutter and Cross Impact.
Sonic Acceleration: Katar skill. The user pushes themselves to the limit, accelerating their body to the extreme. Increases the user’s ASPD, ASPD Limit, and Movement Speed for a short duration.

Dark Claw: Katar skill. Delivers a rending blow, seeking out weaknesses in the enemy’s armor. Deals additional damage to Vulnerable enemies. During Sonic Acceleration, this skill’s cooldown is halved.
During Toxic Blades, inflicts Poison.
During Flashing Blades, inflicts Bleeding.
During Rejuvenating Blades, inflicts Blind.
During Peerless Blades, reduces Sonic Acceleration’s cooldown by 5 seconds.
Phantom Claw: The user lunges at a distant target, closing the distance between them and inflicting significant damage. During Sonic Acceleration, its cooldown is halved.
During Toxic Blades, inflicts Deadly Poison.
During Flashing blades, inflicts Vulnerable.
During Rejuvenating Blades, grants the Hallucination Walk status for a few seconds.
During Peerless Blades, subtracts 5 seconds from Sonic Acceleration’s cooldown.

Meteoric Claw: The user unleashes a burst of shockwaves from their weapon, tearing through nearby enemies. All enemies around them take massive damage and receive the Bleeding and Vulnerable statuses.
During Toxic Blades, also inflicts Poison.
During Flashing Blades, the damage is increased by the user’s Vulnerable Potency.
During Rejuvenating Blades, also inflicts Stun.
During Peerless Blades, the user backslides and enters Deadly Shadow after casting.

Guillotine Cross.x: Guillotine Cross is the alternative advancement option for Assassins. While Assassin Crosses eschew dependency on Poison for their damage, preferring to rely entirely on combat skill, the Guillotine Cross has no such inhibitions. Their playstyle revolves around rapid and repeated application of the Poison Status, both to debilitate enemies and set up their own skills for stronger combos.

The key skill to the entire Guillotine Cross kit is their new Blade Enchant, Fatal Blades. This Blade Enchant coats the user’s weapon with a specialized toxin, altering the behavior of any Poison Status they inflict.

Once the Guillotine Cross has chosen their toxin, they can turn their attention to one of two skill tree paths. The first is a set of weapon skills, taking advantage of the user’s Blade Enchant and the enemy’s Poison status to deal exceptional physical damage. The tree culminates in Final Fang, a single target skill which consumes the targets Poison and Deadly Poison to deal incredible damage.

Alternatively, the Guillotine Cross can focus on Toxin skills, a set of ranged abilities that turn them into somewhat of a Ranged Caster. These skills excel at inflicting the Poison Status to a wide range of enemies and amplifying that Poison Status to deal more damage. The tree is capped off by Toxic Shock, a ranged physical attack that does minor damage, but if the target is Poisoned, causes them to explode and deal massive damage across a wide area.
Skills:

Fatal Blades: Blade Enchant. Coats the user’s weapon with a specialized toxin, modifying the Poison status inflicted by them. Each level applies a different poison. The poisons required to activate this skill from level 2 onward must be crafted.
Level 1: Increases the duration of Poison inflicted
Level 2: Poison also inflicts Blind. Poison damage is increased by Blind Potency
Level 3: Poison Damage is increased by a portion of the user’s Bleeding and Burning Damage.
Level 4: Whenever Poison ticks, it has a chance to spread to all allies of the victim in a short range.
Level 5: Poison Damage ticks twice as fast.
While any of the above are active, Assassin and Guillotine Cross Weapon skills gain Luck scaling, and all Assassin skills are enhanced.

Venom Eater: Consumes any poison suffered by the target to heal the user. The amount of healing is based on the strength of the target’s Poison. If the target is suffering from both Poison and Deadly Poison, only Poison will be consumed.

Toxic Shadow: Toxin Skill. The user imbibes a powerful toxin that deals constant damage to them over time, but in exchange massively increases their physical abilities. The damage taken from this skill is treated as Poison Damage, but is not increased by the user’s Poison Damage bonuses and cannot be cured or resisted. While active, the user gains a bonus to ASPD Limit, Movement Speed, and Attack, and all Toxin skills are enhanced.

Toxic Breath: Toxin Skill. The user unleashes a blast of toxic air, dealing Poison Property Physical Damage to all enemies in the targeted area. All enemies struck have a chance of being inflicted with the Poison Status. During Toxic Shadow, this skill inflicts Deadly Poison instead, and the chance is doubled.

Toxic Surge: Toxin Skill. Amplifies the Poison suffered by the target, refreshing its duration and increasing its damage. The target additionally takes a burst of Poison property damage that is treated as Poison Status Damage. A target’s poison can only be enhanced by Toxic Surge once, no matter how many characters apply the effect. During Toxic Shadow, this skill can be used on non-Poisoned targets.

Toxic Cloud: Toxin Skill. Creates a short-lived cloud of toxic gas that repeatedly damages enemies within its area. Enemies struck have a chance of being Poisoned. During Toxic Shadow, the damage dealt is treated as Poison Status Damage, and the skill’s damage interval is twice as fast.

Toxic Shock: Toxin Skill. Deals a moderate amount of Poison Property physical damage to a single target. If the target is suffering from Poison or Deadly Poison, instead it consumes the status to do massive Poison Property damage to all enemies in an area around them. During Toxic Shadow, all enemies struck receive the Deadly Poison status.

Thirsting Fangs: Weapon Skill. Temporarily applies a second Guillotine Cross toxin to the user’s weapon. This second poison stacks with both Fatal Blades and ordinary Assassin Blade Enchants. While active, all Blade Enchants are disabled (but not removed). Multiple copies of the same toxin (from Fatal Blades and this skill) do not stack.
Piercing Fang: Weapon Skill. Deal a quick, piercing stab to a single target, attempting to inflict the Poison status. If the target is already Poisoned, this skill ignores Defense.
During Toxic Blades, this skill inflicts Deadly Poison instead.
