During Flashing Blades, this skill additionally inflicts Vulnerable.
During Rejuvenating Blades, this skill additionally inflicts Slow.
During Fatal Blades, the skill is guaranteed to be Critical against poisoned enemies.

Seeking Fang: Weapon Skill. Lunge at a distant target, dealing significant damage. If it strikes a Poisoned enemy, this skill cannot miss. If it strikes an enemy with Deadly Poison, it is guaranteed to Crit.
During Toxic Blades, this skill additionally inflicts Poison.
During Flashing Blades, this skill’s cooldown is halved.
During Rejuvenating Blades, this skill increases the user’s Movement Speed for a short time.
During Fatal Blades, the skill is guaranteed to be Critical against poisoned enemies.
Hurricane Fang: Weapon Skill. The user spins wildly with their weapon, tearing apart enemies in an area around them.
During Toxic Blades, this skill’s Cooldown is reduced for each Poisoned enemy it strikes.
During Flashing Blades, this skill inflicts Blind.
During Rejuvenating Blades, this skill grants the user the Endure effect for a short time.
During Fatal Blades, the skill is guaranteed to be Critical against poisoned enemies.

Final Fang: Weapon Skill. Delivers a final, fatal blow to a single target, consuming their Poison and Deadly Poison Statuses to deal incredible damage. If the target is not suffering from Poison or Deadly Poison, the skill deals half damage.
During Toxic Blades, the target’s Poison and Deadly Poison are refreshed instead of consumed.
During Flashing Blades, this skill ignores Defense.
During Rejuvenating Blades, this skill grants the user the Hallucination Walk effect for a short time.
During Fatal Blades, the skill is guaranteed to be Critical against poisoned enemies.

Rogue.x: Rogue is the secondary advancement option for the Thief. While the Assassin turns its efforts towards putting out raw damage supplemented by the Status Effects offered by their Thief roots, the Rogue focuses primarily on putting those Status Effects — and as many others as possible — to good use.

Similar to the Assassin Blade Enchants, Rogues have access to two “Stance” skills: Predatory Instinct and Malicious Instinct. Unlike the Blade Enchants however, the Instincts suffer from a lengthy cooldown, and so most Rogues will find their playstyle dictated by their single Instinct of choice.

Predatory Instinct gives a bonus to the user’s Blind and Vulnerable Potency. It builds into a variety of damage-oriented skills, where the application of statuses like Blind and Vulnerable serve to amplify their final damage, all while keeping the Rogue safe from harm. In addition, the Predatory Instinct Stance gives Rogues a bonus to Dexterity, the primary scaling stat for Predator side skills.

Malicious Instinct is more focused on applying a wide range of statuses, rather than direct damage. Though less consistent than Envenom and Sand Attack, these skills can apply up to a whopping six status effects in a very short time frame. Malicious Instinct also boosts the user’s Luck, the scaling stat for Malicious side skills.

Finally, the Rogue has access to two more defensive skills that mesh equally well with both Instincts. Tunnel drive allows the Rogue to move while hiding, giving them the opportunity to reposition slightly while invulnerable, and also serves to increase Hiding’s duration. Dramatic Exit cuts out the middleman of the equation, combining Hiding and Backslide into a single skill that also leaves behind a nasty surprise for enemies thinking to give chase.
Rogues gain access to the following skills:
Predatory Instinct: Stance. While active, gain bonus Dex, Blind Potency, and Vulnerable Potency.
Disorient: Slashes at a target and vanishes, putting the user in the Hiding state and attempting to inflict the Vulnerable status on the enemy. The chance is doubled if the target is Blind.
Backstab: Snaps behind the target to deliver a lethal blow. Deals additional damage to enemies suffering from the Blind or Vulnerable statuses. This skill can be used from Hiding.

Ambush: Leaps from Hiding to deal damage across a wide area, attempting to inflict the Blind and Vulnerable statuses to all enemies struck. Has a very low cooldown, but requires the Hiding status to be cast.
Malicious Instinct: Stance. While active, gain increased Luck, and Bleeding, Burning, and Poison damage are increased.
Intimidate: Deals a swift blow that inflicts minor damage, but has a chance to inflict the Poison, Bleeding, and Burning statuses. The chance for each status is rolled separately.
Debilitate: Deals a swift blow that inflicts minor damage, but has a chance to inflict the Blind, Slow, and Vulnerable statuses. The chance for each status is rolled separately.
Eliminate: Delivers a swift and deadly blow to the target, inflicting heavy damage that is amplified for each negative status the target is suffering from.
Tunnel Drive: Passive. Allows movement while hidden, and slightly increases the duration of Thief’s Hiding skill.
Dramatic Exit: The user backslides and enters Hiding, leaving behind a clone that explodes after a short duration to deal minor damage to all enemies in the area.

Stalker.x: Stalker is the primary advancement option for Rogues. Stalkers perfect the quick and dirty fighting style of the Rogue, either capitalizing on Blind and Vulnerable to cripple their opponent’s offenses and defenses, or dealing out a large number of damage statuses in quick succession to keep their foes reeling.

The first branch of Stalker skills are designed to pair with Rogue’s Predatory Instinct. They quickly and efficiently deal out Vulnerable, Blind, and sometimes even Bleeding, and gain a new version of Ambush that allows the user to use Ambush without hiding for a short duration. The tree is capped by Fate Sealer, a powerful single target skill that can be used flexibly to either soften up a hard target, or finish off a weakened one.

The second branch of skills takes advantage of Malicious Instinct. These skills are designed to rapidly inflict Bleeding, Burning, and Poison to large numbers of enemies simultaneously. These skills both take advantage of the user’s bonuses to their associated Status, while also becoming more efficient as other statuses are applied to their enemies. The tree finishes with Annihilate, a companion skill to Rogue’s Eliminate that focuses entirely on Bleeding, Burning, and Poison.

Together with both of these branches, Stalkers gain access to two utility skills that work equally well with either. Stalker’s Instinct gives the user an incredibly powerful Cooldown Reduction effect that applies to all skills they use, but ends early if the user takes damage. Lightning Reflexes allows the user to react defensively to attacks, blocking any type of Physical skill, then granting the user a bonus tailored to their specific fighting style, allowing them to extend the active duration of Stalker’s Instinct.
Skills:

Stalker’s Instinct: The user hones their instincts for dirty fighting, taking every battlefield advantage they can and leaving their opponents no opportunity to fight back. For a short duration, the cooldowns of all other skills are massively reduced. If the user takes damage from any skill, the status ends early. This effect DOES stack with other Rogue Instincts.

Lightning Reflexes: The user responds instantly to an incoming attack, preventing the damage and taking advantage of the enemy’s now misdirected momentum. Blocks a single Physical Skill against the user. If a skill is successfully blocked, the user gains a different benefit based on which level of this skill was cast.
Level 1: Increased Movement Speed for a short time.
Level 2: Inflicts Blind on the enemy. Deft Stab and Ricochet Knife are refreshed.
Level 3: Inflicts Vulnerable on the enemy. Blindside and Scorpion Lash are refreshed.
Level 4: The user enters Cloaking. Breakout and Firecracker are refreshed.
Level 5: The Cooldown of Stalker’s Instinct is reduced by 10 seconds.

Deft Stab: The user delivers a quick, distracting jab to the enemy. If the target is already Blind, inflicts Vulnerable. If the target is already Vulnerable, inflicts Bleeding. If the target is already Bleeding, inflicts Blind.
Blindside: The user dashes to a distant target, hitting them with a surprise attack that has a chance to leave the target Blind.

Breakout: The user jumps out from hiding, striking all enemies around them. For two seconds after this skill is cast, the user can cast Ambush as if they were in Hiding. Requires the Hiding or Cloaking status.

Fate Sealer: The user delivers a whirling strike to the target, dealing massive damage that has additional properties based on the target’s HP. If the target is above half health, the skill inflicts Blind and Vulnerable and has its cooldown reduced. If they are below half HP, it deals double damage instead.

Ricochet Knife: The user hurls a throwing knife at the target, which then ricochets between them and all enemies in the area around them. All enemies struck are inflicted with the Bleeding Status. For each Burning target struck, the Cooldown of this skill is reduced by 1 second. The damage of this skill is treated as Bleeding Damage.

Scorpion Lash: The user lashes out around them with a venom-tipped knife, damaging and inflicting the Poison Status on all enemies in an area around them. For each Bleeding target struck, the Cooldown of this skill is reduced by 1 second. The damage of this skill is treated as Poison Status damage.

Firecracker: The user throws a handful of gunpowder into the air around them, which ignites and explodes after a short delay. All enemies around the user take Fire Property Physical damage and receive the Burning Status. For each target struck that is suffering from Poison, the cooldown of this skill is reduced by 1 second. The damage of this skill is treated as Burning Damage.

Annihilate: Delivers a savage blow to a single enemy, dealing exceptional damage. If the target is suffering from Bleeding, Burning, or Poison, consumes those statuses to inflict additional damage and reduce this skill’s Cooldown. If all three statuses are consumed, additionally inflicts the Stun status.

Shadow Chaser.x: The Shadow Chaser is the alternative advancement option for Rogues.

The Shadow Chaser focuses primarily on enhancing the Malicious side of the Rogue skill tree. Their new skills manipulate status effects to gain exceptional advantages in combat - primarily by the way of capitalizing on those status effects to do exceptional damage.

The first branch of Shadow Chaser skills focus on status application. These skills are guaranteed to apply their given effects - Bleeding, Burning, and Poison - even at level 1, but come with a significant drawback of inflicting the same status on the user at the same time. But even that is part of the Shadow Chaser’s plan, turning those self-inflicted statuses into either recovery or even more damage.

The second branch is less direct, a series of Mark skills. Again, there is one for each damaging status. If used on an enemy that is healthy, it will inflict the given status immediately. But if the enemy is already suffering from the given status, it will instead cause the mark to explode, spreading the damage of that status to all enemies in the area around the target.

Both of these branches operate to give the Shadow Chaser a high risk, high reward playstyle, capitalizing on the extreme survivability of the Rogue class before them to capitalize on this new territory available to them.

Needle Burst: Unleashes a burst of razor sharp needles, dealing damage that is treated as Bleeding damage and inflicting the Bleeding status on both the target and the user. If the target is Burning or Poisoned, this skill repeats an additional time for each at half damage.

Scalding Blade: Delivers a searing strike to the enemy, dealing damage that is treated as Burning damage and inflicting the Burning status on both the target and the user. Reduces the active cooldown of Chaser’s Respite for each of Bleeding and Poison that the target is suffering from.

Plague Touch: The user cloaks themselves in noxious fumes before striking the target, dealing damage that is treated as Poison damage and inflicting the Poison status on both the target and the user. If the target is Burning or Bleeding, the intensity and duration of those statuses are increased.

Malicious Reprisal: The user delivers a retaliatory strike against all enemies in the area around them, inflicting exceptional Physical damage. For each of Bleeding, Burning, and Poison the user is suffering from, those statuses are consumed to amplify the damage dealt and inflict those statuses on all targets struck.

Bloodletter’s Mark: The user draws a cursed mark on the target, inflaming their Bleeding status. If the target is not Bleeding, inflicts the Bleeding status. If they are, the mark ignites to deal Bleeding Damage to all enemies around the target, including the target themselves, every second.

Arsonist’s Mark: The user draws a cursed mark on the target, inflaming their Burning status. If the target is not Burning, inflicts the Burning status. If they are, the mark ignites to deal Burning Damage to all enemies around the target, including the target themselves, every second.

Noxious Mark: The user draws a cursed mark on the target, inflaming their Poison status. If the target is not Poisoned, inflicts the Poison status. If they are, the mark ignites to deal Poison Damage to all enemies around the target, including the target themselves, every second.

Maelstrom: The user draws a cursed mark on the target, creating a storm of negative energy around them that constantly inflicts negative statuses on them and all enemies in the area. Enemies struck are randomly inflicted with Bleeding, Burning, Poison, Blind, Slow, and Vulnerable every second.
Chaser’s Respite: The user refreshes themselves, removing Bleeding, Burning, and Poison from themselves. For each status removed, the user restores a small amount of HP.

Chaser’s Instinct: The user hones and sharpens their instincts, maximizing their ability to debilitate and disable enemies. While active, Intimidate, Debilitate, Disorient, and Ambush inflict their statuses at 100% chance, regardless of level, and all Shadow Chaser skills inflict additional Status Effects. This skill DOES stack with other Rogue Instincts.

Mage.x: Mage occupies a similar role to the Archer, but shoulders more risk while gunning for a higher reward. The Mage has access to a suite of high damage Bolts of varying elements, allowing them to capitalize on enemy weaknesses where other classes are forced to deal Neutral damage, coupled with a host of AoE skills that can inflict various status effects to multiple enemies simultaneously. This gives them unparalleled control over the battlefield, all while dealing huge amounts of damage.

This control is absolutely necessary for Mages, though, as their small HP pool and weak defensive options cause them to quickly fold under any sort of pressure. Encounters against multiple, ranged, or particularly fast enemies quickly put them on the backfoot, as their long cast times steal much of the mobility away that Archers enjoy.
Mages rely on three key status effects: Burn, Chill, and Sleep.

Burn follows the same pattern as Bleeding and Poison. It deals a steady stream of damage based on the user’s Int, scaling up with their Base Level. This gives Mages the ability of putting out strong, consistent damage even when stopping to throw Bolts isn’t an option.
Chill follows in the same vein as Slow. It reduces the victim’s movement speed, though not quite as drastically as Slow does.
Sleep carries on the traditions of Stun. It totally incapacitates an enemy for a brief duration, rendering them unable to act and reducing their Flee to zero, at least until they take another hit.
Mages cap at job level 50, giving them 50 skill points to invest in the following skills:
Magical Attunement: Restores SP for the user while they are not moving, reduces the SP cost of all skills, and increases the effectiveness of consumables that restore SP.
Fire Bolt: Deals heavy fire element damage to a single target, which is increased if the target is Burning.
Fire Ball: Does minor fire damage to an area, with a high chance of inflicting the Burning status on all targets struck.
Cold Bolt: Deals heavy water element damage to a single target, which is increased if the target is Chilled.
Frost Blast: Deals minor water element damage to an area, with a high chance of inflicting the Chilled status on all targets struck.
Lightning Bolt: Deals heavy wind element damage to a single target, which is increased if the target is Sleeping.
Static Burst: Deals minor wind element damage to an area, with a high chance of inflicting the Sleep status on all targets struck.

Wizard.x: Wizard is the primary advancement option for the Mage.

Upon advancing to this class, Wizards will find they suffer from much the same problem that they did as Mages: there are far too many skills. With twelve skills to allocate points into and only 50 job levels available, the first decision most Wizards will find themselves having to make is “which element am I willing to focus on?”

The Wizard skill tree is divided into six branches. The first three branches, for Fire, Water, and Wind skills, are divided between a setup and finisher skill. Each setup skill inflicts an elemental vulnerability on the target, enhancing all damage of that element the target takes from any source. The second skill is a large AoE that deals heavy damage and inflicts that element’s associated status effect.

The next two branches are a bit more unique, playing catch-up with the “status effect > bolt” playstyle of the Mage skills. The Earth branch uses Heaven’s Drive to inflict the Bleeding status over an area, while Earth Spike deals increased damage to Bleeding enemies. Meanwhile, the Neutral tree offers Gravitational Collapse to slow enemies and inflict the Vulnerable status, while Force Pulse deals increased damage to Vulnerable enemies—a pair of effects you might find odd, until you learn both skills inflict Physical damage based on the user’s Magic Attack.

The last branch of Wizard skills consists of a pair of Utility skills. Energy Coat returns from days of yore, providing a powerful damage reduction effect based on the user’s remaining SP, but draining SP every time the user takes damage. Paired with it is Rapid Incantation, a short buff that removes the Fixed Cast Time of all spells cast for a short duration.
Wizards gain access to the following skills:
Cloak of Flame: The user wraps themselves in flame, dealing Fire property damage to all enemies that approach within a 5x5 area. Enemies struck suffer from Fire Vulnerability for ten seconds.
Crimson Rock: Calls a flaming meteor from the heavens to deal heavy Fire property damage and inflict the Burning status to a target and all enemies around it.
Freezing Breath: Unleashes a blast of cold air at a target location, dealing Water property damage and attempting to inflict the Chilled and Water Vulnerability statuses.
Storm Gust: Summons a wintry storm at the targeted location, dealing repeated Water property damage with a chance to inflict the Chilled status each time.
Jupitel Thunder: Fires a ball of lightning at a target, knocking them back and inflicting the Wind Vulnerability status for ten seconds. Sleeping enemies take additional damage.
Lord of Vermillion: Summons a barrage of lightning bolts that does significant damage and possibly inflicts the Sleep status on all targets over a huge area.
Earth Spike: Deals Earth property damage to a single target, which is increased if the target is Bleeding.
Heaven’s Drive: Deals Earth property damage to targets over a small area, with a high chance to inflict the Bleeding status. Bleeding inflicted by this skill scales with Dex instead of Str.

Force Pulse: Deals Neutral Physical damage to a single target, which is increased if the target is Vulnerable. This skill takes its damage from the user’s Magic Attack, but is only reduced by Physical Defense.

Gravitational Collapse: Deals Neutral Physical damage to targets over a small area, attempting to inflict the Vulnerable status with each hit. Enemies within the area of effect are slowed, though this does not count as the Slow status effect. This skill takes its damage from the user’s Magic Attack, but is only reduced by Physical Defense.

Energy Coat: The user creates a magic forcefield around themselves, reducing the damage of all incoming attacks by a percentage based on the amount of SP they have remaining. Each hit taken under this status drains a percentage of the user’s Max SP.
Rapid Incantation: For five seconds, all spells cast by the user have their Variable Cast Time halved.

High Wizard.x: High Wizard is the primary advancement option for Wizards. It continues to excel at what the Wizard does best - dish out huge amounts of elemental damage over a wide area.

The High Wizard turns back to its roots, focusing on the four natural elements with its magic, leaving the more esoteric magics to the Warlock. Their skills divide into the four branches you would expect: fire, water, wind, and earth magic.

Each branch comes with two skills. A major skill, dealing a large amount of damage over a wide area, and a minor skill, dealing damage over a much smaller area. The major skills each grant the user an Elemental Affinity, which boosts the effects of all magic used of the same element, even enhancing their Mage and Wizard skills. The minor skills all gain powerful additional effects while their appropriate Affinity is active, and also serve to reset the duration of that Affinity.

Affinities serve two powerful functions. The first is its enhancement to all elemental magic that matches it: while an Affinity is active, all magic of that element gains an enormous bonus to its Magic Defense Pierce. In addition, the Affinities alter the behavior of the remaining two High Wizard skills that sit outside the elemental branches.

Mystical Amplification increases the user’s Magic Attack for a single cast, at the cost of also increasing that skill’s Fixed Cast Time. If an Affinity is active, it is consumed to grant an additional bonus that lasts much longer depending on which Affinity was consumed.

The final High Wizard Skill is Elemental Annihilation, a massive nuke that deals incredible damage of all elements across four waves to the target and all enemies immediately around them. Usually this skill deals damage in the order of Fire, Water, Wind, and then Earth, but if any Affinity is active, it instead deals four waves of that particular element instead.
Skills:

Affinities: Affinities come in the four natural elements, Fire, Water, Wind, or Earth. While an Affinity is active, all magic that matches its element gains additional Magic Defense Pierce. Only one Affinity can be active at a time.

Crimson Arrow: The user fires a bolt of concentrated Fire Magic, striking all targets in a straight line. Any target struck that is Burning takes additional damage, otherwise it attempts to inflict the Burning Status. If Fire Affinity is active, its duration is reset and the damage is treated as Burning Damage.

Volcanic Burst: The user causes a burst of blazing magical energy to erupt beneath their target’s feet, dealing Fire damage to them and all enemies around them. This skill deals additional damage to Burning enemies and applies the Fire Affinity status on the user.

Frozen Grip: The user summons spikes of ice at the target’s location, dealing Water property damage to them and all enemies nearby. If this skill strikes a Chilled target, it deals additional damage. Otherwise, it attempts to inflict the Chilled status. If Water Affinity is active, its duration is reset and this skill has a chance to Freeze.

Frost Nova: The user unleashes a blast of freezing magic around themselves, dealing Water Property damage to all enemies in an area around them. This skill deals additional damage to Chilled enemies, and applies the Water Affinity status on the user.

Chain Lightning: Invokes a burst of lightning on the target, dealing Wind Property damage before repeating against another nearby target. The number of bounces is affected by the level of the skill. If there are no other targets in the area, the same target can be struck multiple times. This skill deals additional damage to Sleeping and Dazed enemies. If Wind Affinity is active, its duration is reset and this skill gains additional bounces.

Static Storm: Creates an electrically charged zone that is struck repeatedly by lightning bolts, dealing rapid Wind Property damage over time to all enemies within it. This skill deals additional damage to Sleeping and Dazed targets, and applies the Wind Affinity Status on the user.

Stone Crush: Summons an enormous stone sphere and drops it on the target’s location, dealing Earth Property damage to them and all enemies around them. Deals additional damage to Bleeding enemies, otherwise has a chance to inflict Internal Bleeding. If Earth Affinity is active, its duration is reset and the damage is treated as Bleeding damage.

Seismic Tremor: Infuses magic into the ground at the target location, causing it to tremor and deal Earth Property damage to all enemies above it. This skill deals additional damage to Bleeding enemies, and applies the Earth Affinity status on the user.

Mystic Amplification: The user infuses their staff with incredible magical energies, amplifying the effects of their next spell. For a single skill cast, the user’s Magic Attack is massively increased, but so is its Fixed Cast Time. If the user is under any Elemental Affinity when this skill is cast, it is consumed to grant and additional buff for thirty seconds:
Fire: Burning Damage increased by 30%
Water: All skills have a chance to inflict Freeze
Wind: All skills have a chance to inflict Sleep
Earth: Bleeding Damage increased by 30%
This skill does not stack with Rapid Incantation.

Elemental Annihilation: The user channels a massive blast of elemental energy, obliterating a single target and all enemies nearby. Attacks in four waves, in the order of Fire, Water, Wind, Earth. If the user has an Elemental Affinity active, all four waves will match that element instead.

Warlock.x: Warlock is the alternative advancement option for Wizards. While their previous job provided them mastery over all of the natural elements, the Warlock is not satisfied with this, and so turns its efforts toward much darker magics. Though not without cost, the Warlock has managed to chain these supernatural forces down, bending them to their will, giving them unique access to Dark and Undead property magic, and they join Soul Linkers in gaining access to Ghost property magic.

The Warlock skill tree is dominated by two primary skills: Void Infusion and Void Channeling. Void Infusion grants the user a buff that alters the property of all magic they use to the property of their choice, either Dark, Undead, or Ghost. This unique ability comes at a price though, saddling the Warlock with a significant weakness based on which property is chosen.

Void Channeling allows the user to convert their HP into magical power. By consuming a large amount of Max HP, they instantly generate a number of Void Spheres, a unique resource used to empower other Warlock skills.

These two skills work in conjunction with three minor branches of the skill tree. The first are the Phantasmal Skills, Ghost Property spells that operate around the use of the Breach status. And for good reason: setting the user’s Void Infusion to Ghost property reduces their Magic Defense Pierce to zero, meaning Breach will be the only way for them to deal with high MDef enemies.

The second branch are the Death skills, dealing Undead property damage while absorbing the target’s HP to heal the user. As you might expect, this is also needed, as setting one’s Void Infusion to Undead property causes them to lose HP over time.

The final branch are the Abyssal skills, Dark property attacks that interact heavily with the Burning status. In addition to being uniquely positioned to handle Holy property enemies, the Abyssal skills also boast the highest raw damage of any of the Warlock branches. These benefits come at the cost of enormous SP Costs, together with the Void Infusion drawback of reduced SP Regeneration. The Abyssal skills offset this demerit by generating SP for the user as they are used.
Skills:
Void Infusion: Converts all magic damage dealt by the user to the specified element. Each element has its own associated demerit.
Ghost: The user’s Magic Pierce is reduced to 0
Undead: The user loses 5% of their Max HP every 5 seconds
Dark: The user’s SP Regen is halved

Void Channeling: The user consumes a portion of their Max HP to channel the power of the void, condensing it into spheres that can be used as a resource to empower other skills. The user can hold a maximum of five Void Spheres at once, regardless of whether they have learned this skill or not.

Phantasmal Burst: Invokes forbidden magic to turn the target’s soul against their own body, dealing Ghost property damage and inflicting the Breach status. Has a small chance to summon a Void Sphere when cast. If Void Infusion: Ghost is active, the chance is doubled.

Phantasmal Crush: Invokes forbidden magic to deal damage directly to the souls of all enemies in a given area, attempting to inflict the Breach Status on them. Deals additional damage based on the number of Void Spheres the user has.
If Void Infusion: Ghost is active, this skill’s cooldown is halved.

Phantasmal Burden: Puts a supernatural burden on the souls of the target and all enemies in the area around them. Consumes the user’s remaining Void Spheres to deal Ghost Property damage over time to all enemies around the target. The damage of this skill is increased by the user’s Breach Potency.
If Void Infusion: Ghost is active, this skill’s Fixed Cast Time is removed.

Death Eater: The user channels necrotic energy to sap the life from the targeted enemy. Deals Undead Property Magic damage to a single target, then heals the user for an amount based on how much HP the target is missing. If the target is killed by the attack, heals for the maximum amount instead. Each cast has a small chance to summon a Void Sphere.
If Void Infusion: Undead is active, the chance to summon a Void Sphere is doubled.

Death Circle: The user infuses necrotic energies into the ground, creating a zone of desecrated land. Deals Undead property Magic damage to all enemies in the area over time for a short duration. This skill gains a small amount of lifesteal based on the user’s number of remaining Void Spheres.
If Void Infusion: Undead is active, this skill’s cooldown is halved.

Grasping Death: The user opens a gate to the netherworld, letting necrotic energies pour through into the world of the living. Consumes all of the user’s Void Spheres to open a portal on all enemies within range, dealing Undead Property Magic damage to them over time. The user is healed for a small amount for each Void Sphere consumed.
If Void Infusion: Death is active, this skill’s Fixed Cast Time is removed.

Abyssal Flare: Unleashes a burst of dark magic laced with fire, incinerating the target with corrupting energies. Deals Dark property Magic damage with a chance to inflict the Burning status. If the target is already Burning, the user restores a small amount of SP. Each cast has a small chance to summon a Void Sphere.
If Void Infusion: Dark is active, the chance to summon a Void Sphere is doubled.

Abyssal Burst: Unleashes a wave of corrupting energy around the user, dealing Dark Property Magic damage to all enemies in the area. Has a chance to inflict Burning on each enemy struck. The user also restores a fixed amount of SP based on the number of Void Spheres they have remaining.
If Void Infusion: Dark is active, this skill’s cooldown is halved.

Abyssal Comet: Drops a comet from the Abyss on the targeted enemy, consuming all of the user’s remaining Void Spheres to deal massive Dark Property Magic damage to all enemies in a wide area and inflict the Burning status. The user restores a percentage of their Max SP for each Void Sphere consumed.
If Void Infusion: Dark is active, this skill’s Fixed Cast Time is removed.

Sage.x: Sage is the secondary advancement option for Mages. While the Wizard focuses mainly on turning the control options of Mage into large amounts of damage, the Sage doubles down on the control aspect of their first job, using their new skills to further restrict their enemies’ movements, all while dealing consistent damage over a wide area.

The Sage builds on its first three elemental skill choices with two new skills each: one to enhance their movement or restrict the movement of enemies, and another that places a large ground-based AoE that deals constant damage over time to all enemies standing within it. Beyond this, the Sage must leverage its first job options to put out competitive amounts of damage.

But damage is not all the Sage offers. It also has access to a plethora of support and utility skills. Endow Weapon gives party members a chance to swap their element without having to rely on costly high-end cards, while also buffing the magic damage of that element used by magic users. Endow Armor does the opposite, giving high levels of resistance to a given element at the cost of reduced resistance from its opposite. Both skills require a catalyst crafted at the Sage Castle to be used to their full effect, but when used without one, can also serve to protect party members from enemies maliciously attempting to change their weapon and armor elements.

More selfishly, the Sage has access to Transposition Spell, a simple ability that allows them to teleport to any location within line of sight, and Spell Eater, a defensive skill that entirely nullifies single-target magic aimed at them. When successful, the user gains a buff that enables them to cast their next spell instantly, ignoring both Variable and Fixed Cast Times.

Finally, the Sage has access to Antimagic Field, a powerful land spell that gives a mind-boggling amount of magic resistance to anyone who stands on it, in addition to conferring immunity to the Burning, Chilled, and Sleep statuses. However, the key is anyone. Both enemies and allies alike will enjoy the bonuses that the field provides, forcing the Sage to be very careful about their positioning to make good use of the skill without neutering their own damage output.
Sages gain access to the following skills:
Elemental Mastery: Passive. Increases the damage dealt and reduces the damage received from attacks of the Fire, Water, Wind, and Earth properties.
Fire Wall: Creates a wall of fire that will inflict minor damage and knock back enemies trying to pass through it. Each hit has a chance of inflicting the Burning status.
Inferno: Summons a blazing inferno at the targeted location, dealing Fire property damage over time to all enemies within. The damage is increased if the target is Burning.

Chilling Frost: Creates a blast of cold air at the targeted location, dealing minor Water property damage and attempting to Chill all enemies in a wide area. Enemies that are already Chilled have a chance of being Frozen.
Deluge: Summons a raging torrent at the targeted location, dealing Water property damage over time to all enemies within. The damage is increased if the target is Chilled.
Tailwind: Calls an enchanted wind to follow the party, increasing all party members’ Movement Speed and Flee for the duration.
Whirlwind: Summons a fierce gale at the targeted location, dealing Wind property damage over time to enemies within. The damage is increased if the caster is under the Tailwind status.
Transposition Spell: Instantly teleports the user to the targeted location. The user must have an unobstructed line of sight to the target or the skill will fail.

Spell Eater: For two seconds, the user enters a defensive stance that will nullify all single-target magic aimed at them. If this skill successfully nullifies a spell, the user regenerates a small amount of SP, and the next spell they cast will be instant.

Antimagic Field: Creates a null zone of magic, massively reducing the magic damage taken by all allies and enemies standing inside. Affected targets will also be immune to the Burning, Chilled, and Sleep statuses.

Endow Weapon: Endows the target’s weapon with one of the natural elements, making all physical attacks take that element and increasing the damage of magic of the same. Requires a catalyst crafted at the Sage Castle in Juno to be used above level 1. At level 1, the spell gives a “Neutral Endow,” forcing the target’s weapon to be Neutral property and blocking all other attempts at changing their weapon property for the duration.

Endow Armor: Endows the target’s armor with one of the natural elements, reducing all damage they take from that element considerably, but also increasing the damage they take of its opposite. Requires a catalyst crafted at the Sage Castle in Juno to be used above level 1. At level 1, the spell gives a “Neutral Endow,” forcing the target’s armor to be Neutral property and blocking all other attempts at changing their armor property for the duration.

Scholar.x: Scholar is the primary advancement option for the Sage. Similar to the Warlock, Scholars are those who have contented themselves with their mastery over the natural elements and so have turned their attention to other forces. But while the Warlock sought out the sinister powers of the Void, Scholars instead turn their efforts on the fundamental laws that make up magic itself.

The primary driving force behind all magic is SP, but the domain of the Scholar lies in turning this passive fuel into a potent weapon in its own right. Virtually all Scholar skills gain benefits from the precise amount of SP the user has at their disposal, either increasing the damage of their offensive skills or enhancing the effects of their supportive ones.

Similar to the Sage before them, Scholars have a suite of offensive skills, but most of their skill points are focused on supportive and utility abilities. These skills are capable of everything from creating magic shields to protect allies, to reducing the SP costs of their allies’ abilities, to even accelerating time itself to reduce the Cooldowns of all of their allies’ abilities.

But their offensive skills are not to be overlooked either. Each of these skills has its damage tied directly to the user’s remaining SP: while over half of max SP, each will deal increased damage in proportion to how much is left, but if below half, they will deal reduced damage based on how much SP is missing. This compounds with elemental bonuses, as all Scholar skills, while Neutral by default, will adopt the element of whatever weapon endow the user has active.
With a final collection of skills to manipulate their own SP, the Scholar is perfectly positioned to turn that ubiquitous resource into an overwhelming advantage on the battlefield.
Free Cast: Enables the user to walk and attack at reduced speed while casting spells. The penalty to Movement and Attack Speed is reduced at higher levels of the skill.

Soul Siphon: The user connects their soul to that of the targeted foe, directly siphoning their magical energy. The user regenerates a fixed amount of SP based on the Current HP of the target, and the target is inflicted with the Breach Status.

Time Shift: The user uses their ultimate mastery over the inner workings of the world to shift time forward for their party. Immediately reduces the active Cooldowns of all party members by a certain amount based on skill level. This skill can never benefit from Cooldown Reduction or effects that reduce active Cooldowns.
Indulge: The user consumes a portion of their HP, converting it into SP. The amount of HP consumed is determined by skill level.

Soul Infusion: The user infuses a targeted ally with arcane magics, fuelling their skills for a short duration. For a set number of skills, the SP cost of the targeted ally’s abilities are massively reduced.

Psychic Barrier: The user creates a barrier of pure magical force, consuming a fixed percentage of their remaining SP to protect themselves and their party members from all damage for a short duration. The barrier’s HP is based on the amount of SP consumed.

Soul Burn: The user attacks the target with a burst of raw magical energy which ignites on contact. Deals Neutral property Magic damage. If the target is Breached, has a chance to inflict Severe Burning. The damage of this skill is heavily influenced by the user’s remaining SP.

Force Barrage: The user unleashes a barrage of psychic energy, dealing Neutral property Magic damage to the targeted enemy and all other enemies in the area. The damage is increased against any targets suffering from the Breach status. The damage of this skill is heavily influenced by the user’s remaining SP.

Psychic Storm: The user unleashes a storm of raw magical energy at the targeted location, dealing persistent Neutral Property Magic damage over time to all enemies within. Each hit has a chance to inflict the Breach status. The damage of this skill is heavily influenced by the user’s remaining SP.

Force Sigil: The user inscribes an arcane sigil on the ground that channels incredible raw magic. For the duration, the sigil immobilizes the caster and all enemies within it, dealing constant Neutral Property Magic damage over time to all enemies. The damage dealt is heavily influenced by the user’s remaining SP.

Sorcerer.x: Sorcerer is the alternative advancement option for Sages. While the Scholar focuses its efforts on learning about and leveraging the unique attributes of magic itself, the Sorcerer turns their focus toward the four elemental attributes, manipulating them with control and precision that even the most powerful Wizards would be jealous of.

The core of the Sorcerer’s kit revolves around their ability to summon Elemental Spirits. Summoning an elemental spirit has two main benefits. The first is that all magic used that matches the summoned Elemental will gain additional Magic Defense Pierce, in exchange for reducing the user’s Resistance to the opposite. For example, summoning Ardor, the spirit of fire, will increase the Magic Pierce of all Fire property skills, but reduce the user’s Water Property Resistance.

The more important aspect of these summoned elementals is the actions they take. Elementals do not attack or use skills of their own accord, and will not be attacked by monsters. Instead, they react to the skills cast by their summoner. When their summoner casts an offensive Sorcerer skill - of any element - the summoned elemental will echo it with an attack of their own. When the Sorcerer uses a supportive skill, the elemental will use their own support skill.

Naturally, this means that each summoned elemental comes with a pair of elemental skills. The first is focused on dealing direct damage, while the second has more of a utility effect. These skills not only serve to trigger the summoned elemental’s skills, but also gain bonuses themselves based on the user’s own bonuses to Summoned Entity attributes.

These abilities, together with the latent abilities of the summoned elementals and the Sorcerers inherited skills from Mage and Sage serve to create a class with great damage and utility, together with the flexibility to match any situation they find themselves in.

Summon Ardor: Summons Ardor, the spirit of indomitable fire, to aid in combat. While summoned, the user’s Fire Property magic gains additional Magic Defense Pierce, but the user’s Water Resistance is reduced. Only one Elemental Spirit can be summoned at a time.

Agni’s Wrath: The user calls on Agni, spirit of flame, to incinerate their foes. Deals a burst of Fire Property damage to the target and all enemies around them. The damage of this skill is increased by the user’s bonuses to Summoned Entity damage, and triggers the user’s Summoned Elemental to use its Offensive ability. This skill’s Cooldown is halved if Ardor is present.

Agni’s Heat: The user calls on Agni, the spirit of flame, to infuse the targeted area with unnatural heat. For a short duration, all enemies that enter the targeted area take damage over time. The damage is based on the user’s Burning Damage, but does not count as the actual Burning Status. The damage is further increased by the user’s bonuses to Summoned Entity HP, and triggers the user’s Summoned Elemental to use its Support Skill. This skill’s Cooldown is halved if Ardor is present.

Summon Diluvio: Summons Diluvio, the spirit of the endless ocean depths, to aid in combat. While summoned, the user's Water Property Magic gains additional Magic Defense Pierce, but the user's Wind Resistance is reduced. Only one Elemental Spirit can be summoned at a time.

Aqua’s Breath: Calls on Aqua, the spirit of water, to strike down their foes, creating a blast of frigid snow and ice to strike the targeted area. All enemies in the are take Water Property damage and have a chance to be Chilled. The damage of this skill is increased by the user’s bonuses to Summoned Entity Damage, and triggers the user’s Summoned Elemental to use its Offensive Skill. This skill’s Cooldown is halved if Diluvio is present.

Aqua’s Relief: Calls on Aqua, the spirit of water, to grant relief to their allies. Causes a gentle healing rain to fall around the user, gradually healing all allies within it over time. The amount of healing is increased by the user’s bonuses to Summoned Entity HP, and triggers the user’s Summoned Elemental to use its Support Skill. This skill’s Cooldown is halved if Diluvio is present.

Summon Procella: Summons Procella, the spirit of storm and gale, to aid in combat. While summoned, the user's Wind Property Magic gains additional Magic Defense Pierce, but the user's Earth Resistance is reduced. Only one Elemental Spirit can be summoned at a time.

Ventus’s Gale: Calls on Ventus, the spirit of the wind, to unleash a violent tornado at their foes, dealing damage to all enemies in a straight line. The damage of this skill is increased by the user’s bonuses to Summoned Entity Damage, and triggers the user’s Summoned Elemental to use its Offensive Skill. This skill’s cooldown is halved if Procella is present.

Ventus’s Haste: The user calls on Ventus, the spirit of the wind, to accelerate their party members. For a short duration, all party members have increased Attack Speed and reduced Variable Cast Time. It also triggers the user’s Summoned Elemental to use its Support Skill. This skill’s Cooldown is halved if Procella is present.

Summon Terra Motus: Summons Terra Motus, the spirit of earth and stone, to aid in combat. While summoned, the user's Earth Property Magic gains additional Magic Defense Pierce, but the user's Fire Resistance is reduced. Only one Elemental Spirit can be summoned at a time.

Terra’s Fangs: Call on Terra, spirit of the earth, to create a tremor in the ground at the targeted location. All enemies in the area are struck for Earth Property damage. The damage of this skill is increased by the user’s bonuses to Summoned Entity Damage, and it triggers the user’s Summoned Elemental to use its Offensive Skill. This skill’s Cooldown is halved if Terra Motus is present.

Terra’s Shield: Calls on Terra, spirit of the earth, to protect all of the user’s party members. Each party member receives a shield that absorbs half of the damage they would take from all Physical and Magical damage. The shield ends after a set duration or after it has absorbed a certain amount of damage. The shield’s HP is increased by the user’s Barrier Potency and by the user’s bonuses to Summoned Entity HP. It also triggers the user’s Summoned Elemental to use its Support Skill. This skill’s Cooldown is halved if Terra Motus is present.

Archer.x: The Archer fills both a damage and offensive support role. With extended range from their bows, they are able to engage enemies from a safe distance and put out steady damage without needing to worry about taking much damage themselves. They have tools both to slow enemies down and speed up their party members, allowing them to mitigate a great amount of damage for all members of the party.

However, not all enemies are so willing to be kited. Those with ranged skills often prove quite dangerous to Archers, as they have a limited HP pool and no defensive options outside of their mobility. Even when Archers can inflict their damage safely from afar, they often are quite slow to take down enemies, as their standard auto-attacks can’t compare to the damage output of other classes’ skills, while their own SP is often reserved for keeping enemies at bay rather than dealing damage to them.

The Archer has one key status effect: Slow. Slow, very simply, significantly reduces the movement speed of the victim. Since Archers can apply it at range, it’s ideal for keeping enemies away from both themselves and their friends, especially in conjunction with Archer’s knockback skills.
Archers cap at job level 50, giving them 50 skill points to invest in the following skills:
Bow Mastery: Increases the auto-attack range and Hit Rate of Bows. Notably, this skill does not increase the range of skills, and does not improve the damage of bows.
Double Strafe: Deals two hits in rapid succession to a ranged target. This skill gains bonus Crit Rate when hitting a Slowed target.
Arrow Shower: Deals splash damage at a target location, knocking back any enemies struck.
Pin Down: Fires an arrow at a target’s legs, dealing minor damage and attempting to inflict the Slow status.
Arrow Repel: Fires a heavy arrow at the target, dealing minor damage and knocking them backwards.
Reposition: Commands the party to move, greatly increasing their movement speed for a short duration and removing most movement impairing effects.

Hunter.x: Hunter is the primary advancement option for the Archer class. It fills much the same role, attempting to finish off enemies from range, but now has a few more tools to aid in the process.

The Hunter skill tree is broadly divided into three branches. The first is the Marksmanship branch, characterized by a number of skills with primarily Variable Cast Times. The first skill is Precision Shot, a skill dealing moderate damage which deals additional damage if the target is Slowed. To aid in this, the next skill is Threefold Arrow, a skill that fires in three modes, either applying Slow, Vulnerable, or Stun, depending on which the target is already suffering from. These skills are supplemented with the self buff Marksman’s Focus, a skill that gives a reasonable increase to Hit and Crit for the user.

The second branch consists of Trap skills, Toxic Mine, Shrapnel Mine, and Incendiary Mine, all doing exactly what you’d expect: inflicting Poison, Bleeding, and Burning respectively. In exchange for this huge range of status effects, the traps come with a glaring weakness — each of them sports a colossal Fixed Cast Time, forcing the Hunter to set up traps before combat to realistically use them, unless they also invest in the companion skill, Trapper’s Focus. This buff not only removes the Fixed Cast Time of all Traps, it also extends the duration of the Statuses inflicted by the three trap skills, allowing potentially full up time on all three.

The final branch is the one you’ve all been waiting for, the Falcon skills. These skills are designed to enhance the other two branches. Blitz Beat, while retaining its autocasting nature, can still be force cast, and in either case will attempt to inflict the Slow status on all enemies affected. Those suffering from Bleeding, Burning, or Poison will have a much greater chance of being Slowed. Paired with it is Aggravating Assault, a skill which does heavy damage to targets suffering from the Slowed status, while also extending the duration of Bleeding, Burning, and Poison on them. This unique pairing of attributes allows the Falcon skills to both support each other and the other two Hunter branches.
Hunters gain access to the following skills:
Marksman’s Focus: Self buff. Increases Hit and Crit Rate. Does not stack with Trapper’s Focus.
Precision Shot: Takes careful aim at a target before firing, dealing significant damage that is increased against Slowed enemies.

Threefold Arrow: Three part skill. Initially attempts to inflict Slow. If the target is already Slowed, instead attempts to inflict Vulnerable. If the target is already Vulnerable, instead attempts to inflict Stun.
Trapper’s Focus: Self buff. Removes the Fixed Cast Time of Trap skills, and increases the duration of statuses they inflict. Does not stack with Marksman’s Focus.

Toxic Mine: Sets a trap that spews a cloud of poisonous gas when triggered. Deals damage scaling with the user’s Agi, and inflicts the Poison status on all enemies in a 5x5 area. This skill has an extremely long Fixed Cast Time.

Shrapnel Mine: Sets a trap that explodes in a cloud of shrapnel when triggered. Deals damage scaling with the user’s Dex, and inflicts the Internal Bleeding status on all enemies in a 5x5 area. This skill has an extremely long Fixed Cast Time.

Incendiary Mine: Sets a trap that releases a cloud of burning gas when triggered. Deals damage scaling with the user’s Int, and inflicts the Burning status on all enemies in a 5x5 area. This skill has an extremely long Fixed Cast Time.
Falcon Mastery: Passive. Allows the usage of a Falcon, and increases the damage of all Falcon-related skills.

Blitz Beat: Commands the Falcon to attack enemies in a small area, dealing Defense-ignoring damage that has a chance to Slow. Enemies suffering from Bleeding, Burning, or Poison have an increased chance of being Slowed. This skill has a chance to be autocast with each non-skill attack made with a bow, ignoring its Cooldown.

Aggravating Assault: Commands the Falcon to harass a single enemy, dealing heavy Defense-ignoring damage that is significantly increased if the target is Slowed. If the target is suffering from any of the Bleeding, Burning, or Poison statuses, those statuses have their durations extended by a fixed amount.

Sniper.x: Sniper is the primary advancement option for Hunters. It gives up on the usage of both traps and Falcon skills to perfect the use of the bow, becoming something of a Physical Caster designed to bring down enemies from a safe distance.

The primary mechanic for the Sniper class is Preparation. Using the Sniper opener skills grants Preparation Counters, each of which enhances the damage and reduces the cast time of their finishers, as well as slightly modifies the behavior of the openers themselves. Preparation comes with one important drawback though: any movement the user makes removes all Preparation Counters immediately.

This creates a situation where the Sniper must think carefully before firing off all of their skills. Is a chain of low cooldown openers enough to take the target down without relying on finishers? Can they reliably get the finisher off before mobs reach them and start dealing too much damage to handle? Handling each encounter requires careful planning and precise execution to draw the most out of each skill.

To aid in this, the Sniper also gets access to a number of utility skills. Tactical Retreat allows a single movement without sacrificing Preparation Counters, Sniper’s Resolve provides a massive amount of damage reduction based on the number of Preparation Counters active, and Called Shot maximizes the damage dealt and minimizes the damage taken from a single target chosen by the Sniper.

Sniper is a class that requires careful planning and a high level of execution skill to make the most of, but those that take the time to learn will be rewarded with exceptional damage output at fantastic range.

Sniper’s Resolve: The user steels themselves, determined to keep fighting no matter the odds. For a short time, the user takes reduced damage from all attacks based on the number of Preparation Counters they have. If they already have three Preparation Counters when casting this skill, most damaging Status Effects are removed.

Tactical Retreat: The user instantly jumps to the targeted location, moving them out of harm’s way, then refreshes all active Preparation Counters. If the user already had three Preparation Counters before casting, all enemies around their previous location are also Slowed.

Called Shot: The user marks a target for elimination. While marked, the user deals more damage to them and takes less damage from them, but all attacks against unmarked targets miss. If the user has three Preparation Counters when casting this skill, the marked target is also inflicted with the Vulnerable Status. Otherwise, they gain Preparation Counters.

Shrouding Shot: The user fires an arrow cloaked in dark fog to inhibit the target’s vision. Deals damage to a single target and generates one Preparation Counter. Attempts to inflict the Blind Status, with an increased duration for each Preparation Counter the user has. If the user already had three Preparation Counters, casting this skill refreshes the CD of Hammer Shot.

Hammer Shot: Fires an arrow with tremendous force, keeping the target from reaching the user. Deals Ranged Physical damage to a single target and generates one Preparation Counter, then knocks the target back. The knockback distance is increased for each Preparation Counter the user has. If the user already had three Preparation Counters, this skill refreshes the CD of Razor Shot.

Razor Shot: Fires a serrated arrow at the target, slicing through flesh to cause heavy bleeding. Deals Ranged Physical damage to a single target and generates one Preparation Counter. Attempts to inflict the Internal Bleeding Status, with an increased duration for each Preparation Counter the user has. If the user had three, it refreshes the duration of Piercing Shot.

Piercing Shot: Fires a tapered arrow at the target, intended to pierce through even the toughest armor. Deals Ranged Physical damage to a single target and generates one Preparation Counter. Attempts to inflict the Vulnerable Status, with an increased duration for each Preparation Counter the user has. If the user had three, it refreshes the CD of Shrouding Shot.

Arrow Storm: The user fires a massive barrage of arrows at the target, striking them and all enemies in a wide area around them for tremendous damage. All enemies struck are left Slow and Vulnerable. For each Preparation Counter the user has, the Cast Time of this skill is greatly reduced, and its damage is greatly increased. After casting, all Preparation Counters are lost.

Heaven’s Arrow: The user fires an enormous arrow up into the sky, arcing it to fall on their foes from directly overhead. All enemies struck are Stunned. For each Preparation Counter the user has, the Cast Time of this skill is greatly reduced, and its damage is greatly increased. After casting, all Preparation Counters are lost.

Explosive Barrage: The user fires an arrow strapped with a powerful explosive that detonates on impact, dealing tremendous damage to the target and all enemies around them. All enemies struck are left Blind and Burning. For each Preparation Counter the user has, the Cast Time of this skill is greatly reduced, and its damage is greatly increased. After casting, all Preparation Counters are lost.

Numbing Volley: The user fires a volley of arrows that disperse a potent numbing toxin, dealing damage and inflicting the Sleep status on all enemies in the area. For each Preparation Counter the user has, the Cast Time of this skill is greatly reduced, and its damage is greatly increased. After casting, all Preparation Counters are lost.

Ranger.x: Ranger is the alternative advancement option for Hunters. While it provides some support for Marksman and Falcon builds from the Hunter, it focuses most of its efforts on the trapping style of combat, preferring to best their enemies through careful planning and preparation, creating a battlefield that gives them every advantage possible.

Hawk Rush and Gale Storm provide options for Rangers that prefer to use their bow, granting an additional stream of damage on autoattacks and a wide ranging AoE respectively. They also gain access to Punishing Bolt, a single target ability that does massive damage based on what Statuses the target is suffering from.

However, the core of the job is undoubtedly its trap skills. Advanced Trap Mastery allows the user to set all traps, including previous Hunter traps, at extended ranges. In addition, they gain access to a new set of traps that persistently deal damage over time to all enemies in the area around them, scaling up with the user’s Status Damage.

Finally, Rangers gain access to a suite of skills known as Nature Rituals. Though burdened with extreme cast times, these Rituals massively alter the environment around the user, greatly altering the effectiveness of different elemental properties of both allies and enemies, and granting additional unique effects. The enormous cast times of these Rituals are offset by the core skill, Ritual Mastery, which both decreases the Cast Time of the Rituals and enhances their effects.

Hawk Rush: Commands the falcon in a joint maneuver, ordering to to strike the target while granting the user a short boost boost to their Attack Speed. Whenever the user performs a basic attack with a bow, this skill has a chance to trigger at half damage.

Punishing Bolt: The user fires an arrow to take advantage of the opponent’s Statuses. If the target is suffering from any of Bleeding, Burning, or Poison, they are consumed to amplify the damage dealt.
Gale Storm: The user fires a hail of enchanted arrows, raining them down on a wide area together with a vicious wind. Enemies struck have a chance of being Slowed.
Advanced Trap Mastery: Training in the advanced deployment of traps. Increases the duration of Ranger traps, and increases the range at which all traps can be placed.

Wind Trap: The user sets a persistent trap that deals Wind property damage to all enemies around it at regular intervals. Enemies struck have a chance of being Slowed. The damage of this trap is increased by the user’s Slow Potency.

Flame Trap: The user sets a persistent trap that deals Fire property damage to all enemies around it at regular intervals. Has a chance of inflicting the Burning status on all enemies struck. The damage dealt by this trap is treated as Burning Damage.

Stone Trap: The user sets a persistent trap that deals Earth property damage to all enemies around it at regular intervals. Has a chance of inflicting Internal Bleeding on all enemies struck. The damage dealt by this trap is treated as Bleeding Damage.

Venom Trap: The user sets a persistent trap that deals Poison property damage to all enemies around it at regular intervals. Has a chance to inflict the Poison status on all enemies struck. The damage dealt by this trap is treated as Poison damage.

Ritual Mastery: Mastery in performing rituals to call on the aid of the spirits of nature. Each level reduces the cast time of Nature Rituals cast by the user. A Nature Ritual that is already active can be recast instantly.

Roaring Winds: Performs a ritual to call on the spirits of spring, ushering in a tremendous windstorm. The user gains an aura that increases the Wind Damage dealt and reduces the Water Damage dealt to all allies and enemies within range. In addition, players in range gain increased Max ASPD. Only one Nature Ritual can be active at a time.

Blazing Heat: Performs a ritual to call on the spirits of summer, ushering in intense heat. The user gains an aura that increases Fire Damage and reduces Earth Damage taken by all creatures within range. In addition, players in range gain increased Crit Rate. Only one Nature Ritual can be active at a time.

Eternal Decay: Performs a ritual to call on the spirits of autumn, ushering in the collapse and decay of the natural world. The user gains an aura that increases the Earth damage and reduces the Wind damage taken by all creatures within its range. In addition, players in range gain increased Bleeding, Burning, and Poison damage. Only one Nature Ritual can be active at a time.

Glacial Chill: Performs a ritual to call on the spirits of winter, ushering in frigid calm and hibernation. The user gains an aura that increases the Water Damage and decreases the Fire Damage taken by all creatures within its range. In addition, players in range gain increased Defense and Magic Defense Pierce. Only one Nature Ritual can be active at a time.

Bard and Dancer.x: Bard and Dancer are the secondary advancement options for Archers. Setting aside their bows, the two performer classes opt for a much more challenging playstyle: it’s not good enough to just deal damage, the damage has to be dealt with style!

Much of the Bard and Dancer kits are shared, as is their core mechanic: Rhythm. Bards and Dancers have a Rhythm Level which is constantly displayed above their heads, except when it’s at zero, to “rate” their performance. Every time the performer uses a Performance skill, it will either increase or decrease their Rhythm level, based on whether the current Rhythm Level is even or odd, capping at 5. Together with a large number of skills at their disposal, this mechanic makes playing a performer quite a handful, as skill cooldowns, positioning, and rhythm level all need to be kept in mind...not to mention actually finding opportunities to put out damage.

To aid in maintaining Rhythm levels, Bards and Dancers get access to the skills Synchronic Strike and Vicious Verse, dealing physical and magical damage respectively, that not only improve based on the active Rhythm Level, but also serve to extend the duration of the current Rhythm Level by a small amount. This allows them to keep contributing damage even while most of their focus is concentrated on their more supportive Performance skills.

In order to generate these Rhythm levels in the first place, Bards and Dancers each have four unique Performance skills: two designed to support the user and their party, and two designed to harm or inhibit enemies. In addition, they have three shared Finale skills, which when used set the user’s Rhythm Level to zero, but provide huge buffs — or in one case, huge damage — based on the Rhythm Level before it was reset.

All in all, Bards and Dancers are potentially the most complex class to play. The reward for mastering that complexity is a class that possesses both incredible support capabilities and excellent damage output.
Bards and Dancers gain access to the following skills:
Bard Only Skills
Musical Mastery: Passive. Increases the Hit Rate and Damage of Instruments, and increases the duration of Rhythm stacks gained. Instruments typically gain Reduced SP Consumption as a mastery bonus.

Restorative Refrain: Plays a gentle song to encourage and reinvigorate the party, healing all party members a small amount over time. If the current Rhythm Level is Odd, it is increased by 1. Otherwise, it is decreased by 1.

Quickening Chorus: Plays an energetic song to inspire the party to quick action. Reduces the Variable Cast Time of all skills cast by each party member significantly. If cast while the current Rhythm Level is even or zero, it is increased by 1. Otherwise, it is decreased by 1.

Darkening Dirge: Plays a haunting melody to cloud the minds—and eyes—of enemies. Has a high chance to inflict the Blind status to all enemies in an enormous area. If the current Rhythm Level is odd, it is increased by 1. Otherwise, it is decreased by 1.

Enervating Elegy: Plays an eerie tune that saps the energy from enemies, leaving them weak and vulnerable. Inflicts the Vulnerable and Breach Statuses on all enemies in the area. If the current Rhythm Level is even or zero, it is increased by 1. Otherwise, it is decreased by 1.
Dancer Only Skills
Dancing Dexterity: Passive. Increases the Hit Rate and Damage of Whips, and increases the duration of Rhythm stacks gained. Whips typically gain Reduced SP Consumption as a mastery bonus.
Noetic Number: The user performs an edifying dance, restoring SP to the party over a short period of time. If the current Rhythm level is odd, it is increased by 1. Otherwise, it is decreased by 1.

Savage Stride: The user performs a savagely beautiful dance, inspiring the party to acts of great violence. Provides a massive boost to Crit Rate for a short duration. If the current Rhythm Level is even or zero, it is increased by 1. Otherwise, it is decreased by 1.
Wearying Waltz: The user performs a strangely enervating dance, attempting to Slow all enemies in the area. If the current Rhythm level is odd, it is increased by 1. Otherwise, it is decreased by 1.

Sinister Saunter: The user performs an alluring dance, distracting enemies into letting down their guard. All enemies in the area take increased damage for a short period of time. If the current Rhythm Level is even or zero, it is increased by 1. Otherwise, it is decreased by 1.
Shared Skills

Synchronic Strike: Uses the Instrument or Whip to throw a volley of arrows at a distant target, carefully timed to synchronize with their performance. Deals increased damage based on the currently active Rhythm level, and increases its duration slightly.

Vicious Verse: The user recites an enchanted verse laced with deadly magic to harm their enemies without breaking the rhythm of their performance. Deals magic damage to the target, which is increased by the current Rhythm Level, and slightly increases its duration.

Hero’s Hymn: The user sings a majestic song to steel the party’s resolve, consuming all Rhythm stacks to provide massive buffs to Attack, Magic Attack, Defense, and Magic Defense for the duration. The duration of the buff is based on the number of Rhythm Stacks consumed. Does not stack with Ardent Anthem.

Ardent Anthem: The user sings an energizing melody, inspiring their party to quicker and safer movement. Consumes all of the user’s Rhythm stacks to give massive boosts to Movement Speed, Flee, and Perfect Dodge to the whole party. The duration of the buff is based on the number of Rhythm Stacks consumed. Does not stack with Hero’s Hymn.

Devastating Descant: The user infuses their voice with destructive power and screams, consuming all Rhythm stacks to deal massive hybrid-type damage to all enemies in the area around them. The damage dealt is heavily influenced by the number of Rhythm stacks consumed.

Clown/Gypsy.x: Clown and Gypsy are the primary advancement option for Bards and Dancers. Unlike most third jobs, where the primary advancement option sticks close in theme and function to the original job, Clown and Gypsy both diverge quite significantly from the playstyle of Bard and Dancer. Content to rely on the supportive abilities of their 2nd job songs and dances, they turn their third job skill points towards more direct and focused intervention on the battlefield.

The first branch of skills for these classes will be more familiar to their 2nd job counterparts. Voluminous Volley and Ravaging Rainstorm provide a way to convert the user’s Rhythm Level into physical damage, while Rhythmic Retort and Crushing Concerto do the same for magic damage.
The second branch of skills for these performers can itself be divided into two branches. These are the Tarot Card skills, divided evenly between supportive and offensive abilities.

The supportive Tarot Cards give the performer a variety of ways to enhance their allies. The Magician and Strength serve to increase their party members’ magical and physical damage respectively. The High Priestess provides emergency healing, while the Lovers protects them from status effects. Finally, the ultimate culmination of this tree is the Wheel of Fortune, which consumes the user’s Rhythm to reduce all of their currently active skill cooldowns.

Standing opposed to these are the offensive Tarot Cards. The Fool and the Hanged Man provide disruptive effects to halt the enemy’s movement and skill use, while the Tower and the Devil inflict direct damage and status effects. These offensive skills are crowned by Death, which inflicts damage based on the user’s Max HP that pierces all defenses for an exceptional burst of damage when needed most.
Unlike their previous classes, Clown and Gypsy gain access to an identical skill tree. Their only difference is the skills they inherit from their second job.
Skills:
Voluminous Volley: The user fires a volley of arrows at a distant target, hitting a number of times based on their Rhythm level for physical damage. If the user’s Rhythm is at 0, the skill will miss.

Ravaging Rainstorm: The user fires a volley of enchanted arrows to rain on a distant area, inflicting physical damage repeatedly to all targets within over time. The interval between hits is reduced by the user’s Rhythm level, which is consumed on cast.

Rhythmic Retort: The user fires a bolt of sound at a distance target, inflicting magic damage while altering their own Rhythm level. If the user’s Rhythm level is below 3, it is increased by 1. If it’s above 3, it is decreased by 1. If the user’s rhythm level is exactly three, its duration is increased by 5 seconds.

Crushing Concerto: Creates a powerful burst of sound, dealing devastating magical damage to all enemies in a small area. The amount of damage is based on the user’s Rhythm level, which is consumed. If the user’s Rhythm is 0, this skill will miss.

Tarot Card: The Magician: Bestows the blessing of the Magician on the targeted ally, increasing all damage dealt by their magical attacks for a short time. The duration of the buff is based on the Rhythm level of the user when it was applied.

Tarot Card: Strength: Bestows the blessing of Strength on the targeted ally, increasing all damage dealt by their Physical attacks for a short time. The duration of the buff is based on the Rhythm level of the user when it was applied.

Tarot Card: The High Priestess: Bestows the blessing of the High Priestess on the targeted ally, causing them to heal a small amount of life the next few times they would take damage. The amount healed is based on the user’s Rhythm Level when the buff was applied.

Tarot Card: The Lovers: Bestows the blessing of the Lovers on the targeted ally, curing them of numerous negative Statuses and shielding them from those statuses for a short time. The duration of the protective effect is based on the user’s Rhythm Level when the buff was applied.

Tarot Card: Wheel of Fortune: Bestows the blessing of the Wheel of Fortune on the user. Consumes the user’s Rhythm Level to reduce all currently active skill cooldowns by a large amount. This skill only affects the caster, it cannot be used on other allies.

Tarot Card: The Fool: Bestows the curse of the Fool on the targeted enemy. For a short duration, skills cast by that enemy have a chance to fail. The failure chance is based on the user’s Rhythm Level when the debuff was applied. The debuff will persist until either a skill fails, or the max duration is reached.
Tarot Card: The Hanged Man: Bestows the curse of the Hanged Man on the targeted enemy, inflicting various disabling statuses based on the user’s Rhythm Level.
1~2: Slow
3~4: Immobilize
5: Stun

Tarot Card: The Tower: Inflicts Hybrid damage on the targeted enemy based on the user’s Rhythm Level. The damage takes the property of the user’s equipped arrow. If the user’s Rhythm Level is zero, this skill will miss.

Tarot Card: The Devil: Bestows the curse of the Devil on the targeted enemy. After a short delay, the target explodes, dealing hybrid damage and inflicting various status effects to all enemies in the area based on the user’s Rhythm Level at the time the debuff was applied.
1~2: Severe Burning
3~4: Deadly Poison
5: Internal Bleeding

Tarot Card: Death: Consumes the user’s Rhythm level to inflict direct damage on a single target proportional to the user’s Max HP. The damage dealt by this skill is neither physical nor magical. The HP to Damage ratio of this skill is determined by the user’s Rhythm Level.

Minstrel/Wanderer.x: Minstrel and Wanderer are the alternative advancement options for Bard and Dancer. They pick up the support mantle that the Clown and Gypsy abandoned, enhancing the already impressive support abilities of the Bard and Dancer with their own unique twist.
Because managing Rhythm levels wasn’t quite enough, Minstrels and Wanderers gain two more effects to juggle: Melodic Mark and Hypnotic Harmony.

Melodic Mark is an offensive ability that, as you might guess, puts a mark on the targeted enemy, in addition to dealing a modest bit of damage. This mark causes all other offensive Minstrel/Wanderer skills to autotarget them, allowing the abilities to exhibit exceptional output against a wide range of foes, if the user is able to manage their marks correctly.

Hypnotic Harmony is the supportive counterpart to Melodic Mark. Casting Hypnotic Harmony on an ally applies its buff both to the ally and the user, slightly increasing their Base Stats for a duration. Once the Harmony is applied, all the supportive Minstrel/Wanderer skills will autotarget that ally, turning the Harmony into a much stronger bonus.

In order to aid in balancing these many marks and statuses, the Minstrel and Wanderer also gain access to two new utility skills. Improvised Interlude allows the user to set their Rhythm Level instantly to any number they wish, while Desperate Dynamic gives them a panic button to immediately apply Melodic Mark and Hypnotic Harmony to all appropriate targets within range.
Minstrel and Wanderer inherit and expand on the complexity of the Bard and Dancer classes, but those that can match their rhythm will dominate the battle with elegance and style.

Improvised Interlude: The user improvises a melody, reaching a crescendo in their performance exactly when it's needed. Immediately sets the user's Rhythm level to a value determined by the skill level used.

Desperate Dynamic: The user adds a powerful chord to their performance, preparing for a desperate and grand climax. Immediately applies Melodic Mark to all enemies and Hypnotic Harmony to all allies within a given range of the user.
Melodic Mark: Applies a musical curse to the target, dealing a small amount of damage and making them vulnerable to further abilities coming from the user.

Sonorant Spike: The user sings a screeching note, triggering all of their Melodic Marks to deal damage to their targets. Deals Physical Ranged damage to all targets affected by Melodic Mark within range of the user, has a chance to inflict the Internal Bleeding status on them, and resets the duration of their Melodic Mark.
Ruinous Rhapsody: The user sings a terrifying note, triggering all of their Melodic Marks to deal Magic Damage, inflict the Burning Status, and then reset the duration of their Marks.

Furious Finale: The user sings a furious note, triggering all of their Melodic Marks to inflict massive damage on their targets. Consumes the user's current Rhythm level to deal enormous Hybrid damage and reset the duration of the targets' Melodic Marks. If the user's Rhythm Level is at 0, this skill will fail.

Hypnotic Harmony: Applies a musical blessing to the target, providing a small increase to the target's stats and marking them to receive bonuses from the other skills of the user. Whenever Hypnotic Harmony is applied to an ally, it is also applied to the user.
