Woeful Warcry: The user sings a vengeful note, spurring their allies on to bloodshed. The user gains the Warcry status, increasing their Strength, Vitality, Defense Pierce, and Crit Damage based on their Rhythm Level. The same Status is applied to all allies within range that currently have Hypnotic Harmony active, and the duration of their Hypnotic Harmony status is reset. Casting this skill resets the user's Rhythm level to zero. Does not stack with Cryptic Cadence or Eternal Echo.

Cryptic Cadence: The user sings a mysterious note, bestowing strength on their allies from beyond their understanding. The user gains the Cryptic status, granting them increased Intelligence, Dexterity, and Magic Defense Pierce, and reduced Cast Times based on their Rhythm Level. The same Status is applied to all allies within range that currently have Hypnotic Harmony active, and the duration of their Hypnotic Harmony status is reset. Casting this skill resets the user's Rhythm level to zero. Does not stack with Woeful Warcry or Eternal Echo.

Eternal Echo: The user sings an echoing note, drawing supernatural strength from their allies' souls. The user gains the Echo status, reducing their Cooldowns and increasing their Agility, Luck, and Max ASPD. The same Status is applied to all allies within range that currently have Hypnotic Harmony active, and the duration of their Hypnotic Harmony status is reset. Casting this skill resets the user's Rhythm level to zero. Does not stack with Woeful Warcry or Cryptic Cadence.

Acolyte.x: Though the Acolyte finds its roots in the support classes of old, don’t let that fool you. Acolytes are more than capable of braving the wilds on their own, with access to a number of damaging skills beyond just offensive Heal. Their preferred weapon, the Mace, also provides a balanced amount of ATK and MATK, and with skills that leverage both, they have no difficulty fighting on their own. Coupled with the supportive abilities of their predecessors in Vanilla RO, the Acolyte is able to provide a huge boost of sustain to the party while still outputting its share of damage.

They are not, however, to be mistaken for the damage-dealing juggernauts like Merchants and Mages. The damaging skills of the Acolyte are locked to the Holy element, making them excellent against Dark and Undead, but in comparison they often feel lackluster against everything else. Together with the moderate cooldowns their skills carry, playing an Acolyte will still require a degree of patience.
Acolytes have access to one key status effect: Aspersio. As with Vanilla, Aspersio endows the user’s weapon with the Holy element, as well as buffs the effects of some other skills.
Acolytes cap at job level 50, giving them 50 skill points to invest in the following skills:
Heal: Instantly recovers a large amount of HP for the target. Can alternatively be used to damage Undead property enemies. Has a considerable cooldown.
Blessing: Increases the Hit, Flee, and Perfect Dodge of the target for a lengthy duration.
Piety: Improves the users Max SP, SP Regeneration, and Healing Power.
Mace Mastery: Increases the damage and Hit Rate of Maces.
Holy Light: Deals Holy element magic damage to a single target, which is increased if the caster is under the Aspersio status.

Smite: Deals physical damage according to the weapon’s property to a single target. If under the Aspersio status, the target will explode after three seconds, doing the same damage again to the target and all enemies in the area around them.
Signum Crucis: Does hybrid Physical and Magical damage that is Holy element to all enemies in an area around the caster. Also endows the user with the Aspersio effect for a short time.

Priest.x: Priest is the primary advancement option for the Acolyte. Much like the Acolyte, Priests have a solid mixture of supportive abilities meant to keep themselves and their party alive, as well as powerful offensive abilities specialized for exorcizing the undead and unnatural.

Priest skills branch in two directions based on their two passives: Divine Grace and Divine Authority. Grace skills offer supportive abilities, from healing over time, to cleansing and protection from status effects, to an extended and enhanced Aspersio effect. The branch is capped by the skill Kyrie Eleison, a defensive buff that halves all damage taken by an ally for a short duration.

Authority skills are offensively oriented. Banishing Light does a small burst of damage, and is especially effective against Demon, Undead, and Angel race enemies. Searing Light burns a target, dealing damage over time that is enhanced if the target is Dark, Undead, or Ghost property, though reduced if they are Holy property. Purifying Light is a small AoE that deals a large amount of damage in its own right, but also leaves enemies vulnerable to further Holy property attacks. Finally, the branch is capped by Divine Judgment, a skill that doubles the damage enemies take for a fixed number of hits based on the skill’s level.

However, as distinct and separate as these two branches seem at first glance, the core mechanic of the Priest class ties the two firmly back together. Whenever the Priest casts a Grace skill, they receive the Divine Grace buff. If an Authority skill is cast while this buff is active, the Authority skill will be cast at the same level as the Grace skill that preceded it: for example, if a Priest casts Aspersio at level 5, then attempts to cast Purifying Light at level 1, the Purifying Light will be cast as if it were level 5 instead.

This interaction works in both directions, allowing both support focused Priests to contribute considerable damage and exorcist Priests to continue offering excellent support capabilities without having to spread their skill points so thinly between the two branches. This extra layer of complexity makes careful planning, both in the skill build and on the battlefield, critical to mastering the Priest class.
Priests gain access to the following skills:

Divine Grace: Passive. Increases the effectiveness of all Grace skills cast by the user. After casting a Grace skill, the next Authority skill they cast will be cast at the same level as that Grace skill, unless the Authority skill is already a higher level.
Aspersio: Grace Skill. Endows the weapons of all party members with the Holy property. For each level of Divine Grace learned, all Holy property damage dealt by those party members is increased.
Renovatio: Grace Skill. Calls a regenerating light to shine on all party members, restoring life over time for a short duration. Higher levels of Divine Grace reduce this skill’s cooldown.

Impositio Manus: Grace Skill. Invokes a miracle of restoration on all party members through the laying of hands. Removes a number of damaging status effects from all party members and provides immunity to them for a short period of time. Higher levels of Divine Grace reduce this skill’s cooldown.

Offertorium: Grace Skill. The user presents themselves as an offering to the divine, preparing themselves to prioritize the will of Heaven before their own wants and needs. While active, the user gains a bonus to Healing Power based on their Strength, and gains a chance to autocast the Smite skill when autoattacking.

Kyrie Eleison: Grace Skill. The user prays for divine intervention, calling on heavenly powers to protect a target from all harm. For a short duration, all damage taken by the target is halved. Higher levels of Divine Grace reduce this skill’s cooldown.

Divine Authority: Passive. Increases the effectiveness of all Authority skills cast by the user. After casting an Authority skill, the next Grace skill they cast will be cast at the same level as that Authority skill, unless the Grace skill is already a higher level.

Banishing Light: Authority Skill.; Summons a holy light to banish the target from the mortal realm, dealing Holy property damage that is increased against Demon, Undead, and Angel race monsters. For each level of Divine Authority learned, a portion of this bonus is applied to enemies of other races.

Searing Light: Authority Skill. Calls sacred fire from the heavens to incinerate the target, inflicting them with a status effect similar to the Burning status. The damage is heavily influenced by the user’s Base Level, Skill Level, and Int, and is increased against Dark, Undead, and Ghost Property targets, while halved against Holy Property targets. The duration of the status is increased by the Divine Authority skill.

Purifying Light: Authority Skill. Invokes a divine light to purify the world of the enemy and their surroundings. Deals significant Holy property damage to enemies in an area around the target and inflicts the Holy Vulnerability status, increasing the damage they take from Holy property attacks from all sources (Holy Vulnerability does not affect Searing Light damage). The strength of the Vulnerability is based on the learned level of the Divine Authority skill.

Austere Light: Authority Skill. The user smashes an enemy with their weapon, dealing Weapon Property Physical damage to a single target and boosting the user’s Attack Speed for a short duration. This skill has a chance to inflict the Vulnerable Status based on the user’s learned level of Divine Authority.

Divine Judgment: Authority Skill. Calls divine judgment down on a target, causing them to take double damage from attacks of all sources for a set number of hits, based on the level of the skill. Higher levels of Divine Authority reduce this skill’s cooldown.

High Priest.x: High Priest is the primary advancement option for Priests. High Priest very much follows in the same footsteps as the Priest, dividing their skills cleanly between Grace and Authority, and allowing skills of either side to enhance the skill levels of the other if used in the correct order.

To further expand on this theme, the High Priest gains access to two new utility skills, Lux Divina and Lux Aeterna. Each of these skills serves no function but to increase the level of the currently applied Grace or Authority Status, or swap to the other if the wrong one is currently active. This allows the High Priest to extend their combos further, or if used wisely, to cast their skills at an incredible level of 15.

As for the skills which they are enhancing, they are once again divided by Grace and Authority. Grace Skills give the High Priest the ability to heal the entire party at once, increase the Crit Rate and ASPD Limit of the entire party, and reduce the SP Costs and grant ignore interrupt to all party members. Authority skills grant the expected Holy Damage, coming in single target, point blank AoE, and ranged AoE variations.

These two trees are capped by ultimate skills, BS Sacramenti for Grace Skills and Epiclesis for Authority Skills. The unique aspect of these skills is that they max at level 1 — getting any sort of reasonable performance out of them will require smart use of the Grace and Authority system.
The whole kit ties together to create a class that excels in both Support and Damage, and can even do both at the same time with a bit of careful planning and precise execution.

Lux Divina: The user is blessed by the divine light of Heaven, granting them unprecedented ability to call on miracles to aid their allies. If the user is under the Grace status, they gain the Authority status of the same level. If the user is already under the Authority status, the level of the Authority status is increased (to a maximum of 15).

Lux Aeterna: The user is blessed by the eternal light of Heaven, granting them unprecedented ability to call down holy wrath on their foes. If the user is under the Authority status, they gain the Grace status of the same level. If the user is already under the Grace status, the level of the Grace status is increased (to a maximum of 15).

Coluceo Heal: Grace Skill. The user casts a wide ranging blessing, mending the wounds of all party members simultaneously. Immediately heals all party members for an amount equal to a Heal skill of the same level. Each level of Divine Grace learned reduces this skill's Cooldown.
Gloria: Grace Skill. The user sings a hymn of praise, lending divine strength to their allies' attacks. Increases the Crit Rate and ASPD Cap of all party members for a short duration.

Magnificat: Grace Skill. The user sings a hymn of praise, granting divine edification to their party members. Reduces the SP Costs of all skills and grants ignore interrupt to all party members for a short duration.

Benedictio Sanctissimi Sacramenti: Grace Skill. Performs a holy rite, massively improving the party's attack and defense. Grants all party members improved Defense Pierce, Magic Pierce, Hard Defense, and Hard Magic Defense.
Flamen: Authority Skill. Summons a holy light to smite an enemy. Deals Holy property magic damage to a single enemy. Does increased damage to enemies afflicted with Searing Light.

Oleum Sanctum: Authority Skill. Shatters a vial of sacred oil, creating a wave of purification that forces out all enemies in the area. Deals Holy property magic damage to all enemies in the area around the user and knocks them back. Has a chance to inflict Searing Light on all enemies struck.

Magnus Exorcismus: Authority Skill. Creates an area of consecrated ground to exorcize the wicked. Places a persistent ground effect that deals Holy magic damage over time to all enemies that stand within it. Demon, Undead, and Angel Race monsters struck are additionally Stunned, while all other enemies are Slowed. Deals additional damage to enemies under Searing Light.

Epiclesis: Authority Skill. Creates an illusory tree of divine light, filling the targeted area with holy energies that reject all of the caster's enemies for the duration. While the tree persists, all enemies in the area take Magic damage over time and are repeatedly inflicted with the Vulnerable, Breach, and Slow statuses.

Arch Bishop.x: Arch Bishop is the alternative advancement option for Priests. While the Priest divided its skills between supportive Grace Skills and offensive Authority skills, the Arch Bishop instead divides its skills into three general branches, each of which offering a Grace Skill, an Authority Skill, and an unaligned skill to tie them together.

The first branch of skills are offensive in nature. Oratio puts a holy curse on enemies, causing them to take additional damage whenever struck by Holy damage. Arbitrium deals direct Holy Property Magic damage to a single target and also inflicts the Searing Light status. Finally, Adoramus deals Holy Property Magic Damage in a wide area around the target, with additional effects based on whether the user is in Grace or Authority status.

The second branch of skills are the supportive ones. Grace Heal instantly recovers HP for a targeted ally, both restoring HP and providing a barrier to prevent further damage. Argutus Vita meanwhile is an Authority skill that increases the Atk and Matk of all party members. These are accompanied by Lux Pacifica, consuming the user’s Grace or Authority status to grant all allies a protective blessing that heals them whenever they take damage (Grace) or deal damage (Authority).

The final branch brings Physical Skills. With a Grace Skill to increase the user’s Atk and Vulnerable Potency, an Authority Skill to deal direct damage, and an unaligned skill to leverage both Grace and Authority Statuses to deal huge burst damage, the Arch Bishop finally has what it needs to draw the Battle Priest out of the wings and into the fight.

Lastly, the Arch Bishop’s skill tree is crowned by one last ultimate skill, Manus Dei. This skill calls for divine intervention, bestowing a miracle upon their party to turn the tides of battle at the worst possible moment. This skill requires Base Level 130 to unlock, but otherwise has no requirements and only takes a single skill point, thus turning any suitably leveled Arch Bishop into an incredible asset for any party.
Skills:

Oratio: Grace Skill. The user calls down a holy curse on all enemies around them, revealing them and increasing the damage they take from Holy Property attacks. Whenever an enemy under the Oratio Status takes Holy Property damage, they take an additional burst of damage.
Arbitrium: Authority Skill. The user calls a divine light from heaven to scour the targeted enemy from existence, dealing Holy property Magic Damage and inflicting the Searing Light status.
Adoramus: Unaligned Skill. The user calls on a purging light to cleanse the targeted area of all foes. Deals Holy Property Magic damage to all enemies in an area around the target.
If the user is under the Grace Status, it is consumed to inflict Slow and Blind on all enemies affected.
If the user is under the Authority Status, it is consumed to inflict Vulnerable and Breach on all enemies affected.

Grace Heal: Grace Skill. Instantly recovers a large amount of HP for the targeted ally, while also granting them a barrier to protect them from further damage. The barrier’s HP is equal to the amount of HP healed by this skill, including any overflow.
Argutus Vita: Authority Skill. The user chants an inspiring prayer, bolstering the faith and confidence of their party. Increases the Atk and MAtk of all party members for the duration.

Lux Pacifica: Unaligned skill. The user bestows a sheltering miracle on their party members. If the user is under the Grace Status, consumes it to apply a buff that heals the targets whenever they would take damage.
If the user is under the Authority status, consumes it to apply a buff that heals the targets whenever they would deal damage.
Whenever this skill grants healing, the original caster loses a small amount of SP. The effect ends early if the caster runs out of SP.
Expiatio: Grace Skill. The user calls upon a blessing of war, increasing their Attack and Vulnerable Potency for the duration.

Petitio: Authority Skill. The user delivers a punishing smite to the targeted enemy, inflicting Physical damage to them and all enemies in an area around them. Vulnerable enemies take increased damage. For a short duration after casting this skill, the Smite skill deals increased damage.
Gladius Sanctum: Unaligned skill. The user calls down swords of divine light, tearing apart the targeted enemy. Deals Weapon Property Physical Damage to the target three times.
If the user is under the Grace Status, it is consumed, and this skill inflicts the Stun Status.
If the user is under the Authority Status, it is consumed, and this skill inflicts the Bleeding Status.

Manus Dei: The user makes a desperate plea for divine intervention, and is granted a miracle to turn the tides of battle. Any dead party members in the area are immediately resurrected, then all party members are healed to full HP and SP and gain the Aspersio and Assumptio statuses for an extended duration.
If the user is under the Grace Status, the user takes half damage from all attacks while this skill is casting.
If the user is under the Authority Status, all enemies in the area of effect are Slowed and Blinded.
A player may only be affected by this skill once every five minutes, even from a different caster.

Monk.x: Monk is the secondary advancement option for the Acolyte class. It forgoes the majority of its ancestor’s supportive potential to focus on closing out fights in the best way possible: damage, damage, and more damage.

Following the same pattern as the Priest, Monk skills are divided into two general branches: Spirit Skills building out of the Spiritual Discipline passive, and Combo Skills building out of the Fist Mastery passive. However, these should not be mistaken for two separate builds—while a Monk may choose to specialize in one side of the skill tree over the other, weaving both sides of the tree together is the key to maximizing the Monk’s potential.

Also similarly to Priest, Monks have the same system of copying skill levels. Using a Discipline skill will cause your next Combo skill to rise in level to meet it, and vice versa. However, the Monk takes this system one step further, with all skills getting a bonus if cast this way, and a different bonus if cast immediately after another skill of the same type.

The Combo skills are extremely straightforward. They do not require a combo state and can be cast freely, and are capable of dealing Critical damage. If they are cast immediately following a Discipline skill, they are guaranteed to Crit, while if cast following another Combo skill, their cooldown is reduced by half.

Spirit skills, while not much more complex, are at least a bit more varied. Each skill deals physical damage with a unique attribute—one gaining damage based on the target’s defense, the other able to be cast at a considerable range—and if cast immediately after a Combo skill, also inflict status effects like Slow and Vulnerable. If instead cast after another Spirit skill, they have their Cooldowns halved.

Finally, Monks possess two skills that slot between the two branches, Spiritual Cadence and Fury. Spiritual Cadence grants the user a stacking buff that increases in effectiveness every time the user switches between Combo and Discipline skills, restoring a small amount of HP and SP each time. Fury fills the opposite niche, granting a stacking buff that increases in strength every time the user uses a skill that matches the previous one, also boosting the user’s Crit Rate. Both effects reset to the lowest level if the wrong condition is met, forcing the Monk to think carefully before breaking from their usual combo routine.
Monks gain access to the following skills:

Spiritual Discipline: Passive. Increases the damage of all Spirit skills. Whenever the user casts a Spirit skill, the next Combo skill they use will be cast at the same level, assuming it isn’t already higher.

Soul Piercer: Spirit skill. The user strikes a target with a concentrated blast of spiritual energy, capable of piercing through any armor. This skill does additional damage based on the user’s Int, and is also increased by the target’s Defense. If cast immediately after a Combo skill, this skill also inflicts the Vulnerable status. If cast immediately after a Spirit skill, its cooldown is halved.

Spiritual Lash: Spirit Skill. The user focuses their spiritual energy into a physical projectile before hurling it at a distant enemy. This skill does additional damage based on the user’s Int. If used immediately after a Combo skill, it also inflicts the Slow status. If used immediately after another Spirit skill, its cooldown is halved.

Soul Quake: Spirit Finisher. The user unleashes a destructive wave of spiritual energy in every direction, damaging all enemies in a wide area. This skill does additional damage based on the user’s Int. If cast immediately after a Combo skill, this skill also inflicts the Stun status. If cast immediately after another Spirit skill, its cooldown is halved. This skill does not grant the Discipline status.

Fist Mastery: Passive. Increases the damage, Hit Rate, and Attack Speed of Fist-type weapons, including when unarmed. Whenever the user casts a Combo skill, the next Spirit skill used will be cast at the same level, assuming it isn’t already higher.

Raging Triple Blow: Combo Skill. Delivers a flurry of three quick blows to an enemy, dealing moderate damage. It can be cast freely, and will not autocast on attacking. If cast immediately after a Spirit skill, this skill is guaranteed to be Critical. If cast immediately after another Combo skill, its cooldown is halved.

Raging Quadruple Blow: Combo skill. Delivers a flurry of four quick blows to an enemy, dealing moderate damage. It can be cast freely, and does not require a combo state to activate. If cast immediately after a Spirit skill, this skill is guaranteed to be Critical. If cast immediately after another Combo skill, its cooldown is halved.

Raging Thrust: Combo Finisher. Delivers a single devastating punch to an enemy. It can be cast freely, and does not require a combo state to activate. If cast immediately after a Spirit skill, this skill is guaranteed to be Critical. If cast immediately after another Combo skill, its cooldown is halved. This skill does not grant the Iron Fists status.

Spiritual Cadence: Perfection through balance. The user focuses on maintaining perfect balance in all things, fighting in a steady rhythm to maximize staying power. While active, whenever the user gains the Iron Fists or Discipline Status, if it replaced the opposite, the stack count of this skill increases by 1. If it replaced itself, the stack count is reduced to zero. For each stack, the user’s Agility and intelligence are increased, and they regenerate a portion of their HP and SP every five seconds. Does not stack with Fury.

Fury: Perfection through extremity. The user focuses all their might into delivering explosive performance, increasing the power they are able to bring to bear. While active, whenever the user gains the Iron Fists or Discipline Status, if it replaced itself, the stack count of this skill increases by 1. If it replaced its opposite, the stack count is reduced to zero. For each stack, the user’s Strength, Luck, and Crit Rate are increased. Does not stack with Spiritual Cadence.

Champion.x: Champion is the primary advancement option for the Monk. While Monks found themselves with the option to dedicate themselves to either Spiritual or Combo skills, the Champion seeks to marry these two skill branches together into a perfect harmony.

As with Monk before it, Champion has two primary skill branches. The first is Combo skills, which either repeat rapidly if under the Iron Fists status, or are guaranteed to be Critical if under the Discipline status. These are matched by the Spirit skills, which similarly gain reduced cooldowns while under the Discipline Status, and inflict various status effects while under the Iron Fists Status.

Linking these two disparate branches together are two support skills. One is Unburden, stripping the user’s Iron Fists and Discipline statuses to heal and recover SP, depending on which status was consumed. This becomes a powerful sustain option when combined with the other skill, Zen, which grants the user both the Iron Fists and the Discipline Status simultaneously.

The final two skills are what everyone who plays Monk inevitably asks about. Unbreakable Resolve consumes the user’s remaining SP to grant themselves a powerful damage reduction buff, while Guillotine Fist consumes the user’s remaining SP to deal unbelievable damage to a single target. Both of these skills gain additional effects based on which of Iron Fists or Discipline are active, and thanks to Zen, are capable of benefiting from both.
Skills:

Zen: The user calms their mind and relaxes their body, drawing out their true inner strength and exceeding their limits for a brief moment. Immediately grants both the Iron Fists and Discipline statuses. This skill does not interfere with the stack count of Spiritual Cadence or Fury.

Unburden: The user releases themselves of all worldly attachments, freeing themselves to focus solely on the enemy before them. Consumes the Iron Fists, Discipline, and Fury Statuses to gain various effects.
If Iron Fists is consumed, the user recovers a large amount of HP.
If Discipline is consumed, the user recovers a large amount of SP.

Raging Barrage: Combo Skill. Deals heavy damage to a single target. If the user is under the Discipline Status, this skill is guaranteed to Crit and grants double the level of Iron Fists. If the user is under the Iron Fists status, its cooldown is halved.

Raging Windmill: Combo Skill. Unleashes a whirling blow, striking all enemies in the area around the user for moderate physical damage. If the user is in the Discipline status, it is guaranteed to Crit and grants double the level of Iron Fists. If the user is in the Iron Fists status, its cooldown is halved.

Falling Mountain: Combo Finisher. Delivers a single crushing blow to the target. If the user is in the Discipline Status, it is guaranteed to Crit. If the user is in the Iron Fists status, its cooldown is halved.
This skill consumes Iron Fists and Discipline, but does not grant them.

Spiritual Rupture: Spirit Skill. The user creates a burst of spiritual energy at the targeted location, dealing Ranged Physical Damage to all enemies in the area. The damage is increased by the user’s Magic Attack. If the user is in th eIron Fists Status, it has a chance to inflict Bleeding and grants double the level of Discipline. If the user is under the Discipline status, its cooldown is halved.

Spiritual Pursuit: Spirit skill. The user wields their spiritual energy to hurl themselves at a distant foe, using their own body as a projectile. Deals Ranged Physical Damage to a single target that is increased by the user’s Magic Attack.
If the user is in the Iron Fists status, has a chance to inflict Internal Bleeding and grants double the level of Discipline.
If the user is in the Discipline status, its cooldown is halved.

Soul Explosion: Spirit Finisher. The user unleashes all of their spiritual power in a massive blast centered on themselves. Deals physical damage in an area around the caster, which is increased by the user’s Magic Attack.
If the user is in the Iron Fists status, all enemies struck are knocked back.
If the user is in the Discipline status, its cooldown is halved.
This skill consumes Iron Fists and Discipline, but does not grant them.

Unbreakable Resolve: The user focuses inward, drawing out a supernatural resilience from within themselves. Consumes the user’s remaining SP to grant them a buff that reduces all damage taken for the duration. While this skill is active, the user cannot gain the Iron Fists or Discipline statuses.

Guillotine Fist: The user focuses all of their strength into a single blow, exhausting everything they have to ensure it is fatal. Consumes all of the user’s remaining SP to deal massive damage to a single target. The damage is based on the amount of SP consumed, and is increased by the percentage of missing HP from the target.
If the user is in the Iron Fists status, this skill is guaranteed to Crit and ignores Defense.
If the user is in the Discipline status, the damage dealt is based on the user’s Max SP instead of the amount of SP consumed.
Once struck by this skill, the target will be immune to the effects of Guillotine Fist from the same caster for the next five minutes.

Sura.x: Sura is the alternative advancement option for the Monk. While Champion sought to bring the Combo and Spirit sides of the Monk tree into harmony, the Sura doubles down on specialization, preferring to focus entirely on one side and drawing out its maximum potential.

Naturally, this means each side of the Monk tree is expanded. Furious Thrust, Furious Barrage, and Furious Execution add to the Combo side of the tree, providing a new rotation that can be added alongside the Monk skills or woven between them to create a new rotation altogether. The same can be said for the Spirit skills, Zealous Hammer, Zealous Echo, and Zealous Rage, which add a persistent Burning effect for the Sura to take advantage of in their combos.

These trees are each capped with a built-in combo skill. Flash Combo rapidly executes all three Monk Combo skills, ignoring their cooldowns, while Last Exorcism does the same for the Monk’s Spirit Skills.

In order to squeeze out even more damage from these skills, Sura skills also have the Stigmata mechanic. Each skill inflicts a set number of Stigmata stacks on the target, to a maximum of 10. For each stack, all Sura skills deal additional damage to that target. Together with some self buffs and passives that add additional interactions with these stacks, Suras are perfectly positioned to deal maximum damage to whatever crosses their path.
Burning Faith: Passively increases the damage dealt by Sura skills against enemies with Stigmata Stacks. When activated, Monk Combo Skills also gain this benefit, and also inflict Stigmata stacks.

Resolute Faith: Passively reduces the damage taken from enemies that have any Stigmata stacks. When activated, Monk Spirit skills are treated as Sura skills for Stigmata damage buffs, and also inflict Stigmata stacks.

Judge’s Conviction: The user channels their inner fury, preparing to turn it against all enemies in the area around them. Inflicts a number of Stigmata stacks on all enemies in the area around the user. All Sura skills deal increased damage for each Stigmata stack on a target.

Furious Thrust: The user throws a quick jab, delivering tremendous force with the minimum motion possible. Deals physical damage to a single target and inflicts one stack of Stigmata. If the user is under the Discipline Status, this skill is guaranteed to Crit. If the user is under the Iron Fists Status, this skill additionally grants the user the Aspersio status.

Furious Barrage: The user unleashes a rapid barrage of strikes against a single target, dealing significant damage and inflicting two stacks of Stigmata. If the user is under the Discipline Status, this skill is guaranteed to Crit. If the user is under the Iron Fists status, the cooldown of Furious Thrust is refreshed.

Furious Execution: The user delivers a single crushing blow to an enemy, dealing exceptional physical damage to a single target and inflicting three stacks of Stigmata. If the user is under the Discipline Status, this skill is guaranteed to Crit. If the user is under the Iron Fists status, this skill splashes in a 5x5 area. This skill consumes the Discipline and Iron Fists statuses, but does not grant them.

Flash Combo: The user unleashes a string of powerful Combo skills, dealing exceptional damage to a single target. Immediately casts Raging Trifecta, Raging Quadruple Blow, and Raging Thrust in quick succession, ignoring the internal cooldowns of the skills. The skills are cast at a level equal to the number of Stigmata stacks on the target, ignoring the learned level. If the target is at 10 stacks of Stigmata, Furious Guillotine is added to the end of the combo.

Furious Guillotine: The user delivers a finishing blow to the target, dealing massive physical damage and inflicting the Stun status. This skill does not benefit from the Iron Fists or Discipline statuses, and does not grant them. This skill cannot be learned, and can only be cast through Flash Combo.

Zealous Hammer: The user slams a fist charged with burning spiritual energy into the target, dealing heavy damage to a single target and inflicting one stack of Stigmata. If the user is under the Iron Fists status, this skill also inflicts the Burning status. If the user is under the Discipline status, this skill also grants the Aspersio status to the user.

Zealous Echo: The user unleashes a concentrated wave of spiritual energy, striking all enemies in the area around them. Deals physical damage to all enemies around the user and inflicting two stacks of Stigmata. If the user is under the Iron Fists status, also inflicts the Intense Burning status. If the user is under the Discipline status, the cooldown of Zealous Hammer is instantly refreshed.

Zealous Rage: The user unleashes an explosive wave of spiritual energy, scorching all enemies around them with holy fire. Deals physical damage to all enemies around the user and inflicts three stacks of Stigmata. If the user is under the Iron Fists status, the skill also inflicts Intense Burning. If the user is under the Discipline status, the Variable Cast Time of the skill is removed.

Last Exorcism: The user unleashes a string of powerful Spirit skills, dealing exceptional damage to their target. Immediately casts Soul Piercer, Spiritual Lash, and Soul Quake in quick succession, ignoring the internal cooldowns of the skills. The skills are cast at a level equal to the number of Stigmata stacks on the target. If the target has 10 stacks of Stigmata, Zealous Pyre is added to the end of the combo.

Zealous Pyre: The user focuses their spiritual might on the targeted enemy, creating a localized inferno to obliterate them and all nearby enemies. Deals massive physical damage and inflicts both Burning and Severe Burning. This skill does not benefit from the Iron Fists or Discipline statuses, and does not grant them. This skill cannot be learned, and can only be cast through Last Exorcism.

Taekwon.x: The Taekwon is the first of the Expanded Classes, a group of classes outside the core six starter classes that sport somewhat more complicated class mechanics than usual, and may have somewhat abnormal class structures.

The Taekwon continues its vanilla tradition of spurning weapons in favor of a mastery that provides considerable amounts of Attack very early in the game, though they shouldn’t put away those weapon cards quite yet. While they can’t equip weapons, they can instead equip “Card Albums,” equipment that take the Weapon Slot of the equipment window, but have no effect at all except to carry Weapon cards. This allows them to punch, or I suppose kick, above their weight class with a bit of investment, sparing them the fate of being left behind by other jobs who continue to gain stronger and stronger weapons as they progress.

Taekwon skills can be divided into two broad categories: Martial Skills and Kick Skills. The Martial Skills are all passive. They each associate with a single core stat (Strength, Agility, Dexterity, etc), increasing that stat and providing a related bonus. These give the Taekwon a strong core that can build themselves to a competitive level against other jobs without even having to consider active skills.

In addition to these passives are the Kick Skills, which function quite differently than those in vanilla. Instead of requiring a stance proc to activate, the Kick skills can all be activated freely, and will instead provide a stance buff upon doing so. While a stance buff is active, it will provide buffs to all following kicks that are used — until the user attempts to double up. The moment a kick whose stance is already active is used, or when the five second timer on the first stance expires, all stance buffs are immediately removed, and the combo must be rebuilt from scratch. This allows skilled Taekwons to “build their own combos,” optimizing their rotations for each specific encounter.

Finally, Taekwons have one more unique characteristic that sets them apart even from other Expanded classes: instead of changing jobs to Star Gladiator or Soul Linker when they reach Job Level 50, they can instead opt to take on the “Taekwon Mission.” This series of quests lock them out of job changing permanently, and in exchange grant them powerful buffs to all of their skills, a new kick inaccessible to ordinary Taekwons, and fifty additional job levels to fill out the remainder of their skill tree.
Taekwons gain access to the following skills:
Martial Training: Training in basic combat and physical fitness. Passively increases the user’s Strength and Hit Rate, and increases the user’s damage while unarmed.
Martial Endurance: Training in endurance and perseverance. Passively increases the user’s Vitality and increases the effectiveness of Healing Potions they use.
Martial Discipline: Training in focus and discipline. Passively increases the user’s Intelligence and increases the effectiveness of SP Potions they use.

Martial Precision: Training in precise and accurate technique. Passively increases the user’s Dexterity, Hit Rate, and Defense Pierce. Defense Pierce gained from this skill is treated as card-like pierce for stacking purposes.
Martial Agility: Training in rapid and flexible movement. Passively increases the user’s Agility, Flee, and Perfect Dodge.

Counter Kick: Delivers a powerful kick to the enemy, ignoring the target’s Flee and bypassing skills like Guard. Activating this skill triggers Counter Stance for 5 seconds, during which all Kick skills ignore the target’s Flee and bypass skills like Guard. Counter Stance ends when any other Stance ends, or when Counter Kick is cast again.

Tornado Kick: The user delivers a wide-reaching kick that strikes all enemies in an area around them. Activating this skill triggers Tornado Stance for 5 seconds, during which all Kick skills splash in an area around the target. Tornado Stance ends when any other Stance ends, or when Tornado Kick is cast again.

Axe Kick: The user delivers a staggering blow to the top of the enemy’s head, dealing significant damage that will leave the target briefly stunned. Activating this skill triggers Axe Stance, during which all Kick Skills inflict various status effects to their targets. Axe Stance ends when any other Stance ends, or when Axe Kick is cast again.
Counter Kick: Inflicts Vulnerable
Tornado Kick: Inflicts Blind
Roundhouse Kick: Inflicts Slow
Demolishing Kick: Inflicts Bleeding

Roundhouse Kick: The user delivers a spinning roundhouse kick to an enemy, utilizing their momentum to keep attacking at a breakneck pace. Activating this skill triggers Roundhouse Stance for 5 seconds, during which the user’s ASPD is increased. Roundhouse Stance ends when any other Stance ends, or when Roundhouse Kick is cast again.

Taekwon Mission: Quest Skill. In exchange for permanently blocking the ability to change jobs, increases the Job Level cap of the user (by up to 50) and increases the damage of all Kick Skills except Demolishing Kick.

Demolishing Kick: The user unleashes a kick with devastating force, dealing exceptional damage to an enemy based on the number of currently active Stances. All Stances immediately end upon casting this skill. This skill cannot be learned unless Taekwon Mission is unlocked.

Star Gladiator.x: The Star Gladiator is the first advancement option for the Taekwon. Though it still utilizes some of the core Taekwon skills, it begins the journey of moving away from simple martial arts and into wielding cosmic powers beyond that any other job can hope to harness.

Similarly to Taekwons, Star Gladiators are very much at home without any weapon at all, and can be used quite effectively with nothing more than the Card Albums of their previous job. However, they also gain the ability to equip Books, transforming knowledge and information into raw power in their kicks.

The other primary characteristic of the Star Gladiator lies in their Skill Tree, which branches off in five directions. Though none of these branches boast enough skills to hog the entirety of the fifty skill points available to them, they all seek to monopolize the Star Gladiator’s focus by providing exceptional buffs to make their skills stand out from the rest. These branches are, of course, the Solar, Lunar, Stellar, and Darkness paths, each fighting in a very different way.

Star Gladiators of the Sun deal exceptionally high damage, augmented by the Burning status. Star Gladiators of the Moon are more defensive, gaining additional life steal on their skills and protecting themselves from numerous negative status effects. Star Gladiators of the Stars find their attacks nigh unstoppable, ignoring virtually all defenses and quickly burning through enemies with rapid fire skills. Finally, Star Gladiators of the Shadows dedicate themselves to dealing Critical Damage over a wide area, dispatching groups of enemies as quickly as possible.

Of course, it makes sense that any prospective Star Gladiator would want to wield all of these powers together, and the fifth and final tree provides that option. The skill Cosmic Union allows the user to forfeit the ability to use all skills in exchange for being able to autocast them at an extremely high rate, and grants them all the bonus effects that their respective trees would otherwise keep to themselves.
Star Gladiators have access to the following skills:

Cosmic Insight: Passive. The Star Gladiator harmonizes themselves with the cosmos, drawing closer to the heavenly bodies and further away from their earthly roots. They gain the ability to divine greater truths from seemingly mundane knowledge, able to transform knowledge into raw physical power. Increases the damage and Hit Rate of Book class weapons, as well as increasing the user’s Luck. Books typically give raw stats as Mastery bonuses.

Solar Heat: Cosmic Alignment. The user infuses themselves with the heat of the Sun, increasing the damage of the Burning status they inflict and increasing their resistance to the Burning and Chilled statuses. In addition, while this buff is active, Counter Kick and Roundhouse Kick deal additional damage based on the user’s Int. Only one Cosmic Alignment can be active at a time.

Solar Pulse: The user delivers a blazing kick, inflicting damage that is increased by the user’s Int and has a high chance to inflict the Burning status. If the user is under the Solar Heat alignment, the damage inflicted by this skill is counted as Burning damage in addition to physical damage for card and skill bonuses. If used during Counter Stance, this skill cannot miss and bypasses skills like Guard. If used during Roundhouse Stance, its cooldown is halved.

Lunar Protection: Cosmic Alignment. The user infuses themselves with the protective essence of the Moon, reducing the damage they take from Burning, Bleeding, and Poison while increasing their resistance to Bleeding and Vulnerable. In addition, while this buff is active, Counter Kick and Axe Kick deal additional damage based on the user’s Vit. Only one Cosmic Alignment can be active at a time.

Lunar Glow: The user shines with the light of the Moon, concentrating it into their hands and feet to deal a powerful blow to a single enemy. The damage dealt by this skill is increased by the user’s Vit. If cast while the Lunar Protection alignment is active, the user regenerates HP equal to a portion of their Max HP. If cast while Counter Stance is active, this skill cannot miss and bypasses skills like Guard. If used while Axe Stance is active, it puts the user into the Cloaking state for a few seconds.

Stellar Blessing: Cosmic Alignment. The user infuses themselves with the ever-present light of the stars, granting them enhanced Hit and Defense Pierce, while also increasing their resistance to Poison and Slow. In addition, while this buff is active, Axe Kick and Tornado Kick deal additional damage based on the user’s Dex. Only one Cosmic Alignment can be active at a time.

Stellar Barrage: The user launches themselves at an enemy, striking them for physical damage that is increased by the user’s Dex. If cast while the Stellar Blessing alignment is active, the attack then repeats two more times at enemies nearby. If there are fewer than three enemies in the area, the same enemy can be struck multiple times. If used during Axe Stance, enemies struck have their elemental property changed to Neutral for a short duration. If used during Tornado Stance, the attack splashes in a 5x5 area.

Umbral Veil: The user shrouds themselves in the infinite darkness of the cosmos, foregoing all pretense at defense in favor of inflicting the maximum possible harm. Increases the Crit Rate and Crit Damage of the user, while also giving resistance to Blind and Stun. In addition, while this buff is active, Tornado Kick and Roundhouse Kick deal additional damage based on the user’s Agi. Only one Cosmic Alignment can be active at a time.

Umbral Blade: The user lashes out at nearby enemies with a blade woven from the emptiness of deep space. The damage dealt by this skill is increased by the user’s Agi, and splashes in a 3x3 area. If cast while Umbral Veil is active, the skill is guaranteed to Crit. If used during Tornado Stance, it splashes in a 7x7 area instead. If used during Roundhouse Stance, its cooldown is halved.

Cosmic Union: Cosmic Alignment. The user unifies with the balanced forces of the cosmos, channeling the power of the Sun, Moon, Stars, and the Darkness between them simultaneously. While in Union status, the following effects are applied:
Max HP, Attack, Defense Pierce, and Crit Rate are increased (based on the learned levels of Lunar Protection, Solar Heat, Stellar Blessing, and Umbral Veil respectively)
Movement Speed is increased
All attacks have a chance to autocast Solar Pulse, Lunar Glow, Stellar Barrage, and Umbral Blade.
All Star Gladiator skills deal additional damage based on the user’s Luck, and gain their bonus Alignment effects.
Max SP is reduced to 1.
Only one Cosmic Alignment can be active at a time.

Star Emperor.x: Star Emperor is the primary advancement option for Star Gladiators. The Star Emperor fully embraces the cosmic powers of the Star Gladiator, all but abandoning their roots in Taekwon Do to draw themselves closer to the cosmos. But while Star Gladiators were incentivized to focus solely on one celestial body, the Star Emperor spreads its wings a little wider. It gains access to a suite of new Sun, Moon, Star, and Shadow skills, but each of these skills shows its true potential only when combined with opposing cosmic alignments.

Each Star Emperor skill naturally gains the bonus of their Cosmic Alignment, even if that alignment is not currently active. However, unlike Star Gladiator skills, Star Emperor skills will also gain the Alignment effects of other Alignments that are active: If Solar Heat is active, all Star Emperor skills will be treated as Burning damage; if Lunar Protection is active, all Star Emperor skills will gain lifesteal, and so on. Thus while it is perfectly acceptable for Star Emperors to continue focusing their skill points on a single Cosmic Alignment of choice, they also have the option to dip into other Alignment skills, giving them a much wider array of utility than the Star Gladiator was capable of.

In addition, the Star Emperor has a pair of skills that are useful to all Star Emperors, regardless of alignment choice - yes, even those who chose the path of Cosmic Union. The first provides a massive buff to all stats for a short duration, but critically, also enables the use of Star Emperor skills without SP, allowing even Union builds to make use of the new skill tree they have advanced into. The second skill is a powerful AoE attack that has no preferred alignment of its own, but gains bonus effects from all other Alignment skills, and unlike other Star Emperor skills, it also has a bonus effect if used during Union.

The result is a remarkably versatile class: with so many options that are all built to synergize with each other, no two Star Emperors need look alike. It will no doubt take considerable time and effort for a budding Star Emperor to settle on the optimal build for their purposes, but no matter which direction their personality and preferences take them, they will find themselves almost invariably with a remarkably synergistic character that is more than ready to face the challenges ahead of them.
Skills:

Solar Flash: The user channels the power of the Sun into a single focused strike, dealing a small amount of damage and inflicting the Burning status. If the target is already burning, it instead consumes the Burning status from them to deal five ticks worth of Burning damage instantly. The damage of this skill is increased based on the user's Int, and is treated as Burning damage. If used under Lunar Protection, the attack gains a small amount of Lifesteal. If used under Stellar Blessing, the attack ignores defense. If used under Umbral Veil, the attack gains bonus Crit Rate.

Solar Prominence: The user channels the power of the Sun, unleashing it in a burst around them to deal damage to all nearby enemies. The damage is increased based on the user's Int, and is treated as Burning damage. If used under Lunar Protection, the attack gains a small amount of Lifesteal. If used under Stellar Blessing, the attack ignores defense. If used under Umbral Veil, the attack gains bonus Crit Rate.

Lunar Eclipse: The user channels the power of the Moon, infusing it into a single strike that then hides them from their enemies. Deals physical damage that is increased based on the user's Vit, heals the user for a percentage of the damage dealt, and puts the user in the Cloaking status for five seconds. If used under Solar Heat, the damage is treated as Burning damage. If used under Stellar Blessing, the attack ignores defense. If used under Umbral Veil, the attack gains bonus Crit Rate.

Lunar Advent: The user channels the power of the Moon, unleashing it to deal devastating damage to a single foe. Deals physical damage that is increased based on the user's Vit and heals the user for a percentage of the damage dealt. If used while in the Cloaking status, the damage is further increased. If used under Solar Heat, the damage is treated as Burning damage. If used under Stellar Blessing, the attack ignores defense. If used under Umbral Veil, the attack gains bonus Crit Rate.

Stellar Flicker: The user channels the power of the Stars, striking a single target for moderate physical damage and briefly marking them. The damage of this skill is increased by the user's Dex. Marked targets have their defense reduced. This defense reduction stacks additively with item based Defense Pierce. If used under Solar Heat, the damage is treated as Burning damage. If used under Lunar Protection, the attack gains a small amount of Lifesteal. If used under Umbral Veil, the attack gains bonus Crit Rate.

Stellar Tempest: The user channels the power of the Stars, calling five of them to rain down and strike enemies in the area around them. Enemies in the area of the falling stars take a moderate amount of physical damage, which is increased by the user's Dex, and are marked for a brief time. Marked targets have their defense reduced. This defense reduction stacks additively with item based Defense Pierce. If used under Solar Heat, the damage is treated as Burning damage. If used under Lunar Protection, the attack gains a small amount of Lifesteal. If used under Umbral Veil, the attack gains bonus Crit Rate.

Umbral Lash: The user channels the power of Shadow, unleashing a wave of darkness that strikes all enemies in a line between the user and a distant target. The damage dealt is increased by the user's Agi, and has a bonus Crit rate. If used under Solar Heat, the damage is treated as Burning damage. If used under Lunar Protection, the attack gains a small amount of Lifesteal. If used under Stellar Blessing, the attack ignores defense.

Umbral Howl: The user channels the power of the Shadow, summoning a massive burst of cosmic darkness to annihilate their foes. Deals massive damage in an area around the user, which is increased by the user's Agi, has bonus Crit Rate, and has a high chance to inflict the Blind status on enemies struck. If used under Solar Heat, the damage is treated as Burning damage. If used under Lunar Protection, the attack gains a small amount of Lifesteal. If used under Stellar Blessing, the attack ignores defense.

Cosmic Revelation: The user channels the power of the unified cosmos, enhancing their abilities for a short duration. For ten seconds, or until a certain number of skills have been cast, the user gains an increase to all stats and has the SP Cost of Star Emperor skills they use reduced to 0. While Cosmic Revelation is active, the internal cooldown for Cosmic Union autocasts is ignored.
Cosmic Nova: The user channels the power of the unified cosmos, unleashing them in the area around themselves to strike all enemies in range. The damage dealt is increased by the user's Luk.
If used under Solar Heat, the damage is treated as Burning damage.
If used under Lunar Protection, the attack gains a small amount of Lifesteal.
If used under Stellar Blessing, the attack ignores defense.
If used under Umbral Veil, the attack gains bonus Crit Rate.
