Sky Emperor.x: Sky Emperor is the alternative advancement option for Star Gladiators. While the Star Emperor expands their abilities by drawing closer to the cosmos, the Sky Emperor focuses their efforts on how those same celestial bodies interact with the earth, tracking their movements through the sky to draw their power out.

Rather than expanding on the previous cosmic skills that the Star Gladiator made use of, the Sky Emperor gains a new parallel set of skills to be utilized alongside them. These fall into three categories: Daylight Skills, focused on single target damage that utilizes Burning, Int, and Dex; Nightfall Skills, that focus on dealing AoE damage, spreading status effects and using Vit and Agi; and the Celestial Skills, a mixed branch that both stands on its own and provides ultimate skills for the Daylight and Nightfall branches.

While the Sky Emperor uses their skills, they will gain a new Celestial Alignment to go alongside their Cosmic Alignment. Rather than a static buff that affects all skills, this Celestial Alignment is a constantly shifting state, tracking the motion of the sun and moon through the sky, and altering the skills the Sky Emperor uses as it does. Learning to manipulate and accommodate this ever shifting alignment is key to maximizing the Sky Emperor’s potential.

One last skill caps off the Sky Emperor’s tree, paying homage to the Umbral line of skills that seems otherwise all but forgotten in this advancement. Encroaching Darkness immediately purges the user’s Celestial Alignment, then grants a powerful defensive buff for a short duration, giving them an opportunity to escape even the most dangerous situations.
Skills:

Sunrise: Draws on the light of the sun, striking enemies with an attempt to inflict various statuses. Naturally attempts to inflict the Burning Status. If the user is in the Rising Sun state, instead inflicts the Internal Bleeding Status. If in High Noon, instead the damage is treated as half burning, half bleeding damage. Will fail if the user is in Nightfall.

Brilliant Noon: Calls down the wrath of the noonday sun to scorch their target. If the user has no Celestial State, the target’s Burning is enhanced. If they are in the Rising Sun state, the target’s Internal Bleeding is enhanced. In High Noon, the skill is treated as half burning, half bleeding damage. Will fail if the user is in Nightfall.

Duskfall: The user calls on the power of the setting sun to finish off their opponent. Deals significant damage to the target and refreshes the Cooldowns of Sunrise and Brilliant Noon, then shifts the user’s Celestial State forward by one into Daylight. If the user has no state or is in Sunrise, it deals additional damage to Burning and Bleeding enemies respectively. During High Noon, it deals additional damage to both, and the Cooldown refreshing effect is disabled. Will fail during Nightfall.

Moonrise: Draws on the power of the moon to strike all nearby enemies. With no Celestial State, attempts to inflict the Blind status. If in Rising Moon, attempts to inflict Vulnerable. In Midnight, deals additional damage based on the user’s Blind and Vulnerable Potency. Will fail if the user is in Daylight.

Dead of Night: The user delivers a whirling kick, scattering enemies with the power of the moon. If the user has no Celestial State, refreshes the Blind duration of all enemies struck. If the user is in Rising Moon, it refreshes the Vulnerable duration instead. In Midnight, this skill deals bonus damage based on the user’s Blind Potency and Vulnerable Potency. Will fail if the user is in Daylight.

Breaking Dawn: Releases a burst of celestial energy to strike all enemies in the area and refresh the Cooldowns of Moonrise and Dead of Night. If the user has no Celestial State or is in Moonrise, deals additional damage to Blind or Vulnerable enemies respectively. If in Midnight, deals additional damage to both, and the Cooldown refreshing effect is disabled. Will fail if used in Daylight.

Celestial Miracle: The user enters a state of perfect harmony with the celestial lights, charging their attacks with their strength. Blocks the user from shifting their Celestial State, and causes all Sky Emperor skills to deal reduced damage based on the user's remaining SP.
If Cosmic Union is active, its autocasts are replaced with Sky Emperor skills. The skills will autocast in the following order:
Sunrise > Brilliant Noon > Duskfall > Moonrise > Dead of Night > Breaking Dawn
The skills will be cast at the same level learned by the user.
Once Breaking Dawn has been cast, Cosmic Union returns to its original behavior.
Celestial Judgement: The user calls down the wrath of the sky, raining destruction in a wide area around them. Enemies struck take massive damage.
If used during Daylight, the state ends and all Daylight skills have their Cooldowns refreshed.
If used during the Celestial Miracle state, the skill's SP Cost is removed and the autocast chain returns to Sunrise.
Celestial Blast: The user infuses the energy of the sky into their hands and feet, inflicting a single devastating blow on the targeted enemy.
If used during Nightfall, the state ends and all Nightfall skills have their Cooldowns refreshed.
If used during the Celestial Miracle state, the skill's SP Cost is removed and the autocast chain returns to Sunrise.

Encroaching Darkness: The user calls on the cosmic darkness of the universe, drowning out the light of the celestial bodies. Immediately ends the user's current Celestial State, then causes all attacks against the user to miss for a short time.

Soul Linker.x: While the Star Gladiator begins the process of distancing themselves from their roots in Taekwon Do, the Soul Linker wastes no time, abandoning them immediately and without hesitation.

Much like in vanilla, Soul Linkers are a class that operates by calling the souls of the dead back to the world of the living to push characters beyond the limits of their class. Unlike vanilla however, where the Soul Linker could provide these powerful buffs to anyone but themselves, Soul Linkers here can only provide those buffs to themselves.

The Soul Linker skill tree is divided into two halves based on which Soul Link they choose to associate themselves with. Vicious Possession grants the Soul Linker powerful physical buffs, turning ordinarily magical stats like Int and Dex into powerful Crit and Crit Damage buffs, while unlocking skills to do physical damage, block physical attacks, and restore SP to allies (including themselves). In contrast, Arcane Possession does the opposite, converting Strength and Vitality into Cast Time Reduction and SP Regeneration, unlocking powerful magical attacks, a strong healing skill usable on both allies and themselves, and a skill to reflect any magic damage received.

Fledgling Soul Linkers may find themselves a bit perplexed at their skill tree, however. Though they gain access to rather powerful abilities very quickly, all Soul Linker skills come with heavy cooldowns that make leveling alone quite challenging. The gap left by these long cooldowns are filled by the unique weapon available to Soul Linkers: Souls.

Souls are weapons that give varied amounts of Attack and Magic Attack, but most importantly, they provide access to a number of skills from other classes. For example, a Soul Linker might equip a Knight Soul to gain access to the Knight skills Rend, Pierce, and Brandish Spear. Or they might prefer going a magical route, equipping a Wizard Soul to gain access to Storm Gust, Force Pulse, and Rapid Incantation. Keen eyed adventurers might even come across more unique Souls, granting access to skills only available to monsters — and sometimes not available at all, except for by those Souls.

The huge array of available skills and the ability to equip up to three of them at a time grants Soul Linkers an unprecedented level of flexibility, giving them the tools to take on any situation another class might handle.
Soul Linkers gain access to the following skills.
Soul Harmony: Mastery. Increases the user’s Hit Rate and reduces the user’s Variable Cast Time while wielding a Soul class weapon. Souls typically give additional Skills as a Mastery bonus.

Vicious Possession: The user calls on the soul of a bloodthirsty warrior to inhabit their body, borrowing a portion of their strength. Converts a portion of the user’s Magic Attack into Physical Attack, and increases the user’s Crit Rate and Crit Damage based on their Int and Dex. Only one Possession can be active at a time.

Spectral Thrust: The user unleashes a burst of spectral energy, striking and knocking away a targeted enemy. Deals Ghost property Physical damage with a chance to leave the target Vulnerable. Each level of Axe Kick learned increases the chance to inflict Vulnerability.

Spectral Claw: The user summons a wraith from beyond the grave to lash out at the target, dealing Ghost property Physical damage to them and all enemies in the area, leaving an open wound that makes them more susceptible to Physical damage for a short duration. This skill deals additional damage to enemies that are Vulnerable. The Physical Vulnerability effect is increased for each level of Tornado Kick learned by the user.

Spectral Veil: The user slips out of the realm of the living, making themselves immune to Physical damage for a single hit. If this skill ends because it blocked an attack, the user restores a portion of their Max HP based on the currently learned level of Counter Kick.

Spectral Toll: The user pulls their own soul closer to the realm of the dead, turning themselves into a conduit that allows power from beyond the grave to flow back into the world of the living. Rapidly drains the user’s HP for a short duration, restoring SP for a targeted ally at the same time. The amount of HP consumed is reduced by the level of Roundhouse Kick learned by the user.

Arcane Possession: The user invites the soul of a powerful mystic to inhabit their body, drawing on a portion of their knowledge. Converts a portion of the user’s Physical Attack into Magic Attack, and reduces the users Variable Cast Time and increases their SP Regen based on their Str and Vit. Only one Possession can be active at a time.
Soul Pressure: Calls on a vengeful soul to suppress an enemy, dealing Ghost property Magic damage and attempting to Slow them. Slow chance is influenced by the user’s learned level of Axe Kick.

Soul Convergence: Summons a horde of vengeful souls to a targeted enemy, dealing Ghost property magic damage to them and to all enemies in the area around them. This skill deals additional damage to enemies that are Slowed. Enemies struck by the attack are left vulnerable to Magic damage for a short duration. The strength of the Magic Damage Vulnerability is influenced by the learned level of Tornado Kick.

Soul Mirror: Summons a protective spirit to shield the user from harmful magic, turning it back on its source. If this skill ends because it reflected an attack, the user regenerates a percentage of their Max SP based on the learned level of Counter Kick.

Soul Reshaping: The user calls on a benign spirit that feeds off their SP to rapidly restore health to an ally over time. The amount of SP consumed by this skill is reduced by the learned level of Roundhouse Kick.

Soul Reaper.x: Soul Reaper is the primary advancement option for Soul Linkers. Leveraging their mastery over spirits of the dead, the Soul Reaper turns their studies to mastering the wicked and evil spirits that torment the world, turning their malice into a powerful weapon.

Calling on these evil spirits does not come without cost, however. Once their power has been exercised, they persist around the caster, constantly draining them of life. Thus enters the second half of the Soul Reaper’s arsenal, skills used to expel these evil spirits, using that expulsion to gain even further advantage on the battlefield.

Though Soul Reapers maintain the infinite flexibility of the Soul Linkers they descended from, this balance of generating and consuming evil spirits often becomes the bulk of their kit, many Soul Reapers choosing to use their Soul slots for supportive and utility abilities rather than direct combat skills. Even so, with some clever planning, a Soul Reaper can still make just as effective use of those powerful Souls as their Soul Ascetic cousins.

With access to a powerful suite of physical, magical, and support skills, together with the limitless possibilities of their Soul options, it is all but impossible for an enemy to predict what any given Soul Reaper might bring to the battlefield, and similarly difficult for any Soul Reaper to find a situation that their endlessly adaptable set of abilities struggles to overcome.

Evil Spirit Mastery: Many Soul Reaper skills call on the power of evil spirits to exert power on their enemies. These evil spirits linger in the air around the Soul Reaper after the skill has been cast, causing all future abilities used by the Soul Reaper, even non-Soul Reaper skills, to consume HP in addition to their ordinary costs. These Souls last for ten minutes or until otherwise consumed.
Spiteful Spirit: The user conjures an evil spirit to attack the targeted enemy, dealing Ghost Property magic damage and attempting to inflict the Breach status. Casting this skill generates one Soul.

Tormented Spirit: The user calls a tormented spirit to haunt the targeted enemy, dealing Ghost Property Magic Damage to them and all enemies in an area around them. All enemies affected have a chance of receiving the Slow Status. Generates 3 Souls on use.

Doomed Spirit: The user conjures a doomed spirit to wreak havoc across the battlefield, dealing Ghost Property Magic Damage in a huge area around them. This skill deals increased damage to Slow and Breached enemies. Generates 6 Souls on use.
Spiteful Shade: The user conjures a spiteful shade to attack the targeted enemy, dealing Ghost Property Physical Damage and attempting to inflict the Vulnerable Status. Generates 1 Soul on use.

Tormented Shade: The user summons a tormented shade to assault the targeted enemy, dealing Ghost Property Physical Damage and attempting to inflict the Blind Status to them and all enemies in the area. Generates 3 Souls on use.

Doomed Shade: The user conjures a doomed shade to wreak havoc across the battlefield, dealing Ghost Property Physical Damage to all enemies nearby. This skill deals increased damage to enemies suffering from Vulnerable and Blind. Generates 6 Souls on use.

Soul Eater: The user draws the power of the evil spirits around them into themselves, using their malice to empower their own attacks. Consumes all of the user's active Souls to gain a short bonus to Attack and Magic Attack. The strength of the bonus is based on the number of Souls consumed.

Soul Sacrifice: The user draws on the power of the evil spirits around them, transforming them into healing power to sustain themselves in combat. Consumes all of the user's active Souls to recover HP for the targeted ally. The strength of the heal increases with the number of souls consumed. The base healing amount scales with the user's Intelligence.

Soul Division: The user draws on the power of the evil spirits around them, dividing their power among all nearby allies to protect them from harm. Consumes all of the user's active Souls to grant a Barrier to all party members. The strength of the barrier increases with the number of Souls consumed, and scales with the user's Strength.

Soul Binding: The user draws on the power of the evil spirits around them, feeding off of their power to empower their own abilities. Consumes all of the user's active Souls to reduce the active Cooldowns of all of the user's skills. Each Soul consumed reduces the Cooldowns further. Skills and equipment that reduce active Cooldowns never affect this skill.

Soul Ascetic.x: Soul Ascetic is the alternative advancement option for Soul Linkers. While Soul Reapers turn their efforts toward studying and mastering the evil spirits that plague the world, Soul Ascetics instead focus on communing with the spirits of the natural world, turning their otherwise aimless—but still very potent—power toward good.

A Soul Ascetic’s bond to these spirits of nature is not a given, though. It is a tenuous balance that they must struggle to maintain at all times. This manifests itself through the Soul Ascetic’s AP. This value always rests between 0 and 200, but as it approaches the exact center of that range, the Soul Ascetic’s abilities become much more powerful. Or from another perspective, one most Soul Ascetics will tend to adopt themselves, the closer their AP comes to the extremes of its spectrum, the weaker their performance.

There are two primary ways the Soul Ascetic manages this balance. The first is through the use of Rituals, two stance-like abilities that immediately give or take a large amount of AP, on top of providing a short duration buff.

In addition to these Rituals, all Soul Ascetic abilities modify the user’s current AP value, either granting or draining AP. Balancing these gains and losses with the Rituals, and knowing when to throw out more Soul Ascetic skills and when to hold them in reserve and rely on your Soul skills forms the core of the Soul Ascetic playstyle.
Skills:

Ritual of Invocation: The user performs a ritual to invoke the powers of the spirits of the natural world, preparing to wield their power to create powerful phenomena in the physical world. The user immediately gains a large boost of AP, then for a short duration they gain increased Crit Rate and reduced Fixed Cast Times.

Ritual of Binding: The user performs a ritual to subdue the spirits of the natural world, blunting their impact on the physical world. The user immediately loses a large amount of AP, then for a short duration they gain a bonus to Attack Speed and a reduction in all SP Costs.

Talisman of Protection: The user calls on the spirits of nature to protect the targeted ally, bestowing on them a talisman of protection. Grants the targeted ally a Barrier for a short duration. The closer the user's AP is to 100, the stronger the Barrier becomes. If the user’s AP is within 50 points of 100, it also protects from Bleeding, Burning, and Poison. If the user’s AP is within 10 points of 100, it also heals them for the same amount as the Barrier.

Talisman of War: The user calls on the spirits of nature to bolster the strength of the targeted ally's attacks, bestowing on them a talisman of war. Grants the targeted ally a bonus to Vulnerable and Breach Potency for a short duration. The closer the user's AP is to 100, the stronger the bonus becomes. If the user’s AP is within 50 points of 100, it also grants protection from Blind, Slow, and Slowcast. If the user’s AP is within 10 points of 100, it also increases the target’s Bleeding, Burning, and Poison damage.

Curse of Absorption: The user calls on the spirits of the natural world to attack the targeted enemy, draining them of strength and weakening their defenses. Deals Ghost Property Magic Damage to a single target and attempts to inflict the Breach status. The Damage of this skill is increased the closer the user's AP is to 100. If the user’s AP is within 50 points of 100, it deals additional damage to Breached enemies. If within 10 points of 100, the user is healed for a portion of the damage dealt.
Generates a small amount of AP when used.

Curse of Doom: The use calls on the spirits of the natural world to attack the targeted enemy, slowly sapping the life of them over time. Deals Ghost Property damage every second to the targeted enemy for a short duration. The damage inflicted by this skill is increased the closer the user's AP is to 100. If the user’s AP is within 50 points of 100, also inflicts the Slow status. If within 10 points of 100, the duration of both statuses is doubled.
Generates a small amount of AP when used.

Curse of Sealing: The user calls on the spirits of the natural world to bind and suppress all enemies in the area around them, dealing massive Ghost Property Magical Damage. The damage of this skill is increased the closer the user's AP is to 100.
If the user’s AP is within 50 points of 100, it also inflicts the Slow status.
If the user’s AP is within 10 points of 100, it also inflicts the Sleep status.
Drains a large amount of AP when used.

Curse of Destruction: The user calls on the spirits of the natural world to attack the target's physical body, dealing Ghost Property Physical Damage and attempting to inflict the Vulnerable Status. The damage of this skill is increased the closer the user's AP is to 100.
If the user’s AP is within 50 points of 100, it deals additional damage to Vulnerable enemies.
If the user’s AP is within 10 points of 100, it also grants the user a Barrier equal to a portion of the damage dealt.
Drains a small amount of AP when used.

Curse of Brilliance: The user calls on the spirits of the natural world to strike the targeted enemy with blindness, dealing Ghost Property Physical Damage and attempting to inflict the Blind Status. The damage of this skill is increased the closer the user's AP is to 100.
If the user’s AP is within 50 points of 100, it also deals increased damage to Blind enemies.
If the user’s AP is within 10 points of 100, it also grants the user a short Movement Speed bonus.
Drains a small amount of AP when used.

Curse of Annihilation: The user opens a gate to the spiritual world, unleashing a torrent of spirits to obliterate all enemies around them. Deals massive Ghost Property Physical Damage to all enemies in the area around the user. The damage is increased the closer the user's AP is to 100.
If the user’s AP is within 50 points of 100, it also inflicts the Blind status.
If the user’s AP is within 10 points of 100, it also inflicts the Stun status.
Generates a large amount of AP when used.

Ninja.x: The Ninja seeks to fill the role of the proverbial “jack of all trades.” Even at the first job level they possess a wide variety of skills, from melee and gap closers, to ranged and spacing, to single target and AoE magic.

While capable of wielding any dagger, Ninjas have access to a set of specialized daggers that improve both their physical and magical attack simultaneously. At the same time they gain access to a unique suite of offhand weapons: Shurikens, Kunai, and Huuma Shurikens. These grant skills to the equipping Ninja allowing them to fight from afar.

As will quickly become apparent to any fledgling Ninja, the key to maximizing a Ninja’s potential is to tap into that versatility. Having access to Melee, Ranged, and Magical skills may seem conflicting at first, but with each set of skills scaling with the primary attribute of the others and providing buffs to them, experienced Ninjas will know just how to weave between the three fighting styles to optimize their performance, ensuring there is no gap in their assault.
Unlike the other First Jobs, Ninjas do not job change at level 50. Instead, they continue honing their skills until Base Level 99, at which point they transition into their final job.
Ninjas gain access to the following skills:
Dagger Mastery: Mastery. Increases the damage, Hit Rate, and Double Attack rate of Daggers.

Flashing Steel: Strikes the target with a blow faster than the eye can follow. Deals moderate physical damage that scales heavily with Dex and Int. This skill ignores Flee, and grants the First Art status on hit. If Second or Third Art are active, it gains an additional 30 Crit. If both, it is guaranteed to Crit, Second Art ends, and Echoing Shadow has its cooldown refreshed.

Soaring Steel: Dashes through a distant target, dealing three successive blows that inflict physical damage that scales heavily with Dex and Int. Grants the First Art status on hit. If Second or Third Art are active, it gains an additional 30 Crit. If both, it is guaranteed to Crit, Third Art ends, and Advanced Ninja Arts have their cooldowns refreshed.

Throwing Mastery: Training in the art of throwing weapons, such as shurikens, kunai, and Huuma shurikens. Each point in this mastery increases the level of the Throwing skill unlocked by equipped throwing weapons.

Departing Shadow: Throws the equipped offhand weapon at a distant target, while the user immediately backslides to safety, granting the Second Art status.. Damage is based on the user’s Dex, and scales heavily with Str and Int. If First or Third Art are active, this skill has a 50% chance to Slow the target. If both, the chance is 100%, First Art ends, and Soaring Steel has its cooldown refreshed.

Echoing Shadow: Copies the Throwing skill of the currently equipped Throwing Weapon. The copied skill is cast at this skill’s level, rather than the known level of the skill being copied, and ignores the original skill’s cooldown.

Throw Shuriken: Unlocked only by equipping a Shuriken in the offhand. Deals quick ranged damage to a target based on the user’s Dex, scaling with Str and Int and granting the Second Art status. If First or Third Art are active, this skill repeats two more times after being cast. If both, it repeats two more times, for a total of five hits, Third Art ends, and Basic Ninja Arts have their cooldowns refreshed. This skill shares a cooldown with Throw Kunai and Throw Huuma Shuriken.

Throw Kunai: Unlocked only by equipping a Kunai in the offhand. Deals substantial ranged damage to a target based on the user’s Dex, scaling heavily with Str and Int and granting the Second Art status. If First or Third Art are active, it has a 50% chance to inflict the status associated with the equipped Kunai. If both, the chance is 100%, Third Art ends, and Basic Ninja Arts have their cooldowns refreshed. This skill shares a cooldown with Throw Shuriken and Throw Huuma Shuriken.

Throw Huuma Shuriken: Unlocked only by equipping a Huuma Shuriken in the offhand. Deals heavy ranged damage to a target based on the user’s Dex, scaling heavily with Str and Int, and granting the Second Art status. If First or Third Art are active, it splashes in a 3x3 area. If both, it splashes in a 7x7 area, Third Art ends, and Basic Ninja Arts have their cooldowns refreshed. This skill shares a cooldown with Throw Shuriken and Throw Kunai.
Magical Attunement: Training in attuning oneself to the magical forces of the world. Reduces the SP cost of all skills, increases SP regen, and improves the effectiveness of SP potions.

Flaming Petals/Freezing Spear/Wind Blade/Stone Lance: The four Basic Ninja Arts. Deals a modest amount of magical damage of the appropriate element to a target. The amount of damage dealt is based on the learned level of Magical Attunement, rather than the level of the skill itself, and scales heavily with Str and Dex. Grants the Third Art status on hit. If First or Second Art are active, these skills have their Fixed Cast Time removed. If both, the entire cast time is removed, First Art ends, and Flashing Steel has its cooldown refreshed. All four Basic Ninja Arts share a cooldown.
Advanced Ninjutsu Mastery: Increases the effectiveness of Advanced Ninja Arts.

Blazing Dragon/Winter’s Grasp/Thunderous Surge/Seismic Collapse: Advanced Ninja Arts. Deals significant magical damage of the appropriate element to enemies around the user. The amount of damage dealt is based on the level of Advanced Ninjutsu Mastery, rather than the learned level of the skill itself, and scales heavily with Str and Dex. Kagemusha.x: Kagemusha, once known as Kagerou and Oboro, is the primary advancement option for Ninjas. After spending a hundred levels perfecting their use of physical, ranged, and magical combat styles, the Kagemusha continue along the same path, adding explosive power to each style of ninjutsu.

Once again, the skill tree of the Kagemusha is split into three branches, Melee, Ranged, and Magic. Each of these branches builds on the foundation of a utility skill — Mikiri, Shifting Shadow, and Serenity respectively — before gaining access to more of the familiar combat tricks that Ninjas are already familiar with.

However, these new skills are distinctively different from the first job skills available to Ninjas. While they take advantage of the same three Arts buffs that original Ninja skills rely on, they never generate them. This leaves the Kagemusha with two possible applications of these new skills: they can either use them as seems like the most obvious intention, as finishers to add a powerful capstone to their previously endlessly looping Ninja combos, or they can take advantage of a new trait that each of the new skills possesses.

While Ninja-level skills only ever benefited from Arts coming from outside their own tree, that is not the case for the Kagemusha. Each of the new skills also gains a benefit if the user is only under that skill’s own Art. For example, the new skill Fulminant Steel gains a bonus as usual for the user being under Second Art or Third Art, coming from Ranged and Magical skills respectively, and gains a stronger bonus if under both, but if they are under only First Art, unique to Melee skills, it gains a different, unique bonus. This allows the Kagemusha to focus their training on perfecting a single branch of their skill tree, rather than diversifying so much as was required in their previous job.

Maboroshi.x: Maboroshi, previously known as Shinkiro and Shiranui, is the alternative advancement option for Ninjas. While the Kagemusha focuses on perfecting the use of their original Ninja techniques, learning advanced ways to make use of their original three Ninja Arts, the Maboroshi decides that original Ninja skills weren’t complicated enough, and decides to kick things up a notch.

While Maboroshi skills can be divided into three branches to match those of the original Ninja skills, Melee, Ranged, and Magic, they add another layer of complexity on top of these three basic arts. All of the Maboroshi kit is built around the “Mirage” mechanic, an ability they gain with their new skills to leave illusionary clones of themselves behind when they use certain skills.

Unlike their namesake, these Mirages can in fact be quite deadly. Every Maboroshi skill will trigger these Mirages to attack, the skill they use being determined by which Ninja Arts the user currently has active. With up to three of these Mirages capable of taking to the field at once, Shinkiro and Shiranui will find themselves faced with a mind boggling level of flexibility in how they approach any encounter.

This unprecedented level of flexibility fuses with an exceptional array of mobility skills, both from their original Ninja skills and the new Mirage-generating skills they gain access to after job change. A master Maboroshi will be like a flickering mirage on the battlefield themselves, striking everywhere yet being nowhere, leaving their enemies bewildered and helpless.

Gunslinger.x: The Gunslinger occupies a space very similar to that of the mage: a ranged character that specializes in dishing out multiple status effects and taking advantage of them to deal exceptional amounts of damage. As one might guess from the name, however, the manner they choose to do this is a bit different.
Gunslingers have access to three primary weapons types: Revolvers, Rifles, and Shotguns.

Revolvers deal minor damage and inflict the Slow status on enemies, making them the most defensive of the weapon options. However, their damage increases massively against enemies suffering from Vulnerable and Bleeding.

Rifles specialize in inflicting Vulnerable on enemies to reduce their defense, deal exceptionally high damage, and gain large bonuses to their Crit Rate against targets suffering from Slow and Bleeding.

Shotguns land somewhere in the middle, dealing significant damage, but over a small area. In addition, they regularly inflict the Bleeding status, amplifying their damage significantly over time. Shotgun skills also have a chance to Stun enemies suffering from Slow, and gain increased Crit Rate against enemies suffering from Vulnerable.
The end result is a character that rapidly shifts between weapon types, applying a wide variety of statuses and then capitalizing on those statuses to put out exceptional levels of damage.
Similar to Ninjas, Gunslingers do not job change at level 50 like most classes. Gunslingers advance to their final job at Base Level 99.

Snipe: Rifle Finisher. The user takes careful aim and fires a shot at the target’s most vital point. The damage of this skill is increased if the target is Slowed or Bleeding.

Scatter Shot: Shotgun Skill. Sprays fire from the shotgun over a small area, hitting multiple enemies with a high chance to inflict the Internal Bleeding status. Slowed and Vulnerable enemies have a chance of being Stunned.

Rebel.x: Rebel is the primary advancement option for Gunslingers. As with the Gunslinger before them, the Rebel’s kit focuses around rapidly switching between Revolvers, Rifles, and Shotguns to deliver a wide range of status effects, using them to maximize their damage potential. There are two primary ways that the Rebel advances this play style.

First, the Rebel gains two new skills for each of their core weapon types. These skills follow a familiar pattern to their original Gunslinger Skills: Revolver skills inflict Slow and benefit from striking Bleeding and Vulnerable targets, and so on. However, unlike their old Gunslinger skills, they gain additional effects if they strike enemies suffering from their own Status Effect. For example, the Revolver skill Disengage inflicts Slow, and deals additional damage to Vulnerable enemies, but if the enemy struck is already Slowed, it instead inflicts Internal Bleeding. This gives the Rebel the ability to pare down their skill rotations, focusing on one or two weapon types rather than relying on all three, but still rewarding them for going all out on the weapon swapping.
Secondly, the Rebel gains access to a new gun type to add to their arsenal: the Gatling Gun.

These unique weapons take a dedicated slot in the character’s equipment window, where one might expect Shadow Weapons to be in vanilla RO, and so do not need to be included in the weapon-swapping frenzy that Gunslingers have already spent a hundred levels perfecting. Instead, they remain constantly equipped, giving their bonuses no matter what weapon the user has equipped, and only coming out to shine when their specific skills are called on.

On top of this, Gatling Guns operate with a new kind of Mastery unique to them and their Night Watch cousins. While most weapon types require a specific passive skill be learned to represent mastery over its use, Gatling Gun Masteries check how many skill points have been invested in any Gatling Gun related skill. This means that while Rebels can make efficient use of Gatling Guns by splashing their skills in amongst other weapon types, those who choose to invest heavily into their new weapon type will be rewarded with a much greater output than any of their other weapon types can offer, each skill point invested reducing the cooldowns of all Gatling Gun skills the user has access to.

Night Watch.x: Night Watch is the alternative advancement option for Gunslingers. Similar to the Rebel, the Night Watch focuses on expanding the original options of the Gunslinger. While perfectly at home with the triple-wielding style of old, they also gain the ability to specialize in a single weapon type of their choosing.

Revolver, Rifle, and Shotgun Specialization are skills that function effectively the same. While active, the weapon skills of their specified type gain benefits to account for their lack of ability to swap weapons, inflicting varied statuses even with a single gun type.

In addition to these enhancements to the original Gunslinger arsenal, the Night Watch gain a new weapon type unique to them: the Grenade Launcher. Like the Rebel’s Gatling Gun, the Grenade Launcher occupies a special equipment slot separate from the user’s weapon, allowing them to offer their bonuses consistently through any number of weapon swaps, and no matter which Weapon Specialization the user chooses to rely on.

Grenade Launcher skills have a number of unique characteristics. Chief among them is that they all have exceptionally low Cooldowns, their use being primarily limited by their ammo. The specialized grenades used for firing these destructive weapons does not come from shops, however, but from making use of the Night Watch’s other weapon skills. Thus, even those members of the Night Watch who wish to focus entirely on using their Grenade Launchers will need to keep firing off a steady stream of other weapon skills to keep their Launchers fed. But once they get that rhythm down, they will be able to unleash exceptional levels of destruction across the battlefield.

Grenade Launchers also share the unique Mastery system of Gatling Guns in that their Weapon Mastery tracks every skill point invested in any Gatling Gun skill. Those members of the Night Watch who choose to focus their efforts on their new Grenade Launchers will find themselves dealing incredible amounts of damage with almost no down time.
